Russell Brand is alleged to have told friends he wanted to “bed 5,000 women in his lifetime” by the prosecution as his trial opened this morning.

The comedian, 51, denies three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one allegation of indecent assault relating to six women in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

The trial started at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, with the prosecution opening its case to a jury of eight men and four women.

The former Big Brother’s Big Mouth presenter is alleged to have been a “ruthless, calculating and manipulative” sexual predator and “bragged” he was “a ladies’ man, a womaniser and an expert pick-up artist”, the court heard.

The jurors were selected on Tuesday, when Mr Justice Bennathan warned them to ignore past reporting on the celebrity.

Brand, who lives in Florida, became one of Britain’s best-known comedians in the 2000s and won presenting roles including the 2007 Brit Awards, Comic Relief and the MTV Music Video Awards, and hosted his own show on BBC Radio 2.

The trial is scheduled to last six to eight weeks.

News.title: Heathrow boss calls for Burnham to get behind third runway scheme
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The boss of Heathrow has hit out at the uncertainty over the airport’s planned expansion after Andy Burnham declined to back the scheme.

Heathrow chief executive Thomas Woldbye said he hoped the Prime Minister will throw his weight behind the scheme, adding “it would be good to know where Government is on this”.

He warned that investment could be lost overseas without a firm commitment to the construction of a new runway.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham has refused to confirm his support for a third runway (PA) ( PA Wire )

Before Mr Burnham entered No 10, predecessor Sir Keir Starmer and then-chancellor Rachel Reeves had backed the construction of a third runway at the UK’s busiest airport.

But Mr Burnham has refused to confirm his support, saying it is subject to a consultation and then the planning process.

Mr Woldbye told BBC Radio 4’s Today: “The most important thing here is what this project delivers for the UK, and I think seeing that, I hope the Prime Minister will come along.”

He said it will provide a “huge economic boost” and offer opportunities such as apprenticeships, which correspond with “the priorities that this Government has set out”.

Mr Woldbye said the process is “ongoing”, adding: “When we get to the end of those processes, which will be sometimes towards the end of the year, it would be good to know where Government is on this.”

He warned that the planned investment in the £33 billion scheme could go overseas unless there is certainty.

“Our private investors, if they cannot invest in Heathrow which they own, they don’t own any other airports in the UK, and there is no project like a Heathrow expansion, then that money will be invested somewhere else in the world, maybe in a motorway in Spain or a hospital in Italy,” he said.

Heathrow expects to submit a formal planning application “in the next couple of years”, he said.

“Right now the discussion with by far most of the people I speak to is not so much about if we’re going to do this, but more how we’re going to do it and get all the factors right.

“I hope we can stay on that path because I think it is really, really important for the UK to get this project built.”

Giving evidence to MPs later, Mr Woldbye said: “There’s nothing of the size of Heathrow, and there’s nothing of the size of Heathrow that has the country-wide, UK-wide positive consequences.

“Sixty percent of the economic benefit of a runway at Heathrow will be felt throughout the entire country. If you compare that with other projects, I don’t think that is the case.”

He added the expansion was not just about a third runway “it is about renewing the entire airport and getting an airport that this country actually deserves”.

News.title: Badenoch and Farage embroiled in furious row over Falklands and Chagos Islands
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A political row has broken out between Kemi Badenoch and Nigel Farage after the Reform UK leader appeared to suggest he would be willing to “trade” the Diego Garcia military base to secure Donald Trump’s silence on the Falklands.

The dispute erupted after Mr Farage told a US-based podcast that he would have told President Trump that the Chagos Islands could be his and ask him in return to “please stop talking about the Falkland Islands”.

The US President has declined to give full support for British sovereignty of the Falklands, which continues to face threats from Argentinian president Javier Milei.

“I’d have gone in and said, ‘Right, you know what, mate? Chagos, it’s yours. Diego Garcia, in perpetuity, the most strategic American military base in the world, which it is,” Mr Farage told The Benny Show podcast.

“Outside mainland America, Diego is the most important thing America has for nuclear subs, for long-range bombers, for all of it.

open image in gallery The Conservative Party leader accused Mr Farage of “giving away British territory in return for someone keeping quiet”, and branded his remarks “humiliating” ( PA )

“I’d have said, ‘Right, I’m guaranteeing you that. I’m giving up on this surrender. In return, just please stop talking about the Falkland Islands. I know you like Milei, but this really matters to us’. And there’s a trade, you see.”

The Conservative Party leader accused Mr Farage of “giving away British territory in return for someone keeping quiet”, and branded his remarks “humiliating”.

“The Chagos Islands are British. And the Falklands are British, and will remain British, irrespective of what the American president says,” Mrs Badenoch said.

“When Donald Trump is right, we should say so. When he is wrong, we should have the confidence to tell him.

“Nigel Farage has made such a huge fuss about defending the Chagos Islands. He calls this making a deal. Giving away British territory in return for someone keeping quiet is not a deal. It is humiliating. There is no pride in our country in the way he talks about us.

“This is careless, loose talk from a man who wants to be responsible for Britain’s national security.”

Last May, the UK government finalised a treaty transferring sovereignty of the territory to Mauritius.

But multimillion-pound payments to Mauritius have been paused while the UK government re-evaluates its agreement to relinquish sovereignty after President Trump branded the pact "terrible".

The Reform UK leader has insisted that he did not mean he would give up British control of the Chagos Islands to America, but “would offer the use of Diego Garcia to the USA in perpetuity”.

open image in gallery The Reform UK leader has insisted that he did not mean he would give up British control of the Chagos Islands to America, but “would offer the use of Diego Garcia to the USA in perpetuity”. ( Getty )

US government sources told several news outlets overnight that they did not interpret Mr Farage’s remarks as an offer to give up sovereignty of Chagos to America, as Mrs Badenoch had.

“He was obviously referring to the use of the Diego Garcia military base, which is critical to countering threats from China and Iran,” a White House official told The Times.

“Anyone claiming otherwise is peddling fake news and undermining the Anglo-American relationship, including, apparently, Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch.”

A Reform UK spokesman said accused Mrs Badenoch of risking a “diplomatic row with Britain’s allies” over the comments.

“The latest Tory lie, about Nigel Farage’s Chagos island commitment, just show that absolutely nothing has changed inside the Nasty Party, and it never will,” they said.

Meanwhile, the self-declared first minister of the Chagossian government in exile Misley Mandarin said Mrs Badenoch “cannot be trusted by the Chagos people”.

"If they really have interest in the Chagos, why would you have started negotiating about things you already own?” he said. “We know Nigel has the Chagossians at heart. He never boast about all his help to us.

“We agree with him: we would be happy for the US to keep using Diego Garcia with a British Chagossian population in perpetuity, with the rest of the Chagos being under the Crown and we the indigenous people at last having our rights respected forever.”

open image in gallery The future of the Chagos Islands has stoked controversy (CPA Media Pte Ltd/Alamy/PA) ( PA Media )

Argentina has in recent months stepped up its rhetoric on the Falklands, and its president Mr Milei has launched a legal challenge which seeks halt British-led exploration work at the Sea Lion oilfield off the islands’ waters.

Foreign Office minister Uma Kumaran told the Commons on Tuesday the Government would engage with the challenge, and insisted she will do “whatever it takes” to support islanders.

Ms Kumaran also attacked Mr Milei’s “inflammatory remarks” and the “increasingly aggressive public statements” of his ministers.

News.title: Wayfair among firms fined millions for ripping off customers with misleading sales tactics
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Three major companies have been handed fines totalling £6 million for employing misleading sales tactics, according to the competition watchdog.

The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) penalised Wayfair £4.8 million over false time-limited promotions. Appliances Direct received a £1.2 million penalty and was ordered to return roughly £432,000 to buyers, while Gold’s Gym was fined £45,000 and told to refund around £9,000.

Wayfair and Appliances Direct misled shoppers using time-sensitive deals that did not actually expire when advertised. Appliances Direct also automatically added paid-for extras into customer orders.

Gold’s Gym failed to state the full price of memberships, including joining fees, in a clear and timely manner.

In total, customers of Appliances Direct and Gold’s Gym will share approximately £440,000 in refunds. The regulator confirmed both firms will contact affected buyers directly, meaning customers do not need to take any action.

open image in gallery Online retailer Wayfair was one of three companies fined over misleading sales tactics (Alamy/PA) ( Alamy/PA )

Hayley Fletcher, senior director for consumer protection at the CMA, said: “Whether buying a new sofa, a washing machine, or joining a gym, people should see genuine, accurate prices and offers – and decide for themselves whether they want optional extras.

“At a time when many households are carefully managing their budgets, people shouldn’t lose out because of misleading sales tactics.

“The time is up for this kind of behaviour. Businesses must treat their customers fairly and make sure they comply with the law – or risk hefty fines.”

The CMA’s investigation found that products were advertised on Wayfair’s website through “Daily Deals” and 24-hour “Flash Deals”, alongside messages such as “Here Today, Gone Tomorrow” and countdown timers, which implied customers needed to act quickly to get the best deal.

However, the CMA found that many products remained available at the same price or lower after the stated deadline, making the time-limited offer false.

Appliances Direct customers were automatically opted into one or both of services to “Remove & Recycle Your Old Appliance” and “Installation on Delivery service”.

open image in gallery Appliances Direct customers were automatically opted into one or both of services to ‘Remove & Recycle Your Old Appliance’ and ‘Installation on Delivery service’ ( Appliances Direct )

Under consumer law, businesses must get customers’ express agreement before charging them for optional extras, and pre-ticked boxes and other forms of automatic opt-in are not allowed.

Appliances Direct also used pop-up countdown banners on some product pages which claimed that discounts of £10 to £25 were available for a limited time, but the CMA found that the same discount codes appeared repeatedly over many days.

Appliances Direct must pay about £432,000 in refunds to customers affected by opt-ins, at an average amount of £25 per person.

The CMA found that Gold’s Gym failed to include the joining fee in the total price shown to consumers for their annual and direct debit memberships, or the total price was shown in a way that was unclear and unlikely to be seen.

Under consumer law, businesses must show customers the total price, including any mandatory fees, clearly and from the outset.

The CMA has ordered Gold’s Gym to refund a total of £9,220 to the 726 affected customers.

The amount repaid to each customer will depend on the type of membership they bought, but it will be either £50 or £10.

A Wayfair spokeswoman said: “Although we believe the fine is excessive and disproportionate, we take the CMA’s findings seriously and we chose to settle so we can continue to focus on serving our customers.”

News.title: Trump backs down in Zambia mineral and data-sharing row
News.content:
Zambia has signed a five-year health financing agreement with the US government after the US dropped demands for access to sensitive health data and separated the deal from negotiations over the country’s mineral resources.

The agreement follows months of negotiations over a $2.49 billion health aid package, with Zambia pushing back against US demands to share medical data and give preferential access to the country’s rich mineral reserves in exchange for money to provide lifesaving healthcare.

Under the final agreement, Zambia will not be required to hand over individual patient records or biological specimens, which the US had previously argued was important for global disease surveillance.

Data sharing will be restricted to monitoring and evaluating US-funded health programmes.

A separate agreement covering US access to Zambia’s critical minerals has also been decoupled from the health financing deal, it was confirmed last week.

“The government will not be sharing any specimens with the United States because we removed all those aspects that raised concern,” Zambian Health Minister Roma Chilengi said last week as the agreement was signed.

Zambia’s Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe also confirmed that the health and mineral agreements had been separated.

“There was this [memorandum of understanding] on health and another on critical minerals, and we were saying that these need to be decoupled, and this has been done,” he said.

News.title: Progress against HIV stalls in South Africa, research shows
News.content:
South Africa’s progress in tackling the Aids and HIV crisis has stalled in one of its most populous provinces, new research has found.

The number of new cases of the infection in KwaZulu-Natal province, centred around the eastern port of Durban, have stopped falling after years of steep declines.

Data from a long-running study following thousands of people also showed those with detectable levels of virus in their blood had risen slightly despite years of medics prescribing antiretroviral drugs.

Researchers said the peer-reviewed study published in The Lancet HIV medical journal “provides a stark warning on prevailing HIV trends in rural South Africa, where ground is being lost in the fight against the HIV epidemic”.

The researchers, led by scientists at Durban’s Africa Health Research Institute (AHRI) and Stellenbosch University’s South African Centre for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis (SACEMA), used a 20-year study which has tested nearly 60,000 people.

Analysis showed that after steep reductions in HIV incidence from 2013 to 2018, incidence rates for both males and females showed little or no decrease from 2019 onwards.

Incidence rates had continued to fall for young people under 35, but that had been offset by a lack of progress for those in middle age.

News.title: Carrick’s United are in crisis and now spotlight is on Wilcox
News.content:
They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

News.title: Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop
News.content:
The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Guimarães had two chances in the first half. Lille’s Japan international Ayase Ueda had a goal disallowed for offside. Guimarães would have a further penalty appeal before the hour as Arteta began to consider the substitutions.

News.title: Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it
News.content:
England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

News.title: Donkey prices in Gaza skyrocket from $1,000 to $30,000
News.content:
The price of a donkey in Gaza has jumped from about $1,000 before the war to $30,000 today, according to one of the embattled enclave’s most senior vets.

The surge in the value of the pack animals is due to the virtual elimination of motorised private transport in the strip and the emergence of a small group of black marketeers who have become hugely rich trading in intercepted aid.

The donkeys, whose number has been halved in the past three years, are also now in comparatively short supply.

“It’s a little bit crazy and people keep asking me ‘are you sure about that number?’”, Dr Ahmed Thabet, a Gazan veterinary surgeon told the Telegraph.

“They say ‘do you mean $3,000?’ but I tell them ‘no’. The average price of a donkey before the war was between $1,000 and $1,200. Recently it was $20,000 and last week I witnessed one that was sold for $30,000”.

News.title: The secret to the perfect holiday in Somerset
News.content:
Somerset’s landscapes are steeped in legend, from the lush fields of “Avalon” to Cheddar Gorge and the wilds of Exmoor. Its winding, country lanes lead to secrets and natural splendour. The local food scene is flourishing, too, involving everyone from Michelin-starred chefs to foragers on the Mendip Hills and farmers selling cheddar and cider from the barn door.

Glastonbury Festival shines as the centre of the musical universe in June – but the region is becoming known for much more than this. Quiet, agrarian villages are now fashionable places to spend time – I’m often found dawdling over a lazy brunch, browsing designer ceramics and paddleboarding down river. Bruton has an internationally renowned art gallery and the county’s hip, country house hotels – from Soho House-owned Babington House to The Newt – are some of the UK’s most desirable.

What makes Somerset so exciting is that it preserves a bucolic way of life while keeping its finger firmly on the pulse.

News.title: Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle
News.content:
You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sports.title: Barcelona boss Hansi Flick locked inside room at Galatasaray as press conference delayed amid scramble to find key
Sports.content:
Next

HANSI FLICK was sensationally locked out of his own press conference after guiding Barcelona to a win over Galatasaray.

The LaLiga giants came from behind to notch a 4-1 victory and maintain their 100 per cent record in the Champions League.



But there were hilarious scenes after the final whistle as Flick, 61, was initially stopped from facing the media.

Embarrassed staff members at Rams Park could not find the key which would open the door and give the Barcelona chief access to the press conference room.



Phone calls were made in a desperate attempt to get Flick in for his post-match questioning.

And, following a short delay, the German was eventually allowed in to reflect on his side’s thumping win.

Flick said: “We are very happy with the result. We played well in the first half.

“They had one chance and scored, but we managed to come back and that was very important.

“In the Champions League, when we played well, in some situations we didn’t make good decisions in the final third, and that’s something we have to improve.

“Today, in this stadium, with this atmosphere, it wasn’t easy, but I’m very happy.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Barcelona fell behind thanks to Aleksey Batrakov breaking the deadlock for Galatasaray.

But former Manchester City full-back Joao Cancelo got his side back on level terms on the stroke of half-time.

Fermin Lopez then turned the clash on its head by adding his name to the scoresheet.

And Anthony Gordon, fresh from playing a starring role for England during the international break, got in on the act three minutes later.



Karim Adeyemi, who arrived from Borussia Dortmund during the summer, ensured there would be no way back for Galatasaray.

Barcelona still have to face the likes of Paris Saint-Germain, Aston Villa and Man City during the league phase of the Champions League.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham’s stunning girlfriend Ashlyn puts on busty display in low-cut top before tucking into burger and chips
Sports.content:
Next

ASHLYN CASTRO was showered with compliments on her latest stunning Instagram post.

The girlfriend of England superstar Jude Bellingham treated her followers to a slideshow of 12 snaps which she captioned: “Here & there”.



One of them showed her almost bursting out of a low-cut white top while sitting in a luxury car.

She was beaming from ear to ear with a burger a chips in her lap and a drink in her hand.



The post was liked well over 100,000 times and attracted over 1,000 comments within 24 hours.

One of Ashlyn’s one million followers gushed: “Unreal face card.”

Another wrote: “You’re so gorgeous.”

A third pined: “The beauty is unreal.”



And a fourth added: “You are truly beautiful.”

Ashlyn, 28, is a model and influencer from California and was first spotted out in public with Bellingham in early 2025.



She was at the 2026 World Cup cheering him on as England finished third, and has attended multiple Real Madrid matches.

Ashlyn has dated other big stars in the past including Hollywood actor Michael B. Jordan and NBA ace Terance Mann.

Sports.title: Premier League boss ‘with just two games to save job’ hit with huge fine for comments about Man Utd
Sports.content:
Next

FULHAM boss Alvaro Arbeloa has been whacked with a £25,000 fine after claiming his side’s draw with Manchester United had been rigged by the match officials.

Under-pressure Arbeloa hit out following United’s late deflected equaliser at Craven Cottage on September 20.



The game a week after Erling Haaland’s wrongly-awarded Manchester derby winner for City at Old Trafford.

Frustrated Arbeloa told Sky Sports: “Every decision was for them.



“And I knew, I knew after the game against Man City that they don’t let Manchester United lose here. We deserved a little bit more.”

FA beaks opened a probe the following day with Arbeloa, whose job is increasingly at risk with the Cottagers winless and bottom of the Prem pile, charged with misconduct on September 30.



In a statement, an FA spokesman said: “Alvaro Arbeloa has been fined £25,000 and received a warning for comments made after the Premier League fixture between Fulham and Manchester United on Sunday 20 September.

“It was alleged that the Fulham head coach acted in an improper manner by making comments in a post-match interview that imply bias and/or question the integrity of a match official. Alvaro Arbeloa subsequently admitted the charge.”

The only decision by ref Peter Bankes that was studied by the Prem’s Key Match Incident panel saw them BACK his call not to award United a penalty for a handball shout against Fulham’s Calvin Bassey.

At an independent commission hearing, Fulham urged leniency, arguing that Arbeloa had shown “early remorse” by not repeating the TV interview claims in his post-match press conference, had an “imperfect command” of English and had shown a “lack of malice”.



But the three-strong panel, headed by Ruth Kirby KC and including former Lionesses star Faye White, ruled there was “no doubt” about his intentions.

The commission said: “He linked the decisions in the game that had just finished to the decision that had

gone against Manchester United when playing Manchester City.

“Everyone watching the interview would have understood the meaning of what Arbeloa was saying.

“Tthose words suggested, not only that there was bias on the part of the match officials



throughout the game on repeated occasions, but also that there may even have been an element

of pre-meditation by them and/or others to try to make up for an error in a different match.”

The commission added: “In his position as a Premier League manager, Alvaro Arbeloa will be seen by large numbers of people.

“He needs to be careful and to think about his duties under the rules and his responsibility to football before commenting to journalists on match officials’ performance.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The fine comes with Arbeloa’s Fulham future already in jeopardy after just seven games at the helm, with former Brentford and Spurs boss Thomas Frank the early front-runner if the Spaniard’s reign is cut short.



Despite draws at Liverpool and against United, Fulham have lost their other four Prem games and defeat at home to Hull on Saturday may prove a fatal blow.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez declares civil war at Man Utd in biggest outburst since Roy Keane – Jason Wilcox is in the firing line
Sports.content:
Next

LISANDRO MARTINEZ channelled Roy Keane with his declaration of civil war at Manchester United.

Martinez’s outburst is the most explosive post-match interview by a United player since Keane opined it was “the end of the road” for his team in April 2001.



That was following a Champions League quarter-final loss to Bayern Munich. This United side are a quarter of the way through the elongated league phase.

Keane questioned whether his team-mates – himself included – were good enough. United had just secured a third consecutive league title.



Martinez has gone further and higher. He looked up and pointed upwards at separate stages of his interview with Gabriel Clarke, explicitly referring to those at the top.

Clarke is a peerless post-match interrogator yet even he seemed taken aback by Martinez’s candour. The interview has already been viewed 7.4 million times on Prime Sport’s X account.

One of the United press officers was taken ill on the eve of the Atletico Madrid game, so a recently-appointed communications team member chaperoned Martinez as he lobbed grenade after grenade. How’s the job going?

Jason Wilcox is no longer the United “technical director” but Martinez was undeniably referring to him. Wilcox was promoted to director of football in June last year after Dan Ashworth got out of dodge.

If or when Michael Carrick goes, there will be a clamour for Wilcox to go, too. He is only at United on the recommendation of chief executive and former Manchester City colleague Omar Berrada.

Elevating the former Southampton DoF to the same role within a year was a leap. Sir Jim Ratcliffe claimed Wilcox has the “best eyes in football” and he will never be able to live that quote down.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

As impressive as United’s 2025 summer window was, Wilcox did want Liam Delap. He also thought Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was worthy of interview in January.

Although the buck still stops with the head coach, that is not the case with transfers at United.

It is Wilcox who poses with signings at their Carrington training complex and whose quotes are attached to the press releases.

We have not heard much else from him. There was a leaked recording from the Manchester United Former Players’ Association dinner that Wilcox spoke at last year. His only specific media engagement was in-house.

That was on the back of a three-game winning streak last October. Less than three months later, United had a new head coach.



Wilcox has been a sheepish figure during his two-and-a-half years at United. He briefly stuck his head around the corner in Gothenburg in August to discuss some trivial topics.

At Selhurst Park last year, Wilcox warmly greeted one of United’s favourite reporters as he walked past the mixed zone.

He knows journalists from his time at City, where he could talk until the cows came home in his role as academy head.

The recent international break was an ideal opportunity for Wilcox to get on the front foot and answer pressing questions about United’s underwhelming and frugal transfer window.

Instead, Wilcox kept mum. That deafening silence is not helping him or United, particularly now that Martinez has questioned his position.



It was telling that United did not provide a backgrounder on their recent summer recruitment, having done so in the previous four summers.

Behind the scenes, Wilcox is not afraid of butting heads. A well-placed source said he was “out of order” during the infamous January meeting with Ruben Amorim that eventually led to the Portuguese engineering his own sacking. Another source described the summit as “horrendous”.

Club sources said Wilcox was entitled to question Amorim and that he was his “biggest supporter”. Amorim was incensed that Wilcox referred to himself as “the manager” to staff at Carrington.



During Amorim’s remarkable press conference at Leeds that preceded his exit, he alluded to figures at United being sensitive to criticism from former captain Gary Neville. Wilcox called one of Neville’s former team-mates to enlighten them following their dismay over the sale of Scott McTominay in August 2024.

Some agency figures like Wilcox. Others say he can be “stubborn and egotistical”.

Few at Southampton shed tears when Wilcox departed after 15 months. His appointment of Russell Martin did secure immediate promotion back to the Premier League.

Martinez may have a sharp axe to grind with Wilcox as he arrived at the beginning of the end for Erik ten Hag, Martinez’s mentor at United and Ajax. Wilcox told Ten Hag that Sofyan Amrabat’s season-long loan would not be made permanent in 2024.

Martinez has form for challenging the hierarchy. He called the Ajax technical director Gerry Hamstra a “f***ing nobody” as he agitated to join United in July 2022.



Do not expect a climbdown from Martinez. He doubled down when he chatted to Peter Schmeichel in Madrid.

Schmeichel is so obsequious where United are concerned he wore a club tie to the funeral for the beloved receptionist Kath Phipps and sings along to the pre-match Take Me Home anthem at Old Trafford. He still bills himself as a club ambassador.

He is a risible choice of an interviewer for US station CBS yet Martinez gave him quotes that suggested Schmeichel had transformed into Clarke.

The Elland Road directors’ box is to the left of the away section and Wilcox will hear ardent support for Martinez on Sunday,

Martinez has been in a rut. He was culpable for Dominic Solanke’s equaliser for Tottenham and scored an own goal at Fulham last month.



This is the 28-year-old’s fifth season at United and he has missed 92 games through injury. Martinez has entered the final year of his contract, though United have the option to extend it by a year. That should be a colourful conversation.

Sports.title: Jurrien Timber reminds Dream Team bosses of his sky-high ceiling with 17-point masterclass against Lille
Sports.content:
Next

HERE at Dream Team HQ we almost forgot that Jurrien Timber (£4.5m) is an elite-level asset.

The Dutchman provided a timely reminder of his pedigree in the form of a 17-point haul as Arsenal beat Lille 3-0 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Separate ankle and groin injuries have forced Timber to miss approximately 25 games for club and country over the last few months.



He’s still yet to play 90 minutes since he was forced off against Everton on 14th March.



However, if his most recent performance is anything to go by, the 25-year-old is more than ready for a full shift whenever Mikel Arteta requires one.

Dream Team managers will remember that Timber, prior to his injury setbacks, was right up there with team-mate Gabriel (£5.4m) as the most effective defender in the game.

On top of the Gunners’ defensive might, he excels individually in terms of tackles, bonus points and attacking contributions.



This was evident against Lille when Timber broke the deadlock with a superbly economical combination of a smart first touch followed by a composed finish, an expertly-executed dink.

Prior to his goal, he created two chances – one of them deemed a big chance by stats boffins Opta – when he found Bruno Guimaraes (£3.9m) with a sharp pullback before his inviting cross picked out Mikel Merino (£3.3m) in a promising position.

Timber also made two tackles (+1 pt) and fell just one PPM short of three bonus points when he was replaced by Ben White (£4.8m) in the 78th minute.



Add in the hosts’ clean sheet and ex-Ajax man banked a cool 17 points.

Consequently, Timber is currently the best-performing player in his position this Gameweek as things stand.

No doubt more than a few gaffers will be itching to recruit him but they will have to be patient.

All the while Timber and White are sharing minutes at right-back, neither are particularly viable.

But if the Netherlands international reestablishes himself as clear first choice, as was the case before his spell on the sidelines, he may become one of the strongest options in the game.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez's rant missed the big point about Man Utd - he's part of the problem
Sports.content:
The ramifications of the Manchester City case are so significant that many football debates cannot avoid mentioning their financial chicanery.

For spending far too much of their own money on players over the past couple of decades - well, for disguising where that money came from - City’s owners have landed their club at the mercy of sanctions that could send it into oblivion.

Running parallel to this storyline is one now promoted by Lisandro Martinez - Manchester United have not spent enough on players.

For spending beyond their means, City are in all sorts of trouble. For spending within their means, United’s hierarchy is getting pelters from one of its own players.

‌



That is essentially that.

Every word from Lisandro Martinez's explosive interview calling out Man Utd board READ MORE :

But leave aside the source of the revenue that funded their transfer activity, the simple fact is that over the last decade, City and United have spent roughly the same amount, in gross terms, on players. City’s gross spend over the past ten seasons is around £1.8billion, United’s around the £1.7billion mark.

In fact, in that time, United’s net spend of around £1.1billion is more than City’s, which comes in at just under the £1billion mark.

Of course, what Martinez was specifically referring to was the transfer activity in the most recent window. In gross and net terms, United lagged way behind City.

‌



In the overall rankings of gross Premier League spenders in the summer window, United were ninth. In the net spending table, they were seventh. But you cannot judge a club’s ambition on one window, as Martinez seems to have done.

View 3 Images The Premier League's 'Big Six' net spends compared for the most recent summer window

The bottom line is that over the past ten years, United’s outlay on players should have given them a more formidable squad than the one Michael Carrick has at his disposal right now.

There has not been a lack of ambition down the years, there has been a lack of shrewd judgement. Too many signings have not worked out, have not had the right character for the challenge.

‌



And you can probably include Martinez in that bracket. He has had his moments, and he has had to recover from some serious physical setbacks, most notably the cruciate ligament injury that kept him out for ten months in 2025.

But Martinez has hardly been a stand-out Premier League defender since he arrived at Old Trafford in 2022.

It has been reported that some senior players support his overt criticism of the executives, in particular his criticism of Jason Wilcox, United’s director of football.

View 3 Images Martinez has struggled with injury issues since arriving at Old Trafford

‌



Fair enough. Fair enough. But never mind the players United should have bought, the ones they have should be taking a long, hard look at themselves.

I was at Old Trafford for the draw against Spurs last Saturday and the deficiencies in that performance could not be laid at Wilcox’s door.

It was down to those characters on the park that the Spurs players, to a man, looked fitter and sharper.

It was down to those characters on the park that the Spurs players, to a man, looked more enthusiastic and hungrier.

‌



It was down to those characters on the park that the Spurs players, to a man, looked faster.

In the defeat to Atletico Madrid, United were a bit better. But it remains painfully obvious that the lack of intensity in this United squad is the core problem.

And where does that come from? It comes from a deep-rooted malaise that sees United’s signings think they have made it when they join such an iconic institution. It comes from complacency. It comes from not having that extra level of self-motivation.

‌



It comes from the players. It doesn’t come from Jason Wilcox.

Sports.title: Man Utd star Amad lets rip after Atletico Madrid defeat - 'F*****g disgrace'
Sports.content:
Man Utd star Amad lets rip after Atletico Madrid defeat - 'F*****g disgrace'

Manchester United suffered their first defeat in this season's Champions League at the hands of Atletico Madrid, with the Red Devils having been reduced to 10 men after Leny Yoro's red card

View 3 Images Amad vented his fury on social media (Image: Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

Manchester United star Amad has branded their controversial 2-0 loss against Atletico Madrid a 'f***ing disgrace' in a charged social media post. Amad, 24, was a second-half substitute as United attempted to salvage at least a draw from the Spanish capital.

‌



‌



The Red Devils gave themselves an uphill battle by conceding inside the first minute, with Atletico's Pablo Barrios putting them ahead. United improved as the game went on but their hopes of taking home a point or three were dashed by Leny Yoro's red card.

‌



Following a VAR check after on-field referee Glenn Nyberg had initially allowed play to continue, Yoro was adjudged to have brought down Jonathan David while being the last defender and he was promptly sent off. Michael Carrick's side struggled to create chances from thereon and conceded a second time through Ademola Lookman in the closing stages.

‌



Post-match, Amad vented his fury with a post on Snapchat. "F*****g disgrace; I have no words," the forward wrote.

Amad wasn't the only United player to speak out, with Lisandro Martinez choosing to direct his anger at the club's board for their supposed lack of investment during the summer transfer window. Carrick hadn't listened to Martinez's post-match interview and wanted to focus on the game instead.

"It is a tough enough place to come and to get the start we had obviously puts us in a more difficult situation but I thought we grew into the game," the United manager reflected. "We had four big chances, big opportunities and the game can look very different.

"They were really good opportunities as well, they weren't just little half ones. I thought we didn't finish the first half particularly well, started the second half a little bit better and started having some control without having a real threat.

"Then we had Bruno's [Fernandes] chance again, another good opportunity, and then the red card. That goes against us and then it's difficult after that.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes at odds with Wayne Rooney again as he launches angry Man City tirade
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes at odds with Wayne Rooney again as he launches angry Man City tirade

Manchester United legends Paul Scholes and Wayne Rooney have very different views on the outcome of Manchester City's guilty verdict and their Premier League titles

View 2 Images Paul Scholes would happily accept another title (Image: The Good, The Bad & The Football/ YouTube)

Former Manchester United star Paul Scholes has doubled down on being more than happy to pick up another Premier League medal after Manchester City were found guilty of breaking the division's financial rules. The former midfielder's stance is in stark contrast to that of his United team-mate Wayne Rooney, who doesn't believe they deserve it.

‌



‌



City were found guilty of 114 breaches between 2009 and 2018 and pipped Manchester United to the Premier League title on goal difference in 2012. United thought they had won the league with victory at the Stadium of Light before discovering City sealed a late comeback against Queens Park Rangers thanks to Sergio Aguero's famous goal.

‌



While City have appealed the Independent Commission's verdict and maintain their innocence, the club's rivals are waiting with bated breath to learn what sanction will be imposed. They could receive a fine, points deduction or even be expelled from the division.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

There is also a possibility City lose their titles, though the chances of the runners-up being promoted to champions instead appears remote for the moment. But Scholes, who has 11 Premier League titles to his name, would happily add another medal to his collection.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite, Scholes emphatically responded to Paddy McGuinness' assertion that he wouldn't want the title.

‌



“Why not?" said Scholes. F*****g yeah. I only played 14 times somewhere in the last six months of the season. But yeah, I would take it.

View 2 Images United's stars found out they'd fallen short after full time (Image: Clive Mason/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"We lost on goal difference that year. Do you not think the rest of our team, our teammates, the manager and the staff are working their bollocks off all year to try and win the league? And just because a team did it wrongly, cheated, that we wouldn’t want it?”

Scholes previously described himself as greedy for more silverware. “Keep hearing ex-teammates saying they want trophies taking off them [City] but don’t want their medals,” Scholes wrote on his Instagram story.

“F*** that, I’m a greedy b****** I want my medal”.

‌



One of those team-mates was Rooney, who was asked whether he would accept a retrospective medal by Match of the Day host Kelly Cates

"It’s difficult," he said. "I look at it from the players’ point of view. I’m assuming all the players didn’t know what was going on.

"They went onto the football pitch and won the league, while we finished second. We didn’t finish first. Why would we want a medal for finishing second?"

‌



Rooney previously admitted he wouldn't be comfortable accepting a winner's medal. "I have heard Rio has come out saying about getting another Premier League medal... I wouldn’t really feel comfortable accepting another Premier League medal, if I’m being honest," said Rooney on the Stick To United podcast.

"I don’t think we deserve it, we didn’t do enough that season to win the league. I think we were six or seven points clear with four or five games to go and we threw it away. I’ve seen everything that has come out over the past few days and listening to people and I was putting myself in a Man City player’s shoes.

"It might happen, they might take them [medals] away, but I wouldn’t want it [a medal] because I don’t think as a team we deserved it that year because obviously we didn’t finish first. So when I see team-mates saying I want a medal’, I’m happy with the five I’ve won. I wouldn’t want this one.

Article continues below

"Should they get it stripped for what the owners have done? Yeah maybe, but I wouldn’t feel comfortable accepting it."

Sports.title: Tragic story of Liverpool's hat-trick hero from LASK who died aged 22 with shirt retired
Sports.content:
Tragic story of Liverpool's hat-trick hero from LASK who died aged 22 with shirt retired

The tragic footballer's two former clubs are due to face off in the Champions League

View 3 Images Besian Idrizaj impressed at Liverpool and LASK before his untimely death (Image: Sportsphoto/Allstar, Getty Images)

Wednesday's Champions League match between Liverpool and LASK pits together two of Besian Idrizaj's former clubs. The Austrian striker joined the Reds after leaving the Linz club as a teenager, but tragically lost his life aged just 22.

‌



‌



Idrizaj made his debut for the LASK first team aged 16 and played more than 30 league games before moving to England. The switch came after he impressed at a European Under-17 Championships tournament featuring plenty of stars who would go on to bigger and better things.

‌



France won that tournament, with the likes of Samir Nasri, Karim Benzema and Hatem Ben Arfa in their side. It was also a chance for Cesc Fabregas and Gerard Pique to impress for Spain, while Mark Noble was part of an England side beaten in the third-place play-off by Portugal.

‌



Austria finished behind England and Portugal in the group stage but Idrizaj caught the eye. He stayed in Linz for the 2004/05 season but wasn't going to pass up the opportunity to try his luck at Anfield.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Ryan Gravenberch red card agreement as Liverpool get unanimous verdict READ MORE :

Florian Wirtz has had long enough - now Liverpool must consider biting the bullet READ MORE :

"I have always been a Liverpool fan and it is a dream come true to play for them. If you get a chance to go to Liverpool on trial then you have to take it," the young striker said upon agreeing to a trial with the Reds in 2005.

‌



He initially joined the academy after impressing, putting himself within touching distance of sharing a pitch with a group of players he had seen lift the Champions League trophy in Istanbul. "You cannot ignore a trial with the reigning Champions League winners. I would even have swum across the channel just to take part," he added

During his debut season with Liverpool's youth set-up, Idrizaj was a team-mate of the likes of Jay Spearing and Jack Hobbs, players who would go on to represent the Reds' first team. Idrizaj was integrated into the senior squad himself by Rafa Benitez during pre-season in 2006 and 2007, bagging an unforgettable hat-trick in a friendly.

Following an impressive display alongside Craig Bellamy in a win over Wrexham in 2006, the young forward headed out on loan to Luton Town, netting his maiden senior competitive goal in English football. Upon his return to Merseyside the subsequent summer, he was given a starting berth in another Wrexham meeting and inside half an hour he had scored all three of Liverpool's goals.

‌



View 3 Images Rafa Benitez blooded Idrizaj in a pre-season squad also including Gabriel Paletta and Alvaro Arbeloa (Image: Gary M. Prior, Getty Images)

"I still remember the day," his brother Qerim told The Athletic in 2020. "At the time, the internet was not like now and if we called Besian we had to have a prepaid card.

"He called home afterwards and he said, 'Did you check the Liverpool website?' I said, 'No. Why? What happened?' He said, 'Just check it.' He was really proud.

‌



"And it was something to be proud of. So I typed in Liverpool FC and went onto the homepage, and the first story was Besian Idrizaj scores a 23-minute hat-trick. I said, 'Wow, man. This is amazing? How did you do that?'"

Rather than promote Idrizaj directly into the Liverpool first team, Benitez permitted him to depart on loan once more - initially to Crystal Palace and subsequently to Wacker Innsbruck in the player's native country. During that period, though, the forward endured a scary moment when he collapsed on the pitch, with medics believing a virus to be responsible.

Idrizaj's contract at Anfield expired in 2008 and Wacker chose not to sign him on a free transfer. After heading back to LASK to train and maintain his fitness, he experienced another health scare and stepped away from football for several months.

‌



The youngster did ultimately make it back onto the pitch, first in Germany and then in Swansea. He featured four times in the 2009/10 Championship campaign but then, just weeks after the season concluded, he suffered a suspected heart attack in his sleep and tragically passed away. He was 22 years old.

View 3 Images Swansea players commemorated the striker after their 2011 play-off final win (Image: Matthew Ashton, Corbis via Getty Images)

Idrizaj made a lasting impression on his Swansea colleagues during his brief spell in south Wales. "A lot of us still talk about him," goalkeeper Dorus de Vries said during the push for promotion under Brendan Rodgers the following season.

‌



"He is still in our thoughts. He was a great colleague, a great team-mate, but he was also a great friend and you can't just forget that. We said as a group that this year would be for him and hopefully we are doing him proud this season."

Following their play-off final triumph at Wembley, Swansea's players hoisted the trophy while wearing T-shirts emblazoned with Idrizaj's name and image, with the club subsequently retiring his squad number, 40. "The journey was a great remembrance to him all the way through the season. I felt that he was really in the heart of the players and people," said Rodgers.

When Liverpool and LASK crossed paths in the Europa League in 2023, Besian Idrizaj was undoubtedly at the forefront of many minds, both at Anfield and the Raiffeisen Arena. As the two sides prepare to lock horns once more in Austria this week, thoughts will surely turn again to a talent cruelly lost far too soon.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher slams Lisandro Martinez for explosive Man Utd interview - 'Out of order'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher slams Lisandro Martinez for explosive Man Utd interview - 'Out of order'

Lisandro Martinez made headlines after Manchester United's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid by calling out the club hierarchy, including director of football Jason Wilcox

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher has hit out at Lisandro Martinez (Image: CBS Sports)

Jamie Carrgher has slammed Manchester United star Lisandro Martinez for his 'awful' comments following their abject 2-0 loss away to Atletico Madrid. Martinez, 28, strongly criticised United's board for a lack of investment in the summer transfer window, leaving Michael Carrick short in several areas for his first full season in charge.

‌



‌



The Argentine even called out the club's director of football, Jason Wilcox, saying that he 'expects more' from him. Martinez's explosive interview has earned him praise from supporters who are also critical of Wilcox and the rest of United's hierarchy, but Carragher - like Wayne Rooney - believes that he was 'out of order'.

‌



"Doesn't do anybody any good at all, and they (the quotes) will be the story now for the next few days, all about this," the Liverpool legend began on CBS Sports. "Every set of supporters don't like the suits, the guys upstairs, so United fans will lap this up and think it's great.

‌



"I think it's awful that he's come out and said that right now, I do. When he's saying they had a fantastic season last season, they didn't. A manager got sacked last season. Sacked.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"They finished third because they had no cup games, they weren't in Europe, got knocked out the cup competitions very early. Man United third. The reason they finished third is because Liverpool and Chelsea were that bad as well.

"Now we're seeing the real Manchester United this season. The reason why they didn't buy players in the summer is because the last four or five years since Martinez has been there, I think they've been in the Champions League once - this season (sic).

"So if every season you don't get Champions League money and every season Manchester United are spending £200million in the transfer market, sooner or later it has to stop because the money's not there.

‌



"So this summer, the money Manchester United are paying out, it's for players they bought years ago, the next instalment of it. That's why there isn't that money there, you can't just keep going with it.

Was Lisandro Martinez right to criticise the Manchester United board? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez and his team-mates have won two of their nine games this season (Image: Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images)

‌



"Because there's a squad of players with different managers, they haven't achieved anything. They've been awful, awful again tonight.

"And him as well when he's talking about the start of this season - I think he's a good player, by the way, he's a World Cup winner, I get that - he's had an awful start to the season. Awful, really poor.

"People will lap it up, Manchester United fans will, that doesn't nobody any good at all... This will just be the talk of the town now. This will blow up, explode and I think he's out of order."

‌



Former United captain Rooney was in agreement with Carragher, describing Martinez's comments as 'disrespectful'. "It's a difficult one because I always used to feel like I was outspoken as a player and you want to have your opinion, but I think he's maybe gone too far," the ex-striker told Prime Video Sport.

"That should be down to the manager, and that should stay internal because the fans want to hear the players speak and they want to see them care. He clearly cares and wants the club to invest more money and more players, and if they do that, I think he'll be one of the players out of the door if I'm being honest with his performances.

View 3 Images Wayne Rooney has told Lisandro Martinez to look at himself before criticising others (Image: Maciej Rogowski/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

‌



"His performances haven't been good enough but I think in some ways he is right, in terms of the club need to invest more at the top end of the pitch and in defence as well. I think it looks like that was a bit of an agenda from him because that doesn't mirror the performance. I thought the performance was better.

"I think it's a bit disrespectful to his team-mates as well because he's disrespecting his team-mates, he's saying they're not good enough. I think Bruno [Fernandes] is probably the only one who has any right coming out and saying something like that, if I'm being honest as captain.

"And even then it should be behind closed doors if there are issues, which does happen. Players have conversations with the manager, the manager then has a conversation with the board.

‌



"But that interview there, it's not going to help the situation the club is in at the minute. Now all that's going to bring is more noise around it, the players are unhappy, they're unsettled, they don't trust in their own team-mates, that's not going to help at all."

United boss Carrick put Martinez's criticism down to being in the heat of the moment after Tuesday's defeat. The Red Devils will travel to Leeds on Sunday back in the Premier League and look to do their talking on the pitch.

Sports.title: Every word from Lisandro Martinez's explosive interview calling out Man Utd board
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez delivered a jaw-dropping post-match interview following Manchester United's defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. The defender came out on the offensive, targeting the club's board and critiquing the hierarchy's lack of investment in the playing squad over the summer.

Already, the Argentina international has come under criticism from former United captain Wayne Rooney, while team-mate Youri Tielemans could not be drawn on his opinion, following Martinez's words. Likewise, Michael Carrick stopped short of providing an assessment on his charge's savage verdict.

Nevertheless, it was an explosive interview that stopped viewers in their tracks. Read the transcript below:

Reporter: How do you sum up the performance?

‌



Martinez: “Really poor. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.

"We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. Today, Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today.

This is not a Champions League-quality squad? You expected more investment in the summer?

‌



"I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

In which areas?

"In general. Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team. It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here. It's disappointing.

"I don't think so. He does his best. Every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season. The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don't change next season, is a big problem.

Often the manager is removed...

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Bruno Fernandes 'fed up' as midfield star speaks about Michael Carrick struggles
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Bruno Fernandes 'fed up' as midfield star speaks about Michael Carrick struggles

Manchester United's sub-par results have manager Michael Carrick feeling the pressure in the Old Trafford hot seat

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is under the cosh at Manchester United (Image: Getty)

Manchester United sit 13th in the Premier League with six games played. Michael Carrick is already facing questions ahead of a trip to face Leeds United.

‌



‌



Carrick was given the keys to begin this season following an excellent end to the 2025/26 campaign. He excelled after taking over from Ruben Amorim and guided United to a third-place finish.

‌



But so far this term, United have won just one of their first six top-flight matches, that being a 5-2 victory over Ipswich Town. They've lost twice, to both Hull City and Manchester City, and their latest league outing was a disappointing 1-1 draw versus Tottenham, who had been reduced to 10 men. Draws against Everton and Fulham have left a lot to be desired.

‌



The manager is coming under a considerable amount of scrutiny for this start, but an ex-United midfielder thinks that Carrick simply needs to be given time. Mirror Football brings you all the latest from Old Trafford.

Paul Pogba speaks out on Michael Carrick

Paul Pogba made a total of 233 appearances for United, scoring 39 goals across two spells with the club. He spoke to Sky Sports and had a clear opinion on the under-pressure Carrick.

View 3 Images Pogba says Carrick needs time (Image: Getty)

‌



"It's just the start of the season, there's nothing much to say, it's just the start of the season and the season is very long," Pogba said. "He showed last season when he came, everybody said he was the manager that will change everything.

"Now that the results don't come they say maybe he's too young. One day or the other it can change a lot, they just have to give them time and it will be fine."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Bruno Fernandes 'fed up'

A current United star, captain Bruno Fernandes, has four goals and three assists to his name so far this season and is currently his side's top scorer. However, with results not going United's way, a club legend thinks he's growing impatient.

Wayne Rooney was asked about Fernandes on Stick to United and said: "He's fed up. I genuinely do think he looks, 'Oh, here we go again.' There are only so many times…

View 3 Images Rooney thinks Fernandes is fed up at United (Image: Getty)

‌



"He has carried the team, but sometimes you need taking out of that position, of that role, to breathe again. I feel like now you can see it building up and there's going to be an explosion with him if this carries on.

"He's not scared to come out and voice his opinion. So there is going to be that explosion if this carries on the way it's going. For me, you need that three in midfield at the minute because they're getting outrun, they're getting outplayed.

"All of a sudden, then you've got [Kobbie] Mainoo and [Youri] Tielemans, who are not the quickest and not the most mobile, to cover the full width of the pitch as two midfield players, and they can't do it."

Arsenal have ground to make up in the Premier League as an away trip to Nottingham Forest awaits

Arsenal turn their attention back to Premier League action after last night's Champions League tie against Lille. The Gunners got back to winning ways in the top-flight against Leeds last week after their surprise 3-0 loss to Brighton before the international break.

‌



Now Mikel Arteta will be hoping his players can string a run together as they chase Manchester City at the top. It's Nottingham Forest up next in the league on Sunday, before visits from Everton and Hull City sandwiched in between a trip to face Liverpool at Anfield.

Mikel Arteta responds to Dowman claim

Mikel Arteta has agreed with Lionel Messi's claim that Max Dowman is on the path to greatness. The Arsenal boss was full of pride for the teenager's mention from the Argentina hero in his top 10 list of rising Adidas athletes, stating: "If Messi, who is the best ever player, says that

Sports.title: NFL player Hill found liable for two counts of battery
Sports.content:
Tyreek Hill found liable for two of 10 counts in battery civil trial; Hill, 32, ordered to pay estranged wife $500k in damages; former Dolphins and Chiefs player's timeline to return to NFL still unclear

Tyreek Hill: NFL free agent receiver found liable for two counts of battery as jury awards estranged wife $500k

Tyreek Hill was most recently with the Miami Dolphins before being released in February

A Miami jury has found Tyreek Hill liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by Lakeeta Vaccaro, ending the high-profile civil trial involving the NFL wide receiver and his estranged wife.

Hill, who has played for the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs and Miami Dolphins, was found liable for two counts of battery - one stemming from an incident in January 2024, and another from April 2025.

The jury awarded Vaccaro $500,000 (£377,000) in compensatory damages but did not award her punitive damages.

The jury found Hill, 32, not liable for eight other counts that included battery, assault and continuing domestic violence.

The trial involved allegations of abuse made by Vaccaro, 30, who on the stand described instances in which Hill allegedly pulled her hair and "treated me like I was, just, a man."

Hill took the stand last week and mostly denied what he called "false allegations" made by Vaccaro, while saying in one instance he shoved her and "created a hole in the wall."

Hill, wearing a dark polo shirt on Tuesday, embraced one of his attorneys and shook hands with others following the verdict before leaving the courtroom by himself.

It is not immediately clear what the verdict means for Hill's return to the NFL.

He is still working his way back from a dislocated knee and torn ligaments suffered in September 2025 while he was with the Dolphins, but his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has indicated he could be ready to play by November.

Sports.title: 'Awful' and 'disrespectful' - Carra and Rooney criticise Martinez outburst
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher has branded Lisandro Martinez's comments criticising the Manchester United hierarchy as "awful" - saying the player should look at himself because of his "really poor" start to the season.

In an astonishing post-match interview after United's 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid with 10 men, defender Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club chiefs, critisicing the lack of summer investment in the squad.

Martinez - who is out of contract at the end of the season - said he expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox, in the most recent transfer window in which they failed to improve their options at left-back and up front.

And responding to those comments, Sky Sports pundit Carragher told CBS Sports: "It doesn't do anybody any good at all, and they will be the story now for the next few days all about this.

Image: Manchester United spent less than the 'Big Six'

"Every set of supporters don't like the suits or the guys upstairs, so United fans will lap this up and think it's great. I think it's awful that he's come out and said that right now. I do.

"And when he's saying 'we had a fantastic season last season', they didn't. A manager got sacked last season. Sacked.

"They finished third because they had no cup games. They got knocked out of the cup competitions very early. The reason they finished third is Liverpool and Chelsea were that bad as well.

"Now we're seeing the real Manchester United this season. They were awful again tonight.

"And him as well, when he's talking at the start of this season - I think he's a good player, by the way, he's a World Cup winner, I get that - he's had an awful start to the season. Awful. Really poor.

"And yeah, people are lapping it up, Manchester United fans will. That does nobody any good at all."

What Martinez said

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is asked about Lisandro Martinez's criticism of the club's transfer strategy following the team's 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League

Man Utd spent £155m on just four major summer signings after a third-place Premier League finish last season, which earned a return to the Champions League for the first time in three years.

But Martinez is not happy with how the club navigated the summer.

"I have to control myself a lot, but sometimes it's a reflection of how our club is at the moment," Martinez told Amazon Prime.

"We had a fantastic season last season, and now we expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete because many teams have brought in many players as well."

Asked whether he had expected more investment in the squad in summer, Martinez said: "Yes, 100 per cent.

"I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest. And also, as a player, we have to do more.

"It's also important to build a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."
