Sports.title: Harry Kane overtakes Lionel Messi in stunning Champions League feat as he chases Cristiano Ronaldo streak
Sports.content:
Harry Kane overtakes Lionel Messi in stunning Champions League feat as he chases Cristiano Ronaldo streak

Harry Kane has impressively overtaken Lionel Messi for Champions League goals scored over the age of 30 in fewer games.

The striker netted twice in Bayern Munich’s entertaining 3-3 draw at Norwegian side Viking on Tuesday evening.

4 Harry Kane fired scored twice for Bayern in a 3-3 draw against Viking and moved past Messi's tally for Champions League goals after 30 Credit: Getty

Trailing 2-0 at the interval, Kane inspired Bayern to a comeback, scoring twice while playing a key role in his side’s third before they unfortunately conceded late on.

Kane’s first came from the penalty spot in the 54th minute and the England captain only had to wait a further six minutes to grab his second of the evening.

And it was that goal that took his tally to 36 goals in 40 games after the age of 30.

Kane, now 33, has bolstered his account since arriving in Bavaria in 2023, so much so that he has now eclipsed Messi’s total.

The Argentine netted 35 goals in 48 games beyond his 30th birthday.

That shows the magnitude of Kane’s prowess in recent years while providing a ringing endorsement for his recent Ballon d’Or nomination.

Kane’s double means he has now scored for nine successive games to equal Robert Lewandowski and Ruud van Nistelrooy's record.

And now Cristiano Ronaldo’s record of 11 goals in succession is firmly in his sights ahead of the visit of Arsenal to the Allianz Arena next week, live on talkSPORT.

Should get on the scoresheet against the Gunners, Kane’s opportunity to equal Ronaldo will come in the trip to Atletico Madrid next month.

Kane’s season at a glance

The striker is now up to eight goals for the season while registering four assists in his nine appearances.

4 Kane has now surpassed Messi's tally and is also chasing Cristiano Ronaldo's record

4 He is also now eyeing Ronaldo's feat of 11 consecutive goals after scoring in his ninth straight European game Credit: Getty

Kane kicked off the season in style with three goals and three assists in five first five Bundesliga outings.

His brilliance has spilled onto the international scene with Kane having achieved his 125th cap for England, matching Peter Shilton's all-time national appearance record.

He scored six times in England’s four matches during the recent international break, taking his tally to 91 goals for the Three Lions.

Kane’s contract with Bayern expires next summer but negotiations are on going over a two-year extension.

Bayern Munich sporting director Christoph Freund said on Friday that he is ‘very positive’ about discussions with Kane who himself has expressed his desire to remain at the club.

"There are always scenarios as long as it's not signed," Freund said. "There's no new development.

4 Kane's goals fired Bayern to a league and cup double as he scored 61 times for the club last season Credit: Getty

"The talks are going well. We're very positive, everyone knows we're determined to extend his contract and Harry feels very comfortable here."

Since his arrival from Tottenham, Kane has scored an incredible 156 goals in 154 appearances.

He has scooped the Bundesliga Golden Boot in each of his three seasons, whilst firing Bayern to two Bundesliga titles.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney slams ‘disrespectful’ Lisandro Martinez as Man United star calls out board in furious outburst
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez slammed the Manchester United board after defeat to Atletico Madrid - but it didn't sit well with Wayne Rooney.

United conceded inside minute one of their 2-0 Champions League loss and Leny Yoro was later shown a straight red for a last man foul.

3 Martinez did not hold back on his assessment of United as he called out the board for their transfer business Credit: Getty

Ademola Lookman made it game, set and match for Atletico with 11 minutes to play as they won their first match of the league phase.

It meant United have won just two of nine matches this season in all competitions, adding further pressure on head coach Michael Carrick.

But Martinez believes their shortcomings are down to the club board and their transfer business in the summer.

What did Martinez say in his outburst?

"It was really poor, really poor," he told Amazon Prime minutes after the full-time whistle.

"I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection of our club at the moment. We did it last season and now we expect more from the top.

"To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from our technical director.

"I have to be honest and also the players have to do more but it's just important when you make a strong squad for this type of night."

Martinez added: "Last season we created a base to build an amazing team. It's annoying and disappointing to come here and I'm not seeing my team get an amazing result here."

On whether Carrick has not been backed enough, he replied. "I don't think so. He does his best. The team knows how you play, every detail and if you don't change the next season, it's a big problem.

"You start changing, changing, changing manager, but what about other areas. I can't say more. It's easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

Rooney responds to Martinez rant

United legend Rooney, who won the Champions League at the club, was a pundit for Amazon and gave an instant response to Martinez.

"I actually disagree, because I think the performance was okay. I think the performance was better, there were some positive signs in there.

"It's a difficult one because I always used to feel I was outspoken as a player, you want to have your opinion.

"I think he's maybe gone a bit too far. That's down to the manager, and that should really stay internal.

"The fans want to hear the players speak, they want to hear the players care, so you can clearly see that he cares and he wants the club to invest more money in more players.

"I think if they do that, he'll probably be one of the players who's out the door, if we're being honest, his performances haven't been good enough.

3 Rooney acknowledged Martinez's frustrations, but claims he was disrespectful to his teammates during the rant Credit: Getty

"I think in some ways he is right, in terms of the club need to invest more at the top end of the pitch, in defence as well. But it looks like that was a bit of an agenda he's wanted to say, because that doesn't mirror the performance, I thought it was better.

Rooney added: "I think it's a bit disrespectful to his teammate as well, because he's disrespecting his teammates, he's saying the team aren't good enough...

"I think Bruno (Fernandes) is probably the only one who has any right to come out and say anything like that, if we're being honest, as captain.

"Even then, it should be behind closed doors if there's issues, which does happen - players have conversations with the manager, the manager has conversations with the board.

"But I think that interview there, it's not going to help the situation the club are in at the minute. That's going to bring greater noise around it, players are not happy, they're not settled, they don't trust their own teammates, that's not going to help at all."

What has Michael Carrick said?

Man United manager Carrick was asked about Martinez's comments, but said: "I haven't seen it.

3 United are now winless in five matches across all competitions, with defeats coming in three of those Credit: Getty

"After a game like this you come here to try and get something from the game and you are disappointed and can be emotional. I have not seen it so I don't think it is the right time.

"We all care and show that in different ways but now is the time to be together and work through."

Sports.title: Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa escapes touchline ban for claiming officials 'would not let Man United lose' after 1-1 Premier League draw
Sports.content:
Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa escapes touchline ban for claiming officials 'would not let Man United lose' after 1-1 Premier League draw

Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has avoided a touchline ban after implying officials were biased toward Manchester United in last month’s Premier League draw.

United rescued a point in the 89th minute at Craven Cottage, prompting Arbeloa to say referee Michael Oliver and his officials ‘would not let Manchester United lose’ in his post-match interview.

Arbeloa admitted the FA charge and was subsequently fined £25,000. However, the FA stopped short of imposing a touchline ban and instead issued him with a warning as it was his first offence.

In his immediate post-match comments, Arbeloa could barely contain his anger.

'Every decision was for them and I knew after the game against Man City that they would not let Man Utd lose, he said on Sky Sports. 'We deserved a little bit more.

'We were so, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team.

'We knew what happened last week (United conceding a contentious goal to Manchester City). We have seen what the referee has been doing in all the matches, so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky.'

Alvaro Arbeloa has yet to win a league game with Fulham, who sit bottom after six games

Fulham argued that there were mitigating circumstances, noting that Arbeloa did not double down on his comments during his post-match press conference, is new to the Premier League and is not a native English speaker.

The former Real Madrid coach is under pressure at Fulham, who sit bottom of the Premier League having failed to win any of their opening six games.

Fulham threw away three points last weekend, conceding twice in the final eight minutes against Ipswich Town.

With Hull City and Coventry City up next, Arbeloa could face the sack if they continue slumping.

Sports.title: Football coach goes viral for his 'fight' not to even glance at glamorous journalist during interview
Sports.content:
A Czech football coach has gone viral for his apparent 'fight' to not even glance at a glamorous journalist during a post-match interview.

Sports reporter Sabina Jákšová was interviewing David Oulehla, coach of the Czech second division team FK Viagem Ústí nad Labem, last Friday following their 3-2 defeat against SFC Opava.

During the interview, Mr Oulehla appeared to be avoiding looking at her at all costs – a move that many on social media noticed.

One person wrote: 'He's fighting for his life.'

Another said: 'His level of self-control is biblical.'

And a third wrote: 'His wife is watching... total respect for his eye control!'

Ms Jákšová joined the second division club as a presenter at the end of the last season.

She said following her appointment: 'The club's management contacted me directly and made me the offer. I admit that I was happy and surprised at the same time.

Sports reporter Sabina Jákšová (pictured, left) was interviewing David Oulehla (pictured, right), coach of the Czech second division team FK Viagem Ústínad Labem

Many online commented on his efforts to avoid eye contact with the glamorous reporter

Sabina Jákšová has worked at the club since the end of the last season

She had admitted that her knowledge of football is 'rather basic'

'I thought about it for a while, but finally said: "Why not? I'll try". However, I had no experience, so I learned everything along the way.'

She said that though her knowledge of football was 'rather basic to minimal... I like to learn something new, try new things and develop. At the same time, it's all very authentic. I'm learning how the club works as I go along.'

Last month, TNT Sports presenter Laura Woods left her colleagues stifling their laughter on a live broadcast with a rogue slip of the tongue.

The presenter was leading the post-game dissection of Liverpool's late 3-2 win over Atletico Madrid when she said: 'Diego Simeone, obviously quite a fiery character, he got himself sent off after the winner from Virgin.... Virgil van Dijk.'

Woods immediately realised the unfortunate mistake and laughed before regaining her composure.

Her pundits on duty for the night, Steve McManaman and Michael Owen, could be heard sniggering in the background.

Fortunately the footage at the time was a replay of an Atletico Madrid goal so viewers were unable to see the full reaction to Woods's blunder.

When the camera does switch back to the pitch-side set-up with all three on screen, Mr Owen and Woods still appeared to be smirking.

Sports.title: Team-mates accuse British cycling's axed golden boy Matthew Richardson of having a 'God complex' - as his girlfriend ignores drama to win at the World Championships in his absence
Sports.content:
British cycling's golden boy Matthew Richardson has been accused of having a 'God complex' after being axed from the team following allegations of using racist language.

Richardson, 27, was sent home from the Cycling World Championships on Monday with the 'misconduct' probe over his behaviour still ongoing, while his 23-year-old cyclist girlfriend Emma Finucane remains at the competition in Shanghai and raced to qualifying victory for the Women's Team Sprint on Wednesday morning.

Richardson has been accused of using racist and discriminatory language towards others and using the n-word, according to The Times, who also report that riders in the World Class Programme described him as 'arrogant' and having a 'God complex'.

'At the velodrome he’s the golden boy,' they added. 'Matty is one of their best chances of a gold medal in LA and he knows it.'

British Cycling began investigating Richardson after a formal complaint was made, it is understood.

The Olympic medallist broke his silence on Tuesday, writing on Instagram that he was 'deeply disappointed' and would co-operate with Team GB, who he joined after leaving the Australian programme.

Matthew Richardson (right) is not competing at the World Championships amid the ongoing misconduct probe but his girlfriend Emma Finucane (left) remains

He said: 'I understand the seriousness of what has been raised in recent reports about my withdrawal from the 2026 UCI Track Cycling World Championships.

'British Cycling has said it looks into matters like this through its established procedures. I will co-operate fully with its processes. I assure everyone that I will do so properly, and appropriately and with contrition for the feelings of anyone who might be affected.

'Out of fairness to everyone involved, and on advice, like British Cycling, I will not be commenting further until any process is complete. I am deeply disappointed to miss the World Championships, and I wish the Great Britain team and every rider competing the very best.'

Richardson's exit sent shockwaves through the sport, while his girlfriend Finucane welcomed her parents to Shanghai ahead of the competition on Monday.

Her brother, Sean, 21, told the Daily Mail of his family's 'shock and surprise' at the latest development.

He said: ‘We are all pretty shocked and surprised - he’s a lovely guy. He’s been here a lot and never shown any signs of that sort of behaviour. My parents flew out to Shanghai yesterday - none of us knew.'

Emma, who won four gold medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, is due to compete in the Individual Sprint, Team Sprint and Keirin while in China.

In a statement sent to Daily Mail Sport, a British Cycling spokesman said: 'British Cycling can confirm that Matt Richardson has been withdrawn from the Great Britain Cycling Team squad for the upcoming 2026 Tissot UCI Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai, China.'

Richardson has been described as having a 'God complex' and being 'arrogant'

Richardson's partner is fellow British cyclist Emma Finucane, who welcomed her parents out in China amid the storm engulfing her boyfriend

When approached by Daily Mail Sport about the misconduct allegations which are believed to have prompted Richardson's withdrawal, the organisation added that they would not be commenting further at this stage.

Richardson and Finucane live together in Manchester and have been dating since February 2024 after 'knowing each other for a long time'.

Richardson had been due to be one of four members of the men's sprint squad at the World Championships.

He had been due to join Harry Ledingham-Horn, Ed Lowe and Joe Truman in the squad.

Richardson had claimed three medals at the European Championships in Konya, Turkey, earlier this year.

The 27-year-old won gold in both the men's sprint and keirin events, as well as claiming silver in the team sprint with Truman and Hamish Turnbull.

Richardson had been due to make his comeback after he was injured during the Keirin World Series in July.

Richardson is pictured with Finucane - the couple live together in Manchester

Last week, Richardson said he is 'lucky' to be walking after being wiped out by a rival in an incident, which ruled him out of the Commonwealth Games three months ago.

Richardson had been slammed off the track by Japanese cyclist Kento Suzuki while competing in the event in July, leaving the velodrome in an ambulance.

The sprinter said he has not received an apology from Suzuki over the incident.

He was favourite to win gold in Glasgow but never got to take part after the horrifying crash. He was unable to walk for four days after coming away with a broken scapula and a heavily bruised hip.

Richardson had been hoping to defend the title he won when competing for Australia in 2022, before he switched nationality to represent Britain, which he claimed was like 'Hogwarts' compared to 'High School'.

The defector, who was born in the English town of Maidstone but moved to Perth at nine and went on to carve out a brilliant track career for Australia, caused a sensation by switching allegiance straight after winning two silvers and a bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics. He received a life ban from competing for Australia.

Sports.title: Thin-skinned Lisandro Martinez has exposed the insidious, destructive lack of accountability that's threatening to rip apart the Man United dressing room: IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Thin-skinned Lisandro Martinez has exposed the insidious, destructive lack of accountability that's threatening to rip apart the Man United dressing room: IAN LADYMAN

Ian Ladyman Football Editor

Lisandro Martinez had one job to do in the 92nd minute of Manchester United’s game against Tottenham at the weekend. Had he done it, United would have won a big Premier League game and, despite their uncertain start to the season, would currently sit only two points outside the Champions League places.

Had he done it, United would have travelled to Madrid for a tough European game yesterday in better spirits and with more confidence and with less noise around them.

Had he done it, he may not have looked quite so ridiculous as he stood before the TV cameras blaming everybody else apart from himself for the defeat that inevitably came against Atletico Madrid.

But Martinez didn’t do that. He didn’t even get close to doing it. As the ball travelled across the United penalty area on Saturday evening, Martinez failed to do his job. He failed to even get off the ground as he tried to compete with Dominic Solanke for the ball.

Instead, he grabbed on to his opponent’s shirt and hoped. At one stage he actually had his back to the ball. That’s what modern defenders do when they are desperate, when they lack the wherewithal or confidence to take real control. And, perhaps inevitably, Solanke headed the ball into the net and United’s three points became one.

It felt like a poor piece of defending at the time and it certainly feels like one now. But for Martinez and perhaps others in that United dressing room, the blame clearly doesn’t belong to them. It always belongs to other people. And when a dressing room becomes infected with a culture like that then the end is never good.

Lisandro Martinez (left) launched into an explosive rant against Jason Wilcox (right) after Manchester United's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid

As far as moral high grounds go, Martinez does not have much of a leg to stand on after his error at the weekend allowing Dominic Solanke to score Tottenham's equaliser at Old Trafford

All football clubs need accountability at all levels if they are to thrive. In the boardroom, the manager’s office and the dressing room.

At Old Trafford, too many people are happy to put their hand up when things are good but not when they are bad. That’s a culture as insidious and destructive as cancer. It may move slowly at times and it may temporarily be masked by a run of decent results, but it will get you in the end.

This week I listened to Michael Carrick – United’s honourable but under-performing manager – talk on TV about suggestions that his team haven’t been running enough. Carrick said that stats can be misleading. He is right about that.

But I was at Old Trafford on Saturday and didn’t need any help from the good people at Opta to tell me that Carrick’s players were failing him on that metric. I could see it with my own eyes.

I have watched enough football to recognise a bunch of players going through the motions. I know cheating when I see it and so do the people who pay to come and watch their team every weekend. It was because of this that United were booed off at half-time against Tottenham and indeed at the end.

Martinez is a thin-skinned individual. He was so upset at criticism from Paul Scholes last season that a meeting between the two was mooted. Scholes’ phone never rang.

Nevertheless he is right when he talks about issues with United’s recruitment. It hasn’t been good enough. Last season I watched an in-house United video that featured director of football Jason Wilcox telling the world how to get a transfer right. Do I really have to spell out the punchline to that one?

But it is not Martinez’s place to fire his bullets upwards in Wilcox’s direction, not when so many in red are failing at the basics every weekend.

All it does is provide his manager with endless fresh questions to answer and open the door to the attitude of a United dressing room that is clearly lacking a few mirrors.

United have to play at Leeds United on Sunday. It was always a big game but now it feels bigger. Now it has an extra layer. Will Martinez play? How will he play? What will he say? What will his manager and team-mates say? We can already imagine the live TV cameras cutting to Wilcox in the directors’ box at Elland Road as the second Leeds goal goes in.

It wasn't Wilcox who put through his own net at Craven Cottage, as Martinez did last month in the draw at Fulham

Martinez is a thin-skinned individual. He was so upset at criticism from Paul Scholes last season that a meeting between the two was mooted. Scholes’ phone never rang

And all of that comes back to the Argentinian who, despite his status as an experienced international, gets a pass mark at best from his four years at the club and who has been front and centre during a time when a succession of managers – from Erik ten Hag to Ruben Amorim and now Carrick – have been failed by their players.

This is not a great United squad. It lacks depth and authority in key positions. But it’s good enough to sit in the top six of the Premier League. It’s good enough to beat a team like Tottenham. But it will never go where it needs to unless everybody in the building understands their own responsibilities.

Wilcox may or may not end up being the real deal at Old Trafford. He has already made some mistakes. But he won a Premier League as a player. He played on the wing for Blackburn and indeed Leeds at a time when pitches were average and protection from full backs was scant.

So the 55-year-old knows what the game is. He knows how it should feel and smell. Wilcox also knows what running felt like. He knows what a good dressing room felt like. So he will know – like the rest of us – that Martinez’s comments point to a desperate and destructive malaise within.

Sports.title: Eight Premier League clubs saw stars withdraw from international duty... here's who the big winners were from the break
Sports.content:
Pulling on your nation's shirt should be one of the proudest moments of a footballer's life, but a growing number are deciding against it.

This malaise was made particularly clear in the most recent international break which, for the first time, was extended to three weeks. Thirteen first-team players across eight different English top-flight clubs opted out of playing for their country having been called up – some citing fatigue, some with more serious injuries.

Daily Mail Sport looks at which clubs benefited the most from their stars having some extra time off...

Arsenal

After the events of the last three weeks, Mikel Arteta will be dreading the next international break as Arsenal saw six of their first-team players pick up injuries away with their nations.

Declan Rice, whose tired legs could not quite carry England to the World Cup final this summer, withdrew from Thomas Tuchel's most recent camp as he continues to feel the effects of last season's gruelling campaign. That rest has reaped its rewards for Arteta, with the midfielder able to play the full 90 minutes in the Gunners' gritty win over Leeds.

Rice (right) provided a wonderfully deft assist for new Bruno Guimaraes (left) after some rare time off

The Gunners are searching for back-to-back Premier League titles for the first time in their history and preserving their best players – while controversial among England fans – will no doubt prove astute when the marathon campaign reaches its conclusion.

Chelsea

Another team that benefited from their players withdrawing from international duty this weekend were Arsenal's London rivals Chelsea.

The Blues went into the international break with worrying form after picking up just one point from the possible nine available against Arsenal, Hull and Brentford and Xabi Alonso's squad looked in dire need of some time off.

And two of Chelsea's biggest stars ensured they did not waste this opportunity for recovery. Cole Palmer, who was left out of England's 2026 World Cup squad, chose not to join England for the first of their Nations League games and get back to full fitness instead. What it means for his future under Thomas Tuchel remains to be seen but the time off clearly did the trick domestically for Chelsea's No 10, who started and contributed an assist during Chelsea's 5-1 drubbing of Bournemouth.

Another star performer on Saturday for the Blues was Joao Pedro, who netted two goals on his return. The Brazilian sustained a minor knee injury just before the international break commenced and it may have been a blessing in disguise.

Pedro, just like Palmer, was bizarrely left out of Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad and was severely missed by the Selecao, who suffered an early exit. Carlo Ancelotti seems to have come to his senses since and wanted Pedro in his latest squad, but the striker did not travel and as a result is back fully fit and firing.

Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer were both denied a place at the World Cup but have now turned down call ups to stay fit and perform for Chelsea

Crystal Palace

The Eagles saw one first team star fail to turn out for their country after being called upon, but there can be no doubting the legitimacy of this withdrawal.

With 46 caps to his name, Takehiro Tomiyasu is an integral figure in Japan's national team but was forced to pull out after sustaining a calf injury during Palace's 0-0 draw away to Leeds before the break.

Even with three weeks on the sidelines, the defender was not deemed fit enough to play a role in Palace's first home win of the season – a 3-1 triumph over Nottingham Forest on Sunday – and Japan fans will not feel aggrieved by his absence.

Manchester City

Man City have lost a lot of friends over the international break, so adding a legion of national team managers will hardly give Enzo Maresca cause to lose sleep.

Following the bombshell verdict from the independent panel, that found Manchester City guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges levelled against them, on the pitch issues were hardly the club's primary concern.

But City, just like Chelsea and Arsenal, were able to benefit from one of their players avoiding game time in the international break.

Semenyo failed to score at Anfield but was lively throughout and helped City to a huge victory

Antoine Semenyo, who has become a fixture in City's team since joining from Bournemouth in January of last year, missed out on playing for Ghana due to an ankle issue the winger was careful not to exacerbate.

Semenyo was, however, deemed fit enough to play the full 90 minutes at Anfield on Sunday, although his impact was limited with fellow winger Jeremy Doku stealing the show off the bench in an emphatic 3-0 win over Liverpool.

Manchester United

From the blue side of Manchester to the red. United saw the most players withdraw from international duty before the first game but did not reap the same rewards as their other big six rivals.

Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were part of the five-player contingent that pulled out of the England squad due to reported injury problems, but unlike Rice and Palmer. the England pair did not taste victory after their rest.

Kobbie Mainoo's lack of public reasoning for his withdrawal saw eyebrows raised among fans and pundits, and he has seen his standing in the squad diminish amid the impressive rise of his replacement, Alex Scott.

But despite the three-week rest Mainoo and United looked poor during their 1-1 draw to Tottenham in which the midfielder played all 90 minutes with minimal impact. Rashford was given insufficient time to affect the game, coming on in the 95th minute.

Benjamin Sesko also pulled out of Slovenia duty due to a shin injury he has been dealing with for over a year now and remains unfit after the international break came to an end.

Kobbie Mainoo snubbed Tuchel to focus on United but as of yet his efforts are yet to change the team's fortune

Newcastle

Next up are the Magpies and after a second 4-1 loss of the season, this time to newly promoted Coventry, Matthias Jaissle may be wondering if his three weeks on the training pitch have been wasted.

Newcastle's second-half capitulation points to fatigue in a side that were ransacked of their star talent over the summer.

Amar Dedic and Tino Livramento were the only members of the squad to miss out entirely on their international camps due to injuries both were not ready to start at Coventry. Dedic did make a second-half substitute appearance but failed to turn the tide.

Sunderland

The Mackems only had one player pull out of international duty early but this time an unusual reason.

The veteran midfielder Granit Xhaka has been capped 152 times for his nation and captained them since 2020, but was forced to withdraw from the squad for the first time in his career after being embroiled in a row over a forged Covid vaccine certificate.

Xhaka issued an apology, paid a £180,000 fine and made his return to action in Sunderland's 2-0 defeat by ten-man Brighton.

Tottenham Hotspur

Spurs went into the break rock bottom and the international calendar was hardly forgiving for Roberto De Zerbi with the majority of his squad representing their nation over the break.

Mohammed Kudus looked bright after returning from injury in Spurs' first positive day of the season

Spurs are enduring their worst start to a season in Premier League and remain winless after six games.

But their latest draw away to United was one that, in isolation, is a good result. Especially considering that while only one of their players withdrew from international duty, Tottenham's squad played more minutes than any other Premier League club over the extended international break.

Mohamed Kudus of Ghana was the player involved for Spurs who withdrew from international duty before the first game and only managed 66 minutes at Old Trafford but looked lively in the first half and on another day could've netted the opener from an early chance he had squandered.

Pedro Porro was the other member of Roberto De Zerbi's squad that stayed at home but even still could not regain match fitness to play on the weekend.

Sports.title: Noni Madueke has the tools and ability but after another frustrating night for Arsenal, the England star MUST step up or see his side suffer, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
By the hour mark, Mikel Arteta had seen enough. Another Noni Madueke dart forward resulting in a goal kick prompted his boss to swiftly turn away in quiet frustration, motioning for Bukayo Saka to get ready to come on.

You see, there is some player in Madueke. The sharp twists and turns, the watertight dribbling all point to a forward with spades of talent in his boots.

Such ability is why Arsenal splashed out £52million on the ex-Chelsea man amid protests from fans over his signature; #NoToMadueke had even harshly trended on X at one point.

Yet it’s his end product which continually stops him from reaching that next level. A decent player who can be very good on his day is a different prospect to a game-changer — which Madueke has the tools to become.

It’s why he can be such a frustrating watch, because of the level he is capable of reaching. His dainty run down the right wing and cut back on 18 minutes rose applause, followed by an awful cross which evaded everyone.

A few of his other crosses in the first half met the same fate: overcooked and lacking accuracy. A glance to the touchline showed Arteta doing his best to mask annoyance at the profligacy.

Noni Madueke has plenty of tools at his disposal but too many times, good build-up fails to end in a goal

He ceased hiding this upon pivoting to Saka, calling him to cut his warm-up short.

When asked about Madueke’s lack of end product, Arteta replied: ‘I said when you talk about players being clinical. And what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score five.

‘So, yeah, it's about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches. He had a really big contribution a few days ago. Today he had a contribution in the last final pass as well. And that's it. We need to get the players to that level, to be decisive in every game if possible.’

In general, though, Madueke caused the Lille midfield and backline problems. There were neat first touches, plucking the ball gently from the air. His rapid acceleration from a standing point is hard to keep up with.

Then there is Madueke’s dribbling, which defenders found tricky to thwart. The ball stays tight within the forward’s grasp, allowing him to motor forward at speed.

So, the tools are there. Utilising them properly is another matter.

With Max Dowman waiting in the wings — he made a short cameo after 85 minutes — Madueke will be watching over his shoulder. He can ill afford not to step up, otherwise his place could well be taken in the coming months.

Even Lionel Messi has recognised the talent of Dowman, recently naming the 16-year-old in his top 10 talents for the future.

It’s the rest for Saka which is the more pressing matter, though. The winger’s introduction created a goal for Eberechi Eze, and he scored one himself, too.

Keeping Bukayo Saka rested is imperative for Arsenal's success but Madueke does not always prove a solid and dependable replacement

The game swiftly turned in Arsenal’s favour after a first half full of frustration and wastefulness, marked by Saka’s introduction, alongside Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard.

Still, if Madueke had properly impacted the game, Saka could have been afforded a night off or a short introduction at the end.

Instead the England man was urgently required to guide the game towards three points.

His workload from the previous two seasons has been well documented, paired with a series of injuries which have hampered this team for Saka is an integral part.

The answer to Saka getting sufficient rest lies at the feet of Madueke.

He has the ability. It’s high time he translates it to end product or face the bench.

Slumbering European giants

The regularity of Arsenal’s wins in recent seasons have masked a mightily impressive run in the Champions League.

The north London club are now unbeaten in their last 17 home games in the group stage/league phase of the competition, stretching back to 2015.

It equates to 16 wins, keeping 14 clean sheets along the way. After enduring heartbreak in last season’s Budapest final, the Gunners are well-equipped to go all the way this time around.

Their home form certainly says so.

Although the Gunners fell short at the final hurdle last season, their formidable home record in Europe stands firm

Arsenal's next crop of teen talents

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Tuesday morning, 18-year-old pair Ceadach O'Neill and Maalik Hashi made the Arsenal squad. With Christos Tzolis injured, O'Neill could get further chances.

The Northern Ireland teenager made his competitive debut for the nation over the international break amid efforts from Republic of Ireland to try lure him to switch allegiance. He’s one to watch and will be eyeing a spot amid Madueke’s indifferent displays.

It follows the likes of Dowman and Marli Salmon having come through the Hale End academy and establishing themselves in the first-team set-up.

It’s a testament to an academy whose conveyer belt keeps churning out young gems.

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Man City are poisoning the Premier League - how can Sky Sports and TNT possibly keep broadcasting their matches?
Sports.content:
When the result of a sporting contest does not matter, when it is diminished by doubts about the legitimacy of the struggle, when it is undermined by suspicions that the result may soon be declared null and void, when a spectator starts to wonder whether what they are watching is real, then what is the point of watching at all?

It felt like that, watching from the stands at Anfield late on Sunday afternoon. Yes, Manchester City were absolutely majestic in the second half, and yes, they exposed Liverpool’s shortcomings. But so what? In a few months, it may not matter. City may have been relegated by then. Or they may have been docked 30 points. Or their appeal may have succeeded.

The point is that for now, when City play, nobody knows what they are watching. And as football still comes to terms with the findings of an independent commission that decided City are the biggest cheats in English sporting history, there is certainly very little public appetite to watch their players gloating in victory as if they were somehow the wronged parties.

It is a question that is exercising Sky Sports and TNT Sports, as the primary broadcasters of the Premier League in the UK.

I’m sure that Liverpool-City garnered excellent viewing figures for Sky. It had novelty value. It was the first sighting of City since the judgments against them. And they were playing Liverpool, one of those who suffered most from City’s chicanery.

But what now? What next? Is it really commercially viable for the leading broadcasters to keep picking City games for their primetime slots on Saturdays and Sundays and Monday Night Football? It is more likely, surely, that City will become kryptonite for viewing figures in this country.

When City play, nobody knows what they are watching. And as football still comes to terms with the independent commission's verdict, there is little public appetite to watch them gloat

Yes, Manchester City were absolutely majestic in the second half at Anfield on Sunday, and yes, they exposed Liverpool’s shortcomings. But so what?

City were once the standard-bearers for the Premier League, a team that played enchanting football, a team guided by a genius manager in Pep Guardiola, a team that had Kevin De Bruyne, David Silva and Erling Haaland, three of the greatest players to have graced our top flight.

But that has changed radically. Haaland is still there, of course, but when broadcasters televise City now, they are showcasing a team that has become a symbol of everything that has gone wrong with the English game.

They are giving more oxygen to a club whose owners have poisoned the product that is Sky’s lifeblood. And so, the more prominence they give to City in the months ahead, the more they poison themselves.

Why would a broadcaster want to do that? Why would a broadcaster want to draw more and more attention to the poison eating away at its most popular product? It doesn’t make any sense. It would represent a form of self-sabotage.

That is why it was hard to disagree with Gary Neville, one of Sky’s headline analysts, when he said after the Anfield game on Sunday that he would prefer not to be involved with City matches for the next few months.

‘I don’t get to volunteer for what games I do,’ Neville said, as he discussed the issue with Jamie Carragher. ‘We get told what games to do. We get a list sent through. I'd prefer not to do Manchester City games for the next two or three months, being honest with you, and that has never been the case for the last 10 or 12 years.

‘I have always admired them enormously. I think of Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva and it was a joy to watch them and now Haaland is world-class. We should be fawning over Manchester City after the way they played against Liverpool. To come and win at Anfield is really difficult and we should be eulogising over them without a "but" or any hesitation.

'But there is that thing in the back of your mind. At the end of the game, it’s quite hard because you’re imagining that if these guilty verdicts are confirmed, Manchester City are not going to be in the position they’re in and there’s going to be a huge cloud hanging over the whole league.’

Neville is absolutely right. Too many people still want to pretend that there is nothing to see here. Too many people want to pretend it is just business as usual. But it is not business as usual.

Gary Neville is absolutely right. Too many people still want to pretend that there is nothing to see here with City

Sky, to their credit, have debated City’s guilty verdicts openly and robustly in studio discussions. Roy Keane, in particular, has spoken of the debilitating effect the verdicts have had on the league and questioned how City’s players must feel, knowing that the club has cheated its way to a clutch of titles.

Others, like Micah Richards, have defended City and urged some restraint until their appeal has been heard. The damage to the product is such that broadcasters must be tempted to ask for a revision to their contract. City, one of their greatest assets, have suddenly become their achilles’ heel.

City’s game against PSG in the Champions League group phase on Wednesday evening still feels like a box-office match. But after that, most viewers would surely rather not be reminded that City’s punishment, whatever form it takes, threatens to turn this into a sham season.

City are due to play Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on the last Sunday in November. That game, just as Sunday’s did, will retain its fascination. Its significance will survive the poisoning of the Premier League. Until then, Sky may decide that City matches have lost their allure.

Sports.title: England Rugby World Cup hero looks unrecognisable after incredible switch to bodybuilding - can you guess who he is?
Sports.content:
A former England World Cup-winning rugby star has shown off his incredible body transformation after taking up bodybuilding.

The star, now 50, was part of England's legendary squad that won the tournament under Sir Clive Woodward in 2003, featuring in all seven games of their campaign.

The 50-year-old was forced to retire through injury in 2010 and has been involved in a variety of ventures since then, including coaching, media, activism about player welfare, and now a new sport.

Taking to social media, the star revealed he took part in a bodybuilding competition in Hull and shared pictures of his physique.

He explained that the hard work required, along with the camaraderie of competing with others, had been extremely positive for his mental health.

But, can you guess who it is?

An England World Cup winner has showed off his astonishing body transformation

The star in question is former England prop Phil Vickery.

After sharing a photo of his ripped physique on Instagram, Vickery said: 'So team it’s been just over a week and I have recovered enough now to show a couple of pictures of my body building competition I took part in for the Physical Culture Association in Hull.

'I get asked all the time why, what for, what’s the point of it, how much money do you get if you win, and on and on.

'First and foremost the gym and lifting weights has helped me physically but mentally more than anything. I love the discipline, the challenge, the atmosphere, the camaraderie and the simple fact it’s f***ing hard work and you can’t fake your way onto stage and you can’t hide behind anyone or anything.

'Your physique is the reflection of your work. It’s not about anyone else for me it’s just you being the best version of you and being better than last time.'

After the inspiring words, Vickery shared heartfelt thanks to his coach Dave Campbell who he described as a 'friend' and 'mentor', adding he 'will always be grateful for those little big things'.

Vickery was showered in compliments in the replies to his post, including one from Campbell.

He wrote: 'It was my pleasure to see your journey from where you were to how good you looked, considering the injuries and setbacks we had to overcome. All in all, you did incredible. Well done mate.'

His former England team-mate Matt Dawson added: 'Bl***y hell mate. No wonder that was so tough. Fair play you colossus…'

England's official account also posted a supportive comment as they said: 'Fancy a game?'

Vickery pictured after the crowning moment of his career with England 23 years ago

Join the discussion Are you impressed by Phil Vickery's remarkable transformation from World Cup-winning rugby star to competitive bodybuilder?

Vickery's achievement was all the more inspiring given the personal struggles he has faced since retirement.

In August, Vickery revealed he has issues with his memory after being diagnosed with 'probable' chronic traumatic encephalopathy, a brain disease that is usually caused by repeated head impacts.

'The sport’s f***ing amazing,' he told The Observer: 'Rugby’s an amazing sport. You know, the sad reality is I sit here today: would I do it all again? Oh my God, I would. I’m f***ing mental, but I would because it’s amazing.

'I also sit here knowing there are lots of people out there, I believe, who are suffering because of the sport. And it’s not about blaming the sport and about getting all nasty and horrible.

'Let’s just f***ing help people. There are people suffering, so let’s help them.'

Sports.title: New Lisandro Martinez footage with Cristian Romero emerges before Man Utd outburst
Sports.content:
New Lisandro Martinez footage with Cristian Romero emerges before Man Utd outburst

Lisandro Martinez didn't hold back in his explosive post-match interview following Man United's 2-0 defeat vs Atletico Madrid

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez appeared to be involved in a heated exchange with international teammate Cristian Romero following Man United's defeat vs Atletico Madrid. (Image: @GermanCarrara/X)

New footage appears to show Man United's Lisandro Martinez being wound up by his Argentina teammates just minutes before his outburst against the club's hierarchy. The defender criticised the summer transfer window following the 2-0 Champions League defeat against Atletico Madrid.

‌



‌



Pablo Barrios opened the scoring for the Spanish side inside the first minute, in the worst possible start for Michael Carrick's team. Leny Yoro was then shown a straight red card in the second half before Ademola Lookman doubled Atletico's lead in the 79th minute.

‌



Following the defeat, Martinez couldn't help but show his frustration. He picked out technical director Jason Wilcox for criticism, highlighting the need for more transfers in the summer window.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I expected more from our technical director," he said. "I have to be honest, you know? And also, as players, we have to do more, but it's also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for these kinds of nights."

When pressed on which positions he believed required reinforcement, he added: "In general. I think last season we did everything; we created a base to build an amazing team. But this is something to be honest and to prove something, you know?

‌



"Yeah, it's annoying, disappointing, to come here and not see my team trying to get an amazing result here. It's disappointing."

View 2 Images Manchester United fell to a 2-0 defeat vs Atletico Madrid. (Image: Denis Doyle, Getty Images)

Prior to the interview, footage from the pitch at the final whistle shows Martinez looking visibly frustrated during an exchange with international colleagues Cristian Romero and Julian Alvarez. The beginning of the clip circulating on social media appears to capture Martinez seemingly confronting Alvarez in anger.

‌



Romero then seems to intervene as peacemaker. A brief tense exchange unfolds between the pair, before a swift handshake as they go their separate ways, with Romero grinning as he departs.

Supporters on social media determined that the incident was the 'catalyst' for the media tirade. Romero himself has been no stranger to publicly challenging a club's leadership.

‌



Back in January, during his spell at Tottenham, he lashed out on social media about individuals 'only showing up when things are going well'. Having shared the summer with the former Spurs defender at the World Cup while representing Argentina, Martinez may well have drawn inspiration to voice his opinions from his international colleague.

United's response as a club to the remarks remains unclear, with Carrick's team returning to action on Sunday afternoon when they face Leeds United away in the Premier League (2pm kick-off).

Offering his instant reaction on Tuesday evening , The United boss said: "I haven't seen the interview; I've heard about it as the interview was done, but I think it's a little bit on the emotions of the game as well.

Article continues below

"Coming here and being disappointed not to get something from the game. Straight after a game for me isn't the time to talk about that interview because I haven't seen it, so I can't really comment on that.

"But I think it's important for us to move forward quickly, really. There is a big game on Sunday, and it's really important that we move forward and we stay focused on that. There's disappointment within the group. I'm very disappointed in certain things, and the boys are as well."

Sports.title: Should Man Utd punish Lisandro Martinez for comments on owners? Have your say
Sports.content:
Should Man Utd punish Lisandro Martinez for comments on owners? Have your say

Lisandro Martinez strongly criticised the higher-ups at Manchester United in the wake of Tuesday's 2-0 loss away to Atletico Madrid, leaving fans and pundits divided

View Image Lisandro Martinez was outspoken after the defeat (Image: Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Lisandro Martinez has stolen the headlines after Manchester United lost 2-0 away to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. His explosive post-match interview saw him criticise the club's board and call out director of football Jason Wilcox.

‌



‌



Martinez, 28, said that he 'expected more' from United in the summer transfer window, as the Red Devils only made four signings - three of them in midfield and one backup goalkeeper. Their recruitment has forced Michael Carrick to put square pegs in round holes just weeks into his first season as United's permanent manager.

‌



Speaking after the game in Madrid, he said: “Really poor. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.

‌



"We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today.

"I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

Article continues below

Fans have hailed Martinez for speaking out, with a large portion of supporters holding the same opinion. But the Argentina international has also been accused of 'disrespecting' his team-mates by ex-United captain Wayne Rooney, while Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher says that he was 'out of order'.

But what do you make of his comments? Give us your thoughts in the poll below.

Sports.title: Geri Halliwell's reaction to Christian Horner texting scandal revealed in new book
Sports.content:
Geri Halliwell's reaction to Christian Horner texting scandal revealed in new book

Christian Horner has opened up about how wife Geri Halliwell stood by him during the texting scandal that rocked their lives

View 2 Images Christian Horner with wife Geri Halliwell (Image: James Bearne/Getty Images)

Christian Horner has disclosed how his wife Geri Halliwell reacted after the former Red Bull boss discovered he had been accused of inappropriate behaviour towards a female colleague. An investigation into his conduct commenced in February 2024 and he was exonerated following an internal probe, though alleged messages between the two parties were leaked shortly after the ruling.

‌



‌



An appeal against the decision was rejected that August. Horner, who steadfastly denied the accusations, served as Red Bull team principal and CEO for 25 years, steering the team to six constructors' championships and eight driver world titles before being relieved of his duties in July 2025.

‌



Outside the F1 paddock, the 52-year-old has been married to former Spice Girl Geri since 2015 and he has revealed how his wife opted to support him throughout the messaging scandal that shook their personal lives.

‌



In his new book Drive, Horner described his initial response when first learning of the allegations made against him during a phone call with a lawyer: "'This can't be right,' I said, eventually, wanting to ask more questions but not knowing where to begin. What was going on? The lawyer, presumably aware that a wrecking ball was being aimed at my life, explained the situation as my sense of bewilderment rose."

Shortly after the conversation, Horner relayed the situation to Geri, with whom he shares a son and two other children from their previous relationships. "In the kitchen, Geri was getting the family ready for school," he wrote. "When everyone had been packed off for the day, I walked downstairs and broke the news.

Christian Horner's huge net worth now with wife Geri Halliwell after giant Red Bull payout READ MORE :

F1 news: Lewis Hamilton taken for medical checks as Sky Sports issue apology READ MORE :

"Geri knew by my face that something was very wrong. 'What's up?' She frowned as I repeated what the lawyer had said. She fell silent as she listened. We both understood the implications immediately. She looked at me. 'Just tell your truth,' she said. 'That's all I can do,' I replied."

‌



Following a visit to the Red Bull factory, Horner returned home visibly troubled, unable to conceal his anxieties from his wife. He praised the former Spice Girl's extraordinary composure as their private lives faced mounting public scrutiny.

"When I returned home and told Geri about my concerns, she reassured me that everything would be all right," he continued. "Her resilience was remarkable. Our lives had been turned upside down, yet she found the strength and conviction to support me through an immensely difficult period, one that was undoubtedly challenging for her as well.

View 2 Images Geri publicly supported her husband during the 2024 Bahrain GP (Image: Sam Bloxham/LAT Images via Getty Images)

‌



"Her belief in me gave me the determination to move forward. At a time when my confidence was being tested, Geri provided the perspective and stability that I needed most. Without her support, I'm not sure I could have navigated those months in the same way. 'Well, the higher you rise, the sharper the knives,' said Geri. Her logic was hard to argue against."

The 54-year-old made her position crystal clear by publicly standing by her husband in March 2024. Just days after leaked messages emerged, depicting alleged text message exchanges, voice messages and conversations between Horner and a female Red Bull employee, Geri showed her unwavering support during the Bahrain Grand Prix.

Looking back on the episode, Horner wrote: "I didn't comment on any of this speculation. Geri was on her way to Bahrain. After she arrived, we walked hand in hand into the paddock on race day as a media scrum jostled around us."

Article continues below

Christian Horner's book Drive is out on Thursday, October 22.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold agreement reached by Liverpool legends - 'We've missed him'
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold agreement reached by Liverpool legends - 'We've missed him'

Trent Alexander-Arnold decided to leave Liverpool for Real Madrid in 2025

View 2 Images Liverpool icons have given their thoughts on Trent Alexander-Arnold's decision to leave for Real Madrid (Image: Florencia Tan Jun - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Trent Alexander-Arnold is still striving to become a star player at Real Madrid but several Liverpool legends say the club have have keenly felt his absence. The right-back decided to leave his boyhood side for Los Blancos in 2025 as he embarked on a new chapter with the Spanish giants.

‌



‌



Alexander-Arnold helped redefine what can be expected of a full-back, with his impeccable passing making him a game-changer from a deeper position. He was integral to Jurgen Klopp’s side as the Reds won the Champions League in 2019 and ended Liverpool’s 30-year wait for a league title in 2020. In his final year at Anfield, the defender signed off by once again lifting the Premier League trophy.

‌



The 28-year-old’s decision to leave for Real Madrid sparked frustration from a section of Liverpool supporters. The England international was widely expected to flourish for the Spanish giants but Alexander-Arnold struggled to find momentum as he battled injuries.

‌



He is yet to become indispensable to Jose Mourinho, who is preparing to face his former club Roma in the Champions League after a mixed start in La Liga, with the full-back starting four of nine games. While Liverpool are focused on facing LASK on Wednesday, three club icons have previously admitted that losing Alexander-Arnold was a huge blow.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Jamie Carragher

Jamie Carragher previously argued that Florian Wirtz arrived from Bayer Leverkusen for a huge fee in 2025 to replace Alexander-Arnold’s creativity. Despite playing in different positions, the legendary Liverpool defender argued that Wirtz was signed to have the same impact on the team but had so far failed to replicate Alexander-Arnold’s success.

‌



“It sounds odd to say it, but Wirtz was signed to replace Trent Alexander-Arnold – a No 10 to provide the passing range and creativity of a unique full-back,” Carragher wrote for The Telegraph in October 2025. “He is yet to add what Liverpool are missing without Alexander-Arnold, while at the same time the team has lost the intensity which made them so difficult to play against.”

Carragher remains unconvinced that Wirtz will ultimately deliver on his £116million price tag. The 48-year-old argued that the Germany international deserves to be dropped following Liverpool’s recent defeat to Manchester City.

View 2 Images Andy Robertson admitted the impact that losing Trent Alexander-Arnold had on Liverpool (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Andy Robertson

Andy Robertson thrived on the opposite flank to Alexander-Arnold throughout most of his time at Anfield. The left-back remained with Liverpool for a year after Alexander-Arnold’s exit and conceded that the Reds had been impacted by his move to Madrid, but commended his former teammate for stepping into the unknown.

“I think obviously we’ve missed him as a player, there’s no doubt about that. We’ve missed him as a character as well,” Robertson said on The Overlap in May. “But he’s went on to try something new and sometimes you just have to take your hat off to that.”

‌



Steven Gerrard

As a fellow Liverpool academy graduate, Steven Gerrard admitted that it was difficult to see Alexander-Arnold join another club. The former Reds captain outlined the challenge of replacing the right-back, despite signing Jeremie Frimpong in 2025 and having Conor Bradley in their ranks, and shared his hope for an emotional return to Anfield.

“I wished and hoped that Trent didn’t leave us,” Gerrard told BFM Radio in May. “Certainly, you understand and respect that every player has got their own career and can make their own decisions.

Article continues below

“But it’s very difficult to replace a player at Trent’s level because he’s world-class. Hopefully, hopefully, he might return one day.”

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez savages Man Utd owners and says club weren't ready for Champions League
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez savages Man Utd owners and says club weren't ready for Champions League

Manchester United slipped to their fourth defeat of the season against Atletico Madrid with defender Lisandro Martinez issuing a withering assessment of the goings on at Old Trafford

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez speaks after Man Utd's loss at Atletico Madrid

Lisandro Martinez tore into Manchester United's hierarchy in the aftermath of their defeat to Atletico Madrid.

‌



‌



The Red Devils slipped to their fourth defeat of the campaign in Spain on Tuesday night. They had a woeful start with Pablo Barrios giving Atletico the lead within the opening minute.

‌



Ademola Lookman doubled the lead shortly after Leny Yoro's red card. The defeat leaves United with just two wins in all competitions this season.

‌



But Martinez has suggested that the fault is not with the players and instead took aim at those running the club.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Speaking to Amazon Prime Video, he said: “Really poor. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.

"We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today.

"I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

‌



View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez was furious after Man United's defeat against Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Asked which areas could have been strengthened, the Argentine defender said: "In general. Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.

"It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here."

‌



Asked if any of the fault could be with boss Michael Carrick: "I don't think so. He does his best. Every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season. The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don't change next season is a big problem.

"You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas? I can't say more. Tonight it is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

United spent around £150m strengthening their side in the summer ahead of Carrick's first full season at the helm, albeit all of their investment came in midfield. Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos were signed from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively, while Carlos Baleba completed a big-money move from Brighton.

‌



View 3 Images Jason Wilcox was the target of Martinez's furious rant (Image: Getty Images)

Tielemans was asked about Martinez's comments after the full-time whistle but simply replied: “I’ve got no comment on that.”

United boss Carrick was also probed about Martinez's comments. He said:"I haven't seen it. After a game like this you come here to try and get something from the game and you are disappointed and can be emotional. I have not seen it so I don't think it is the right time to comment.

‌



"We all care and show that in different ways but now is the time to be together and work through."

United icon Wayne Rooney also spoke out on Martinez's comments and criticised the former Ajax man for his rant, particularly with United in such a difficult spot. He said: "It's disrespectful to his team-mates, he's saying his team-mates aren't good enough.

"I think Bruno is the only one who has the right to say this. That interview is not going to help the situation the club are in at the minute."

Sports.title: Luis Enrique delivers clear Man City punishment wish ahead of Champions League clash
Sports.content:
Luis Enrique delivers clear Man City punishment wish ahead of Champions League clash

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules during 2009 and 2018

View 2 Images Luis Enrique has spoken out about Man City's financial charges case (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique hopes Manchester City can avoid punishment for breaking rules, insisting that the club deserve credit for their trophy-winning success in recent years. City remain at the centre of an unprecedented financial charges case after being found guilty by an independent commission of 114 Premier League charges.

‌



‌



The Premier League alleged that the club used 'sham' sponsorship deals to inflate their revenues by £900million. However, City continue to deny any wrongdoing, maintaining their innocence and citing 'irrefutable evidence' to support their defence.

‌



An independent commission will oversee the case, with an outcome expected before the end of the year. A key part of City's defence is understood to be that the sponsorship deals were legitimate and funded by the Abu Dhabi government rather than the club's owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG).

‌



Football regulator David Kogan says he will QUIT if Andy Burnham interferes in Man City case READ MORE :

Enzo Maresca's side returned to Premier League action for the first time since the verdict, securing a 3-0 victory over Liverpool on Sunday. As expected, the Cityzens were met with boos and jeers as they stepped onto the pitch at Anfield following the international break.

Their attention has since turned to their Champions League clash against the reigning European champions, PSG. The French champions' boss, Enrique, was quizzed about the ongoing charges against the club.

Enrique and former City boss Guardiola, who played alongside each other at Barcelona, have both established themselves as two of the most successful managers in modern football. Guardiola has won numerous trophies during his time at the Etihad, and Enrique was full of praise for the 'incredible' work done by his compatriot, suggesting he'd like to see City avoid sanctions.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"There is a lot of noise around Manchester City and there is often noise around big clubs," Enrique said.

"We have just have to wait and see what the final decision will be. I hope everything works out well for Manchester City because I think what they have done on the pitch has been incredible over the last few years and they certainly deserved to win on the pitch all the trophies they have won.

‌



"Now we have to wait to see what the authorities decide or the judge is going to say."

View 2 Images Guardiola and Enrique

He added: "The trophies you win on the pitch remain on the pitch. They deserved to win that and I hope they can avoid the sanction.

‌



"But we have to wait. The things I will say to Pep I will do in private."

There have been calls for City to face severe punishment should their appeal fail, including expulsion from the Premier League.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta's massive gamble pays off but struggling Arsenal star fluffs his chance
Sports.content:
This was some turnaround and proof there is no substitute for proven quality.

Arsenal blitzed Lille with a three-goal second half salvo from Jurrien Timber, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka as the Gunners maintained their winning start in the Champions League.

But it needed Mikel Arteta to bring on the big guns to really seal the win after a frustrating hour in which a much-changed line-up struggled before it eventually became very comfortable.

It now sets up Arsenal for their heavyweight clash at Bayern Munich next week but it also showed they are on a mission in Europe this season.

‌



There is a sense of unfinished business in the Champions League for Mikel Arteta after losing last season’s final to Paris Saint Germain.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Arteta almost left his last sentence hanging before the match as he talked about regrets, falling below their usual standards in Budapest last May and trying to go one better this time.

‌



They certainly delivered a statement of intent as they won their first Champions League tie at Napoli and this felt like a big opportunity to keep the momentum going against French club Lille.

But Arteta gambled by changing half of his outfield starting line-up - and, for much of the match, it looked like it was in serious danger of backfiring.

They looked like strangers against what was, quite frankly, a very average looking Lille side as the fresh faces struggled to seize their opportunities.

In came Timber, Bruno Guimaraes, Eze, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres from the team which beat Leeds on Saturday. You might have thought Gyokeres would be chomping at the bit after his frustrating start to the season but he looked miles off it.

‌



View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres failed to deliver on a rare start for Arsenal

They missed chances in a very dull first half and you could sense the frustration beginning to build inside the Emirates.

It took Arsenal 20 minutes to even have a shot. Gyokeres fed Timber and his pull back set up Guimaraes who, despite his goalscoring supersub heroics on Saturday, had mislaid his shooting boots this time and fired wide.

Two minutes later, Timber was at it again as his cross found Merino but his header was straight at Lille keeper Berke Ozer. Merino normally eats up those sort of headed chances.

‌



Merino was having an off night and the frustration got to him as he was booked for a blatant trip on Lille forward Ayase Ueda.

That was the story of Arsenal’s night. They were lacking in rhythm and momentum. Then it all changed with three goals in the space of seven minutes.

The first came after 64 minutes. Madueke’s short pass found Timber who turned neatly and then fired a cross shot into the far corner to break the deadlock.

View 3 Images Eberechi Eze made it two for Arsenal

‌



Suddenly the mood inside the Emirates changed. Arteta also brought on the big guns as Saka came on and his low cross was swept home by Eze who scored his first of the season.

Then it got even better after 71 minutes. Arsenal substitutes Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard combined beautifully to set up Saka whose low shot flew into the far corner to make it 3-0.

When he needed them most, the big guns stepped up from the bench to maintain Arteta’s perfect start to the Champions League campaign.

There was a late cameo for Lille’s former Arsenal striker Olivier Giroud who came on to a mixed reception after his defection to Chelsea.
