Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Could Await Tyson Fury After Joshua
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury could face Agit Kabayel in Germany after Anthony Joshua, according to his manager Spencer Brown. The suggestion depends on Fury winning on December 11, although a crushing defeat might still leave a fun fight for Kabayel’s home supporters.

Managing both fighters gives Brown an easy angle, and he claimed their friendship will not stand in the way of a bout. They will share the ring if required, according to Brown.

“If he beats Anthony Joshua, you know, there’s Agit Kabayel in Germany,” Brown said to the The Ariel Helwani Show. “They’d do the dance if they needed to.

Longtime Wladimir Klitschko supporters would remember Fury taking his titles in Düsseldorf in 2015. Watching Kabayel beat Fury on German soil could feel like settling an old score. If Joshua had already battered him, some might enjoy seeing their current heavyweight star finish the job. That would make for a lively atmosphere, even if Fury arrived with his best years behind him.

Both Fury and Joshua share the exact same problem right now. Their legs are nearly gone, their punch resistance has diminished, and they rely heavily on smoke, mirrors, and holding to stay upright against anyone capable of applying sustained pressure. Kabayel is wrong for both of them. He throws with bad intentions downstairs, refuses to give opponents room to breathe, and punishes excessive clinching by working free hands into the flanks.

The British public loves watching former belt holders test their luck one time too many, and German fans would gladly pay top dollar to see Kabayel dismantle whatever remains of Fury.

The question is, would Fury agree to the fight? A fighter whose entire public persona rests on invincibility does not sign up to become fodder for a younger, hungrier pressure puncher. Even if Turki dangled a massive paycheck in front of him, taking the bout means accepting a scenario where he cannot dictate terms, control the tempo, or hide behind basic veteran survival tactics against Kabayel.

The Makhmudov and Wach performances laid everything bare. The legs were heavy, the reflexes were delayed, and the movement that once bailed him out looked completely gone. Against stationary targets, he managed to scrape by on pure size and roughhouse clinching, but Kabayel represents a completely different proposition.

For Fury, taking a battering from Joshua only to travel into Kabayel’s backyard is a recipe for humiliation

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Faces Race Against Time Against Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley could be racing against time to stop Daniel Dubois in Saturday’s rematch, with his damaged nose threatening to undermine his attempt to reclaim the WBO heavyweight title.

Wardley dropped Dubois twice in the first three rounds of their May fight, proving he has the power to hurt him. He couldn’t finish the job, and Dubois’ sustained attack left him with a badly cut nose and a swollen right eye before the 11th-round stoppage.

That makes another prolonged fight a concern. Paul Smith raised the possibility of Wardley’s nose reopening after seeing him in talkSPORT’s studio this week. Simon Jordan also questioned how well it had healed, predicting an early cut. Neither view establishes what will happen on Saturday, but the first fight showed how damaging Dubois’ punches can be.

Trying to out-jab Dubois looks a difficult route for Wardley. He hasn’t shown the same powerful, ramrod jab, and following Oleksandr Usyk’s approach requires more than putting combinations together.

Usyk’s movement allowed him to step into range, land, and get away before Dubois could respond. Wardley hasn’t demonstrated that same footwork. Throwing combinations while remaining in front of Dubois would give the champion opportunities to answer.

Wardley is intelligent, though, and five months may have given him time to make meaningful changes. He doesn’t need to reproduce everything Usyk does. Moving after punching and changing angles could reduce the punishment and buy him more time to find an opening.

His clearest opportunity remains Dubois’ vulnerability when caught clean. Those two early knockdowns give Wardley a reason to believe he can end the fight before cuts or swelling restrict his vision. Chasing that finish recklessly would also expose him to the punches he needs to avoid.

Smith would accept Wardley walking away afterward.

“I’d have no problem with him if he didn’t want to fight again after this,” he told talkBOXING.

Wardley hasn’t announced retirement plans. His immediate challenge is finding a way to finish Dubois—or showing enough tactical improvement to keep that clock from running out.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Backs Canelo Alvarez Over ‘One-Dimensional’ Mbilli
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora backs Canelo Alvarez’s boxing to beat Christian Mbilli, dismissing the challenger as too one-dimensional. That prediction leaves a bigger question unanswered: whether Canelo can handle the pace without tiring against a younger fighter who keeps coming.

“Canelo has the edge in this one. Mbilli is a good fighter, a strong fighter, but for me, he’s too one-dimensional,” said Fundora to DAZN.

Fundora pointed to Mbilli’s fight with Lester Martinez to explain his doubts, saying he expected a knockout.

“We saw when he fought Lester Martinez; he kind of lost, and I expected him to knock out Lester. But he lost, and Canelo has way more boxing [skills] than that.”

Fundora is committing two classic errors here: analyzing a fighter based on past reputation rather than current reality, and constructing an entire technical case on a false premise.

First, getting the outcome of the Martinez fight wrong completely undercuts his credibility. Mbilli did not lose that fight; it was a grueling split draw where Martinez had to resort to repeated, blatant shoving just to survive the inside pressure and create punching room. Building an argument that Mbilli will fold against Canelo because he “kind of lost” collapses the moment you look at what actually happened in the ring.

Second, Fundora is talking about Canelo as if this were the 2018 or 2021 version who could slip, counter, and control the center of the ring for twelve uninterrupted rounds. That fighter is gone.

At 36, after extensive wear and tear, long stretches of inactivity, and noticeable stamina drops in the second half of fights, Canelo has become an economy puncher. He relies on explosive, low-volume bursts to bank rounds while resting on the ropes.

Mbilli is the absolute worst style for an aging champion trying to conserve energy. Mbilli does not care about taking two clean shots if it allows him to land five to the body and force a phone-booth brawl.

Against a tireless pressure fighter who refuses to let him breathe, Canelo cannot just rely on superior technique. Ring IQ only works if the legs and lungs can carry out the plan for three full minutes of every round. Fundora is picking the name and the highlight reel, completely ignoring the clock and the stylistic nightmare right in front of Canelo.

Sports.title: Team Schofield Attacks Shakur Stevenson’s Power And Reputation
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield Jr. and his father criticized Shakur Stevenson’s punching power, opposition, and reputation, with the elder Schofield arguing that his elite billing comes from his connections to famous fighters rather than the opponents he has beaten.

“He got no power. He’s only elite by association, not by who he fought, because he haven’t fought nobody elite,” said Floyd Schofield during their Fight Hub TV interview. “People put him on the scales. Why? Because Andre Ward managed him. Because Crawford is like his big brother. Because Floyd Mayweather wanted to manage him when he was coming out the Olympics.”

Schofield’s father also called Shakur “a clown,” questioning why the boxing community gives his opinions so much attention.

The criticism followed Stevenson’s comments on X after Schofield’s unanimous decision win over Lucas Bahdi for the vacant WBA lightweight title. Shakur dismissed Schofield as a C-level fighter, something the newly crowned champion clearly hadn’t forgotten during the interview.

“When he tweeted, I was like, he really a fan because he was watching me. I can’t remember the last time I watched a Shakur fight,” said Schofield Jr.

The younger Schofield questioned Shakur’s right to criticize him after sharing the ring with a puncher like Bahdi. His complaint focused on Stevenson’s use of movement when facing dangerous opponents.

“He uses the whole ring like a track field,” said Schofield Jr. “Somebody who fights like that can’t tell me how I fight or how I should fight or what type of fighter I am.”

Schofield acknowledged that he has things to improve, yet remained pleased with his performance and the crowd’s reaction. Later, he endorsed his father’s comments: “You said everything I could say, bro. I agree 100%.”

The father’s strongest argument concerns opposition. Having Ward and Crawford’s approval doesn’t replace beating top fighters. Shakur’s power is a separate question, because a fighter can succeed through timing, accuracy, and defense without producing knockouts.

For all their criticism, the Schofields aren’t pushing to face Stevenson next. His father said their plans have nothing to do with Shakur, while discussing William Zepeda as an easier fight to arrange.

The insults are getting louder, while a fight between them remains outside Team Schofield’s immediate plans.

Sports.title: Vito Mielnicki Targets Major Step Up Against Xander Zayas
Sports.content:
Vito Mielnicki Jr. is asking for a major step up in class against Xander Zayas, calling for the fight on social media and offering to meet the former unified light middleweight champion at Madison Square Garden or in Puerto Rico.

Mielnicki’s win over Austin Williams has put him in position to pursue a bigger fight. Zayas would test whether Vito’s fairly basic style can take him much further against opponents with championship experience.

“Nothing but respect for my guy @xander.zayas, but this is the fight that needs to happen!!” Mielnicki wrote. “The big room at MSG or in Puerto Rico.”

Vito deserves credit for seeking it, especially with Puerto Rico among his proposed locations. He has been matched well and kept mostly out of harm’s way. The Williams victory was a good result, although Austin had already been softened up by defeats against Carlos Adames and Hamzah Sheeraz.

Zayas would bring quicker combinations and a more polished offensive game. This could be as high as Mielnicki goes unless he shows more versatility than he has needed through much of his career.

It’s also a good fight for the Top Rank-promoted Zayas. He has the skills to beat Vito through boxing or trading, with enough firepower to make an offensive approach worth watching.

The concern is whether Xander chooses to use it. His movement and holding against Jorge Garcia Perez and Abass Baraou produced wins without consistently showing how entertaining his offense could be. Taking that same approach against Mielnicki would be a disappointing choice against an opponent he should be able to attack.

Zayas tried boxing Jaron Ennis, found little success, and eventually traded before being stopped. Vito doesn’t present the same threat. Xander should have more opportunities to plant his feet and throw combinations without facing the punishment Ennis delivered.

Eddie Hearn has proposed interim fights for both before a summer meeting. Nothing is signed, but Mielnicki has made his interest clear. If it happens, Vito gets a chance to prove his ceiling is higher than it looks, while Zayas gets an opportunity to win with some excitement.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Accepts Keyshawn Davis Fight, Awaits Contract
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says he agreed to face Keyshawn Davis more than a month ago, contradicting Davis’ claim that he only just agreed to their planned December bout. Hitchins states the paperwork has still not arrived.

Keyshawn has spent the week hyping up his plans for fight night. Hitchins insists nothing is real until promotional teams deliver actual contracts.

“I accepted this fight over a month ago still no contract or anything official I’m still waiting for a contract and time is fucking ticking Keyshawn,” Hitchins posted on X.

That timeline cuts directly into the narrative Davis presented online. Davis made it sound like Hitchins stalled before giving in. Hitchins argues the delay sits entirely with the business side.

“Buddy finally accepted the fight.. this fight in December, this sh*t personal. Africa, I’m on yo ass in December, and I’m gonna beat yo ass,” Davis said.

Trash talk builds interest, but the bout still needs signatures. Hitchins and Davis represent two of the elite talents around the welterweight limit. On pure ring ability, they sit above most rivals, which makes the pairing significant regardless of social media squabbling.

Hitchins controls range behind a stiff jab. He rarely surrenders clean targets. Opponents who charge him blindly spend full rounds eating counters from outside.

Davis brings fast hands, heavy body work, and sharp punch selection. He must apply disciplined pressure. Following Hitchins without cutting off the ring will cost him rounds on the scorecards.

The central tactical issue comes down to style. Keyshawn needs to impose his tempo. Hitchins aims to make opponents second-guess their timing and reset from distance. Both possess the technical sharpness to punish miscalculations.

Before strategy and tactics, promoters must produce the paperwork. Hitchins insists he signed off on the bout weeks ago. With December fast approaching, the matchup remains talk until the contracts land.

Both guys carry themselves like established pound-for-pound attractions, but neither draws genuine ticket sales or pay-per-view numbers on his own. Hitchins has an Olympic pedigree and slick defensive fundamentals, yet his style often alienates casual fans, and his biggest career win is a controversial nod over Gustavo Lemos. Keyshawn Davis has real offensive talent, but he is still largely living off Olympic silver medal hype.

Sports.title: Saudi Boxing Money Has To Come Down
Sports.content:
Spencer Brown sees a noticeable shift coming to Saudi boxing. Tyson Fury’s manager expects the massive purses to shrink, with fewer mega cards happening each year even though the Kingdom plans to stick around. From his perspective, the current spending pace simply cannot hold, creating a whole new reality for fighters across the sport.

“I think that the money has to go down because nobody can keep paying that sort of money,” Brown told The Ariel Helwani Show.

He made sure to dismiss rumors that Saudi investment is drying up completely. Instead, he sees Riyadh scaling back the volume of blockbuster events.

He pointed to Fury’s December 11 meeting with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff, a deal he helped put together, calling it one of the final spectacles of its kind. Moving forward, he predicts fans will see just one or two events of that size annually. While speaking as a dealmaker rather than an official spokesperson for Riyadh Season, his perspective carries genuine weight.

“I think this is one of the last of the big fights we’re going to see. I think you might get one or two big fights a year in future,” Brown said about the Fury vs. Anthony Joshua clash.

The real trouble will be convincing boxers to accept smaller checks again. Once a fighter pockets Saudi riches, traditional offers funded by gate receipts or pay-per-view sales feel like an insult. A matchup can make all the sense in the world on paper, yet stall out completely if someone insists on another monster payday.

That dynamic could trigger prolonged layoffs. Fighters risk sitting around, holding out hope for an invitation to the rare marquee card. Veterans near the end of their careers do not have time to waste on the sidelines, but the temptation of holding out for life-changing money remains strong.

A market cool-down could ultimately force promoters to build fights around realistic budgets again. For that model to succeed, fighters who want to stay active will have to adjust their financial expectations accordingly.

Fighters who grew accustomed to eight-figure guarantees for low-demand, mismatched events are going to hit a wall of stubborn inactivity before reality sets in.

Human nature and boxing economics suggest the immediate reaction won’t be humility. It will be entitlement.

When a boxer makes $10 million to $20 million fighting an unheralded opponent in an atmosphere with minimal gate pressure, that number ceases to be a windfall in their mind. It becomes their baseline. Returning to a traditional promotional model where their guarantee is tied directly to pay-per-view buys and ticket sales in London, New York, or Las Vegas feels like a drastic demotion.

The fallout is likely to split fighters into distinct groups:

First come the holdouts. The biggest names with heavy bank accounts will sit on the sidelines, convinced that their manager or promoter simply isn’t trying hard enough, or that Riyadh will eventually circle back when a headline slot opens.

They will post training clips on social media, call out other stars, demand absurd splits, and reject viable market-rate offers. Some will sit out twelve to eighteen months before grasping that the sovereign wealth subsidy has actually contracted. For aging stars, this wait will quietly run out their athletic primes.

Second comes the rude awakening for mid-tier names. Fighters who received inflated purses simply to fill out stacked undercards will discover that traditional promoters have zero appetite to subsidize them. If a fighter does not shift tickets in their home market or drive subscriptions, domestic promoters cannot afford them at Saudi rates.

These fighters will face a blunt ultimatum: accept pay cuts of 60 to 75 percent, or retire. Those who need money to maintain luxury spending habits will swallow their pride, sign realistic contracts, and return to competitive, grinding fights where they actually have to take risks.

Ultimately, the market correction will be painful. Boxing spent years living in an artificial economy where risk and commercial return were completely divorced. Once the spigot tightens, the fighters who want to stay relevant will have no choice but to get back in the gym and fight each other on realistic budgets, while the ones chasing long-gone purses will simply wait themselves into irrelevance.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Signs With Zuffa Ahead Of WBC Deadline
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames has joined Zuffa Boxing, handing the company another 160-pound titlist along with natural pairings against Aaron McKenna and Denzel Bentley. His immediate task centers on an existing top contender who has been waiting in line.

The WBC champion must handle top-ranked Meiirim Nursultanov. Both camps face an October 20 deadline to strike a deal before purse bids get called. Switching promotional banners does nothing to erase that mandate.

“One of the most avoided men in boxing has just joined the Zuffa Boxing roster!” the promotion posted on X, citing Adames as the reigning titlist and The Ring’s top middleweight.

The official statement omitted any debut date or specific rival, leaving open how rapidly matchmakers plan to get him inside the ring.

This acquisition allows the company to pit its stable against one another. Adames taking on IBF belt holder McKenna offers an obvious starting point, assuming both men navigate their mandatory duties. It would offer McKenna a prime platform to test himself against someone marketed as the best in the weight class.

Bentley has publicly staked his claim as well. Following his agreement to box Shane Mosley Jr. on November 7, he declared that facing McKenna would crown the division leader, openly doubting if Adames or Erislandy Lara truly deserve top billing based on their track records.

Adames landing under the same roof gives Bentley a direct chance to back up his talk. Overcoming McKenna would serve as a massive victory, yet stepping in against Adames settles the debate outright rather than trusting opinions and rankings.

The roster now holds enough talent to orchestrate high-level clashes at 160 pounds. The real objective lies in turning those names into actual fights. With the WBC cut-off date arriving in seven days, Adames faces a quick choice on how to direct his championship reign.

A title unification between Adames and Bentley makes plenty of sense on paper, yet Bentley must sort out his WBO status before anyone starts drawing up contracts. Yoenli Hernandez sits in the mandatory slot, leaving officials to rule on whether Bentley can take a voluntary defense against Mosley Jr. Skipping Hernandez risks Bentley losing his hardware at the conference table, which instantly ruins the appeal of unifying later.

Bentley might slip up against Mosley Jr. this November, while Hernandez represents an even sharper tactical threat if the order gets enforced.

The real problem Zuffa faces is its middleweight stable. Collecting belts and accumulating regional contenders looks great on a corporate roster sheet, but packaging belts does not automatically manufacture marquee attractions.

Adames, Aaron McKenna, and Bentley are capable fighters, but none of them possess the crossover appeal required to anchor major pay-per-view broadcasts on their own. Callum Walsh has UFC machinery and Dana White pushing him hard in Irish-American hubs, but his ceiling remains heavily questioned by anyone paying attention to genuine top-tier opposition.

Holding sanctioning body hardware without undisputed public recognition leaves the stable vulnerable. Hardcore observers recognize Yoenli Hernandez as the absolute boogeyman at 160 pounds. His Cuban amateur pedigree, slick defensive mobility, and offensive timing make him the nightmare matchup that sanctioning bodies love to avoid mandating. Bentley or McKenna entering a ring with Hernandez would mean walking into a technical trap with minimal mainstream commercial reward and massive downside risk.

Zuffa essentially has an internal ecosystem of mid-tier titleholders who can trade belts among themselves, but as long as Hernandez sits outside that circle waiting for his shot, any claims to real division supremacy remain empty to knowledgeable fans.

Without Yoenli, Zuffa is essentially running an insulated tournament of secondary names where the belts act as promotional props rather than proof of true dominance.

You can stage Bentley versus McKenna or feed Adames to Walsh to generate domestic buzz, but knowledgeable boxing audiences see right through internal round-robins that deliberately bypass the best fighter on the planet at 160 pounds. Hernandez is the legitimizer. He provides the genuine world-class credibility that transforms a manufactured stable into an authentic division takeover.

Until Zuffa opens the checkbook to bring Hernandez into the fold or puts their titleholders in front of him, their middleweight project remains a closed shop, avoiding its true acid test.

Ghana News.title: World Cup Visa Scandal: There is no ‘justification’ to dismiss me – Kofi Adams
Ghana News.content:
Mr Kofi Iddie Adams, Ghana's Minister for Sports and Recreation

Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Adams has rejected calls by the Minority in Parliament for his dismissal over an alleged visa scandal linked to the FIFA World Cup.

About 90 people reportedly paid between $10,000 and $15,000 each, but only five of them obtained visas for the global showpiece, which was staged in the USA, Canada and Mexico.

Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has already been suspended as National Sports Authority (NSA) boss, and further heads are expected to roll at the Sports Ministry as the Presidency is set to launch a probe into the matter, JoySports can confirm.

When asked about calls for his removal, Adams said: “Government money has not been lost,” he told Citi News.

“Well, I don’t see the justification. Both the American Embassy and TRIBE Culture Fest, the NSA and the GTA were doing their thing behind the Ministry. The Ministry didn’t know.

“The first time I ever sat and had a conversation in relation to that matter was when the May 19 letter requested the forwarding of event coordinators and volunteers to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Embassy. That’s when I got to know the details of what was happening.”

Ghana News.title: 2028 Olympic Games qualification ‘really tough’ – Black Queens coach Björkegren
Ghana News.content:
Björkegren

Black Queens head coach Lars Kim Björkegren has described the path to qualifying for the 2028 Olympic Games as “really tough” but says he “believe[s] in the girls” to get the job done.

Having received a bye in the first preliminary round of the qualifiers, the Queens dispatched Mauritius 10-0 to progress to the next phase.

The senior women's national team will face Zambia in the third round, scheduled for 23 February to 6 March 2027.

A total of 16 nations will compete in the third round of the African qualifiers, with the continent having just two slots at the global showpiece.

"We have the potential to go all the way,” Björkegren said.

"In football, there is no easy game, especially when it comes to qualifying for the Olympics, as only two countries from Africa will go to Los Angeles.

"It is really tough and to get there, we need to win. I believe in the girls and I think we [will] be there.”

The Black Queens have never qualified for the Olympic Games in the country's history.

Ghana News.title: GRFU, GOC Women’s Commission hold breast cancer awareness, expresses gratitude to Sunda International Ghana
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Rugby Football Union (GRFU), in collaboration with the Women’s Commission of the Ghana Olympic Committee (GOC), has held a breast cancer awareness education programme for female athletes, coaches, officials and community members.

The initiative focused on the importance of early detection, regular self-examination and screening in the prevention and management of breast cancer.

The organisers said the programme was aimed at improving awareness among women involved in sports and encouraging them to take early action when they notice potential symptoms.

President of the Ghana Rugby Football Union expressed appreciation to Sunda International Ghana Ltd, makers of Softcare, for supporting the initiative.

“Breast cancer affects all women, including our athletes,” the President said.

The President said the partnership had helped educate and encourage participants to pay greater attention to their health.

The GRFU and the GOC Women’s Commission said they remained committed to promoting women’s health, safety and well-being through sports.

They also thanked Sunda International Ghana for its support towards the breast cancer awareness activities.

Ghana News.title: COCOBOD raises GH¢3.4bn as Cocoa Capital PLC lists inaugural commercial paper on GFIM
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) has raised GH¢3.396 billion from domestic institutional investors through its inaugural commercial paper issuance, as the cocoa regulator moves to diversify its financing sources and reduce reliance on external borrowing.

The funds were raised through Cocoa Capital PLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of COCOBOD, under a GH¢16.3 billion Domestic Cocoa Notes Programme, comprising GH¢14 billion in commercial paper to finance cocoa purchases and GH¢2.3 billion in bonds to refinance existing cocoa-sector debt.

The inaugural issuance, known as Series 1 (Tranche 1), has been admitted to the Ghana Fixed Income Market (GFIM) of the Ghana Stock Exchange, marking a significant step in the development of a domestic financing framework for the cocoa industry.

Speaking at the official commercial paper listing ceremony, COCOBOD Chief Executive, Dr Randy Abbey, described the transaction as an important milestone in the evolution of Ghana's cocoa financing framework.

He said the listing demonstrated the potential of domestic capital markets to mobilise resources for strategic sectors of the economy while strengthening the financial foundations of the cocoa industry.

"Today’s ceremony is more than the listing of a financial instrument. It represents an important milestone in the evolution of Ghana’s cocoa-financing framework and demonstrates what can be achieved when public institutions, regulators, capital-market participants, professional advisers and domestic investors work together towards a shared national objective," he said.

The issuance attracted total bids of approximately GH¢3.586 billion from 38 institutional investors, with 36 successful bids amounting to GH¢3.396 billion accepted at a clearing yield of 11 per cent.

Dr Abbey said the level of demand reflected confidence in the cocoa sector and the transaction structure, as well as the capacity of Ghana's domestic investment community to support large-scale financing initiatives.

"The breadth of participation and the level of demand recorded are particularly encouraging for an inaugural issuance under a newly established financing framework," he said.

He added that the successful listing should encourage more domestic institutional investors to participate in subsequent issuances under the programme.

Financing cocoa purchases

The proceeds from the inaugural commercial paper issuance will provide working capital to support cocoa purchases during the 2026/27 crop season.

Dr Abbey said the financing was ultimately intended to ensure that funds were available to purchase cocoa beans from farmers across the country.

"At its heart, therefore, this transaction is about the cocoa farmer. It is about ensuring that adequate funding is available to purchase cocoa beans produced through the hard work of farmers across the country," he said.

The COCOBOD Chief Executive noted that the financing arrangement was part of broader efforts to safeguard farmer incomes, facilitate timely payments and place the cocoa industry on a more sustainable financial footing.

For the 2026/27 season, the producer price has been set at GH¢42,400 per tonne, equivalent to GH¢2,650 per 64-kilogramme bag. This represents 71.18 per cent of the realised gross free-on-board (FOB) value, according to Dr Abbey.

He said the pricing arrangement was consistent with the framework under the Ghana Cocoa Board Act, 2026, which guarantees cocoa farmers at least 70 per cent of the realised gross FOB price.

Shift towards domestic financing

For years, Ghana's cocoa purchases have relied substantially on external financing arrangements. However, changing market conditions and the need to strengthen COCOBOD's financial resilience have prompted efforts to diversify the sources of funding.

Dr Abbey said the Domestic Cocoa Notes Programme represented a deliberate move towards mobilising domestic savings to finance cocoa purchases and meet other funding requirements within the sector.

"The Domestic Cocoa Notes Programme represents a deliberate transition towards a cedi-denominated financing model that mobilizes domestic liquidity, reduces reliance on offshore borrowing and establishes a stronger connection between Ghana’s capital market and one of the country’s most important productive sectors," he said.

He explained that the programme was designed not merely to replace one source of funding with another, but also to broaden COCOBOD's financing options, diversify funding risks and provide a flexible platform for meeting the seasonal and longer-term needs of the industry.

Cocoa Capital PLC was established as a dedicated financing vehicle wholly owned by COCOBOD to raise funds through the domestic capital market for approved cocoa-sector financing and refinancing purposes.

Under the programme, the commercial paper component will provide short-term liquidity for cocoa purchases, while the bond component is intended to refinance designated legacy obligations.

Transaction structure and investor confidence

The programme incorporates arrangements intended to strengthen transparency and discipline in the management of funds and repayment obligations.

Under the structure, selected receivables from executed cocoa forward-sales contracts have been assigned to Cocoa Capital PLC. Collections from these receivables are channelled through designated ring-fenced accounts and applied according to an agreed payment waterfall.

Dr Abbey said the arrangements were intended to improve cash-flow management and provide investors with greater visibility over repayment.

He, however, clarified that the commercial paper remained a senior unsecured obligation of Cocoa Capital PLC, with the assigned receivables and supporting cash-management arrangements forming part of the broader transaction structure.

He said maintaining investor confidence would require strong governance, transparent reporting and the consistent fulfilment of financial obligations.

"Ghana Cocoa Board and Cocoa Capital PLC remain fully committed to these principles," he said.

Boost for Ghana's capital market

The listing also expands the range of fixed-income instruments available to investors on the Ghana Fixed Income Market.

Dr Abbey said the ability to mobilise approximately GH¢3.4 billion for the inaugural issuance demonstrated the capacity of Ghana's domestic capital market to support transactions linked to productive sectors of the economy.

He expressed hope that the transaction would encourage other Ghanaian companies and public-sector institutions to explore capital-market financing as a credible and sustainable funding option.

For domestic investors, the programme provides an opportunity to invest in a cedi-denominated instrument linked to the cocoa value chain, while the broader financing framework is intended to strengthen the relationship between domestic savings and local production.

Dr Abbey stressed that the long-term success of the programme would depend on effective governance, financial discipline and the productive use of funds raised from investors.

Institutions behind the transaction

The issuance involved several financial institutions, regulators and professional advisers.

The Securities and Exchange Commission provided regulatory oversight, while the Ghana Stock Exchange facilitated the admission and listing of the commercial paper on the Ghana Fixed Income Market. The Central Securities Depository supported the issuance, settlement and depository arrangements.

SEM Capital served as transaction adviser, while Absa Bank Ghana, CalBank, Fincap Securities, GCB Bank, One Africa Securities and Stanbic Bank Ghana acted as joint lead managers and bookrunners.

Sory@Law served as transaction counsel, KPMG as the special-purpose vehicle manager, PwC as reporting accountant and Beacon Ratings as the ratings agency.

Dr Abbey commended the institutions and the wider transaction team for their contributions to the structuring, regulatory engagement, investor education and execution of the programme.

He said the listing marked the beginning of a broader responsibility to manage the financing arrangement transparently, meet debt-service obligations and ensure that the benefits of the funds raised were felt across the cocoa value chain.

"The long-term strength of the platform will depend on our continued commitment to sound financial management, effective governance and the productive use of the funds entrusted to us," he said.

The successful admission of Series 1 (Tranche 1) to the Ghana Fixed Income Market marks the first step in implementing the GH¢16.3 billion Domestic Cocoa Notes Programme, which seeks to connect Ghana's domestic capital market with the financing needs of its cocoa industry.

Ghana News.title: No Party Card, just a Party Microphone! A Ghanaian story of Elections, Referees and Convenient Amnesia
Ghana News.content:
By Jimmy Aglah

In a certain Ghanaian town, two football clubs quarrelled over the appointment of a referee. The lady chosen was an accomplished professional who had recently travelled with one team, explained its tactics and encouraged supporters to believe in victory. The club chairman dismissed the protests: the referee had never possessed an official membership card. Surely the spectators could now go home satisfied. What more convincing evidence of neutrality could anyone demand?

If this sounds like village comedy, replace football with elections and the pitch with Ghana. On 12 October, President John Dramani Mahama swore in Emelia Afi Agbenyo as Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission, alongside Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah. He urged them to serve without favour. Excellent advice. Unfortunately, Ghana, that hardworking factory of political contradictions, has noticed a complication in the packaging.

In August 2024, the NDC officially listed Agbenyo among the spokespersons for the governance section of its election manifesto. This is documentary evidence, not WhatsApp archaeology. Presidential staffer Beatrice Annan explains that Agbenyo has never been a card-bearing NDC member and that her campaign engagement reflected longstanding advocacy for women's representation. Her explanation and Agbenyo's professional credentials deserve consideration. But the public may still reasonably ask whether speaking for a party's election manifesto creates an appearance of political affinity.

The membership card has apparently become Ghana's newest miracle-working object. You may carry a party's microphone, explain its promises and help persuade the electorate, but if no card emerges from your handbag, every hint of association vanishes. The mouth that has tasted pepper may now swear the tongue knows nothing of heat. Perhaps our political scientists should stop studying institutions and begin studying handbags.

The NPP has greeted the appointment with thunder. Its communications director, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, questions the wisdom of placing a former NDC manifesto spokesperson in electoral leadership. It is a question worth asking. But memory, that inconvenient village elder, has arrived carrying a stool from 2023. Under President Akufo-Addo, appointments of Peter Appiahene and Salima Ahmed Tijani to the Commission provoked objections over alleged NPP affiliations. CODEO and other civil society organisations warned that even the appearance of partisanship could damage public confidence. Their protest did not produce the resignations they sought.

The NDC now offers a familiar defence. Rashid Tanko-Computer recalls how concerns about earlier appointments were dismissed. But when your neighbour's goat destroys your cassava, you do not repair the injustice by releasing yours into his maize. Two farms ruined do not make a bumper harvest. If the previous government set a poor example, why must its successor treat the mistake as an heirloom?

Let us be fair to Agbenyo. Earlier advocacy does not establish future dishonesty. A citizen can publicly support particular policies and later perform a national duty impartially. Equally, a fine curriculum vitae cannot by itself settle questions of public trust. The Electoral Commission is not a family funeral committee where the chairman may award his cousins the best seats. It administers elections whose losers must trust the arithmetic as much as the winners.

Our Constitution allows the President, acting on the advice of the Council of State, to appoint the Commission's leadership while requiring the institution to remain independent. There lies the puzzle: the political executive helps select the referee and then asks the crowd to forget who handed over the whistle. Proposals for a more transparent appointment process already exist. Why prefer elaborate assurances to stronger safeguards?

Perhaps the real scandal is not the appointment itself but our national talent for manufacturing principles that expire whenever governments change. In opposition, politicians become fierce defenders of institutional independence, quoting the Constitution with the solemnity of a chief priest consulting the oracle. Once in government, yesterday's outrage mysteriously becomes today's administrative wisdom. The same mouths change their sermons without changing their congregations. As our elders warn, the crab cannot give birth to a bird. Yet Ghanaian politics has perfected the art of laying political eggs and announcing that the chicks are completely independent of their parents.

Agbenyo deserves the opportunity to demonstrate impartiality through her conduct. But Ghana deserves something greater than assurances that the referee will behave. We deserve institutions whose credibility does not depend on which political party last occupied Jubilee House. For when citizens begin to suspect the referee before the match has even started, every whistle becomes a controversy, every decision a conspiracy and every defeat a potential national crisis.

And therein lies the question our politicians would rather we did not ask: *If the NDC and NPP can recognise the dangers of partisan appointments so clearly when they are in opposition, why do those dangers suddenly disappear when they enter government?*

Perhaps the answer is painfully simple. In Ghana, we do not appear to object to the referee wearing party colours. We object only when the colours are not our own.

Ghana News.title: Minority welcomes suspension of teachers’ strike, demands timely payment of promotion arrears
Ghana News.content:
The Minority Caucus in Parliament has welcomed the suspension of the nationwide teachers’ strike by the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG), while urging the government to honour its commitments to the unions.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, the Minority commended teachers for returning to the classroom despite their outstanding grievances, saying they had prioritised the education of Ghanaian children.

“Their return is an act of patriotism and good faith,” the statement said.

The caucus also commended the union leadership, parents and the National Council of Parent-Teacher Associations, and acknowledged the roles of the Council of State and the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission in facilitating discussions.

The Minority argued that the strike could have been prevented if the government had implemented previously agreed conditions of service, including the placement of promoted teachers on their new salary grades, payment of the 20 per cent Deprived Area Allowance and negotiations towards a new collective agreement.

It said that although the government and the unions agreed on a process for placing promoted teachers on their new grades on August 31, only 6,079 of the 58,620 promoted teachers had their documents received by the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department as of September 22.

According to the statement, the government missed the unions’ September 24 deadline, leading to the withdrawal of teachers’ services on September 25.

The Minority said the resulting disruption affected pupils across the country, particularly candidates preparing for the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) and the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE), as well as children in deprived communities.

The caucus said the government had made commitments to address the outstanding issues within specific timelines.

It cited October 16, 2026, as the deadline for promotion arrears for the first batch of 51,000 teachers, and October 31 for the placement and arrears of the remaining promoted teachers.

It also listed November 2026 for payment of the Digital Instruction Support Allowance, December for the Continuous Professional Development Allowance, and January 2027 for the rollout of the Deprived Area Allowance.

The conclusion of a new collective agreement remains subject to a timeline to be agreed with the unions.

“The unions have made clear that the strike will resume if any of these dates is missed,” the statement said, urging the government to meet the commitments in full and on time.

The caucus has called for the prompt placement of all promoted teachers on their correct salary grades and payment of arrears dating from January 1, 2026.

It also wants the government to reconcile the union’s figure of more than 80,000 promoted teachers with the official figure of 58,620 and publish a verified list to ensure that no eligible teacher is excluded.

Other demands include digitising the promotion-to-payroll process, briefing Parliament’s Education Committee on progress, agreeing on a firm timeline for a new collective agreement, and developing a learning recovery plan for BECE and WASSCE candidates and pupils in deprived communities.

The Minority said it would monitor the government’s performance against each deadline and report to the public.

“The 2024 Collective Agreement already provides the framework to resolve these matters. What is needed now is implementation, not more promises,” the statement said.

The suspension of the strike follows engagements between the government and the unions over delayed promotions, allowances and negotiations on a new collective agreement. The next key deadline identified by the Minority is October 16, when the first batch of 51,000 teachers is expected to receive their promotion arrears.

Ghana News.title: Customary ownership accounts for 80% of land; it complicates land administration – Lands Commission
Ghana News.content:
The Lands Commission says family disputes, multiple sales of the same plots and inadequate planning on customary lands remain major obstacles to effective land administration in Ghana.

Its Deputy Executive Secretary in charge of Operations, Surveyor Raphael Hokey, said an estimated 80% of the country’s land falls under customary ownership, leaving about 20% classified as public land.

He explained that this ownership structure complicates efforts to manage land and ensure orderly development.

“It’s been roughly estimated that about 80% of the land is customary land. Only 20% are public lands,” he said in an interview with Citi FM.

Mr Hokey explained that public lands include state and vested lands. For vested lands, customary owners retain the beneficial interest, while the legal interest rests with the state.

He said these arrangements present difficulties for institutions tasked with administering land, particularly where they lack full control over the property concerned.

“You are trying to manage what you don’t own and control properly,” he stated.

Mr Hokey identified disagreements within landowning families and disputes over traditional leadership as recurring problems affecting transactions.

He explained that competing claims over who is authorised to represent a family or community can lead to litigation and uncertainty for prospective buyers.

The sale of a single parcel to different purchasers, he added, continues to create ownership disputes and undermine land administration.

Beyond ownership conflicts, Mr Hokey expressed concern about the lack of planning and infrastructure on some customary lands.

He said plots are often sold without access roads, essential services or clearly marked boundaries, leaving buyers to contend with difficulties when developing their properties.

This, he noted, also raises questions about whether landowning families or the State should provide the infrastructure needed to support those developments.

On enforcement, Mr Hokey said stronger cooperation among public institutions was necessary to address unauthorised construction and other land-related challenges.

He explained that local assemblies could seek Police assistance to deal with unauthorised development and pursue court orders where cases require judicial intervention.

Ghana News.title: NRSA to auction vehicles of non-subscribers who fail to pay towing charges within 21 days
Ghana News.content:
Abraham Amaliba

The Director-General of the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA), Abraham Amaliba, has warned that vehicles belonging to drivers who fail to subscribe to the mandatory towing service could be auctioned if the Authority removes them from the road and the owners fail to pay the resulting charges.

Speaking in an interview on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Wednesday, October 14, Mr Amaliba explained that the Authority would remove vehicles that break down in dangerous locations and pose a risk to other road users, regardless of whether their owners had subscribed to the towing service.

He said the owners would be surcharged for the removal and could lose their vehicles if they failed to settle the charges after being contacted through the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA).

“If you don’t subscribe, and we find that your car is stationary and will cause an accident, we’ll come and remove it, and we’ll surcharge you,” he said.

Mr Amaliba added that the Authority would use vehicle registration records to trace owners who fail to pay.

“If you don’t pay the surcharge, we will find you through your registration processes at DVLA. We will contact you within 21 days. If you don’t come, we will gazette the sale of the car, and then auction it,” he stated.

His comments come as the government prepares to implement a new road safety policy expected to accompany the Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill, 2025, which seeks to address the dangers posed by broken-down vehicles on Ghana’s roads.

Mr Amaliba also announced plans to develop a mobile application that would connect motorists whose vehicles break down with the nearest available towing company.

When asked what a driver who had subscribed to a towing service in Accra should do if their vehicle broke down in Wenchi, Mr Amaliba said the proposed application would allow motorists to request assistance from a nearby towing operator rather than wait for their registered company to travel a long distance.

“We are going to develop an app. We know your towing company could be far away from where you are, and so calling the towing company to come may take time as well. And the law says that you must remove the car immediately,” he explained.

He said the application would work in a similar way to ride-hailing services, matching motorists with the nearest available towing company.

“We are going to develop an app where you can, just like Uber, have the nearest available towing company come and remove you,” he said.

Mr Amaliba added that towing companies would be responsible for resolving payment arrangements among themselves when a company other than the motorist’s subscribed provider responded to a call.

“The towing companies will now deal with how to exchange their money,” he said.

According to him, the application would also provide a practical way of demonstrating that the required notification had been made promptly.

During the Joy FM interview, concerns were raised about whether towing companies would be able to respond quickly enough, even when drivers notified them immediately.

The host pointed to the NRSA’s indication that stationary vehicles contribute to between 10 and 12 per cent of fatal accidents and asked how quickly towing companies were expected to arrive after being informed of a breakdown.

Mr Amaliba said the proposed application was intended to address that concern by identifying the nearest available operator.

“That’s why we are supporting with an app,” he said.

“When you go on your Uber app, you find the nearest Uber car. You don’t wait for the Uber car that is coming from Tema to you when there is one in Kokomlemle. So that’s how we are going to deal with it,” he said.

This comes after the National Road Safety Authority revealed that drivers whose vehicles break down in major city centres will be required to arrange towing within 30 minutes under a new road safety policy expected to accompany the implementation of the Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill, 2025.

The policy is aimed at preventing broken-down vehicles from causing traffic congestion and road hazards, particularly in busy urban areas.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Israeli air strike kills Palestinian woman in Gaza City
World.content:
The woman’s young daughter was rescued from a large fire inside the apartment caused by the attack.

An Israeli air strike on an apartment block in Gaza has killed a woman and wounded two other people, hospital officials said.

Reem Asaad Awad, 33, was killed in the attack early on Wednesday in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood of Gaza City, the Turkish state news agency Anadolu reported, quoting a source at Al Shifa hospital.

The source said the strike caused extensive destruction to the targeted apartment and nearby buildings.

The daughter of the woman who was killed was rescued from a large fire that broke out after the attack.

Israel says it is investigating the strike and claims it targeted a member of Hamas, without providing evidence.

Reporting from Gaza City, Al Jazeera’s Ibrahim al-Khalili said the strike happened at 4am (01:00 GMT).

Israel has killed 1,501 Palestinians in Gaza since it agreed a “ceasefire” with the Palestinian group Hamas last October. The truce was part of a wider United States-backed proposal to end Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in Gaza.

Talks aimed at advancing to the second phase of the US plan, which includes the withdrawal of Israeli forces and the disarmament of Hamas, have stalled.

The agreement states that 600 trucks of humanitarian aid are to be allowed into Gaza each day, but Israeli authorities have continued to impose severe restrictions on supplies entering the enclave, and reconstruction of the war-shattered territory has not begun.

World.title: How a radio glitch triggered a false hijack alert in Germany
World.content:
Authorities scrambled fighter jets to escort a plane on its way from Corfu to Nuremberg after a pilot sent a hijack alert.

German authorities briefly closed an airport and scrambled fighter jets to escort a passenger plane on Tuesday following an emergency alert indicating a hijacking was taking place on board. However, the alert had been accidentally triggered by a radio “malfunction”.

Corendon Airlines said its Boeing 737-800, which was en route from the Greek holiday island of Corfu to Nuremberg, Germany, sent out an emergency code while it was flying over Croatia “due to a brief malfunction in the radio communication system”.

In a statement, the airline said that “no emergency situation occurred”, and the 178 passengers, flight crew and aircraft had not been in danger at any point. The plane landed safely in Nuremberg.

What happened?

German police said Corendon Airlines flight XR456 “inadvertently” sent out an emergency “squawk” alert with the code 7500 while flying over Croatia on Tuesday.

A squawk is a four-digit code a pilot sends via the jet’s transponder to air traffic control. The code 7500 tells air traffic controllers that a hijacking is in progress.

However, air traffic controllers were unable to make contact with the pilots or crew, causing the alarm to be raised further. It is unclear why this happened.

“The aircraft could no longer be reached by radio to clarify the situation”, prompting warnings to be activated in several European countries, police said.

A Rafale fighter jet was scrambled from Croatia to intercept the Boeing passenger jet, while the German military also dispatched warplanes.



Police cordoned off the Albrecht Dürer airport in Nuremberg as a precaution until they knew the reason the pilot had sent the hijack alert.

Police spokesman Michael Petzold explained that authorities had “received a code directly from the cockpit that suggested a hijacking”.

“Since we were then unable to reach the cockpit, and the tower was also unable to contact the cockpit, we had to assume the worst – that it might indeed be a hijacking,” Petzold said.

The incident disrupted flights, with six flights delayed and two inbound flights diverted to other airports as a precaution, a Nuremberg airport spokesperson said.

Why are aviation authorities so concerned?

The hijack scare has come amid heightened concerns about aviation security after the copilot on board a Flydubai jet bound for Israel from Dubai attacked the captain with an emergency crash axe, forcing the flight to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on September 30.

On Friday, the United Arab Emirates’ prosecutor general said the copilot was on a “suicide” mission to crash the plane at Ben Gurion airport in Tel Aviv and called the incident a “terrorist attack”.

Also, before the false hijack alert in the early hours of Tuesday, flights had been briefly disrupted at Nuremberg ‌airport after pilots reported suspected drone sightings.

Authorities across Europe have already stepped up surveillance of the skies in recent weeks after a series of mostly mysterious drone incidents and concerns about Russian hybrid warfare.

Western nations, including Germany, have accused Moscow of launching a campaign of sabotage, espionage and disruption to undermine European support for Ukraine and destabilise the continent.

Several German airports have had to suspend operations for brief periods in recent months due to drone activity, with suspicion often falling on Russia.

Last month, the German government blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle airport in August using a drone laden with explosives. Berlin closed the Russian consulate among other measures.

Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed the allegations, saying Berlin “fabricated” the evidence. However, in light of the concerns, NATO’s top general told the Warsaw Security Forum earlier this week that the alliance has a new war plan for countering a Russian attack on its members, embedding lessons learned from the Ukrainian front lines.

How common are radio glitches and false hijack alerts?

Radio glitches are common, but incidents rarely escalate to major security events because pilots use back-up radios to communicate with air traffic controllers when they lose communication signals.



In 2019, a pilot flying an Air Europa jet from Amsterdam to Madrid accidentally transmitted hijack alert 7500. For half an hour, aviation authorities thought the alarm was a genuine emergency and followed safety protocols, which disrupted flights and led to the evacuation of part of Schipol airport in the Netherlands.

In 2011, a flight from Chicago to Germany was diverted to Toronto when a pilot spilled coffee and accidentally set off a hijack alarm. The spill caused distress signals to go out, including the 7500 transponder code.
