World.title: China’s exports surge amid AI-driven demand
World.content:
Exports grew by 36.3 percent in September, the biggest leap since the COVID-19 pandemic.

China’s exports surged by more than one-third in September, a boost to the world’s second-largest economy as it faces slowing growth.

Exports grew by 36.3 percent last month year-on-year to reach $447.18bn, accelerating from a 25 percent gain in August, government figures released on Wednesday show.

The leap marked the biggest monthly rise in exports since 2021, when China’s trade figures were skewed by the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and stringent lockdowns.

Tech-related trade led the growth, with semiconductor exports surging more than 108 percent and shipments of automatic data processing machines jumping nearly 55 percent.

Imports increased 31 percent year-on-year, up from 28.2 percent in August, according to the figures from the General Administration of Customs.

“High-tech demand, supported by the global and domestic AI upcycle, remained the key driver, while China’s pricing and supply-chain competitiveness in other major export categories also helped sustain the momentum,” Taylor Wang, an economist at HSBC in Hong Kong, said in a note to clients.

China’s total exports in the first nine months of the year rose 21.3 percent to $3.37 trillion, while imports gained 27.5 percent to $2.43 trillion.

The gap between exports and imports in the first three quarters gave China a trade surplus of $938.1bn.

The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was China’s biggest export market by a wide margin, with exports rising more than 52 percent in September to $81.7bn.

Exports to the European Union rose 25.3 percent in September to $60.15bn, while shipments to the United States jumped 39.6 percent to $47.88bn.



After decades of relying on state-led investment and exports to power its economy, China is striving to find new avenues for growth amid a falling population, deflating property market, and weak domestic consumption, which contributes far less to gross domestic product (GDP) than in advanced economies.

China’s economy is expected to grow 4.5 percent in 2026, according to the International Monetary Fund’s latest growth outlook, which would be the slowest expansion since 1990, excluding the outlier years of the COVID pandemic.

“The strong export growth should keep China’s growth on track to achieve its growth target of 4.5-5 percent for 2026,” Lynn Song, chief economist for Greater China at ING, told Al Jazeera.

“Nonetheless, growth remains quite unbalanced, with domestic data quite soft in comparison,” Song said.

“It will be important to rebalance growth over the medium term if China is to achieve its longterm growth targets.”

World.title: How do Iranians move money abroad to avoid US sanctions?
World.content:
From currency brokers to crypto, Iranians find ways to circumvent sanctions, but each comes with its own problems.

Share How do Iranians move money abroad to avoid US sanctions? on social media

Tehran, Iran – Decades of international sanctions have severely restricted Iran’s access to the global financial system, making cross-border payments difficult for individuals and businesses alike. The sanctions have only increased with the current US-Israeli war on Iran.

Unable to rely on conventional banking for international transactions, many Iranians have turned to alternative channels to pay for goods and services abroad.

And while each workaround channel offers a way to navigate some of the restrictions, it comes with its own costs and risks, often falling short of the security, reliability and efficiency of a functioning international banking system.

One alternative financial channel is relying on networks of currency exchangers that operate across borders, an informal system that matches those who need local currency in Iran with those who need foreign currency abroad. By balancing these opposing needs, transactions can be settled without money necessarily moving directly between Iranian and foreign bank accounts.

There are other similar methods.

Intermediary firms offer services comparable to currency exchange traders. Typically, a customer pays the intermediary in local currency in Iran, while the firm or an overseas partner arranges payment to the foreign supplier in a convertible currency, using funds held abroad.

Using currency traders or intermediary firms can help bridge gaps in international banking access, but both often involve additional fees, exchange-rate costs, delays and greater complexity.



Other Iranians don’t deal with companies, but resort to private arrangements with individuals, including people they do not know personally, to transfer money across borders. Those deals may offer a practical solution when formal channels are unavailable, but they rely heavily on trust rather than enforceable guarantees.

“The transaction involves strangers having to trust one another to conduct a deal without any legal documentation or proof,” said Reza, an Iranian IT manager in Germany, who did not wish to give his full name. “It relies entirely on trust, and either party can back out at any time, leaving the others out of pocket.”

The methods used – whether through companies or individuals – are informal and not the most secure. “We have to use informal exchange and remittance systems for international trade, which carries risks such as lost funds, fraud and high transfer costs,” explained Ashkan Bahrami, an Iranian trade expert.

These networks are also vulnerable to geopolitical shocks. Some operating through Gulf countries have been disrupted by the war, adding another layer of uncertainty for businesses and individuals dependent on them.

The crypto route

Cryptocurrency has offered another route, enabling users to transfer wealth without relying on conventional banks. But even these digital assets have not provided a fully reliable escape from sanctions. Earlier this year, the US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned several major Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges, including Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin and Ramzinex.

Alireza Yaghoubi, chairman of Iran’s FinTech Association board, warned that crypto transactions are traceable, “and very bad things can happen, such as the sanctions imposed on multiple Iranian wallets, whether they belonged to individuals, the Central Bank, or other entities”.

The possibility of sanctions, combined with periodic internet disruptions, makes cryptocurrency an uncertain option.

Import delays

For businesses importing physical goods, the challenges extend beyond payment itself. War-related disruptions and restrictions, particularly after the US naval blockade on Iran, have complicated transportation, lengthened delivery times, and increased uncertainty over when shipments will arrive.

Arghavan Ghazanfari, CEO of Aron Trading Group, described the scale of the disruption facing importers using the port of Shanghai in China, a major gateway for goods shipped to Iran.

“Transit time used to be 26 days. But when it stretches nowadays to 102 or even 120 days, customers are bound to reconsider importing,” Ghazanfari said. “Unfortunately, the main problem now is that our supply routes are gradually being cut off.”



And even when Iranians find a way to make payments abroad – and are willing to accept the delays in receiving their goods – another problem remains: whether they can afford what they are trying to buy.

The Iranian rial’s sustained depreciation has sharply eroded purchasing power. Against the US dollar, Iran’s currency has lost more than 10 percent of its value over the past month, more than 55 percent over the past year and almost 90 percent over the past five years.

And there is little certainty that the pressure will ease anytime soon.

With the prospect of another escalation in the conflict looming over Iran and uncertainty clouding the country’s economic outlook, the question for many Iranians is not simply how to move money across borders. It is how long they can keep navigating an increasingly restrictive financial system, and what it will cost them to do so.

World.title: Trump says oil, gas and mineral exploration to begin in Greenland
World.content:
Trump also praises the security advantages from last month’s deal with Denmark and Greenland.

Share Trump says oil, gas and mineral exploration to begin in Greenland on social media

United States President Donald Trump has said that “massive” exploration for oil, gas and minerals is set to begin in Greenland.

In a post on his Truth Social platform on Wednesday, Trump said that the Arctic island, a self-governing Danish territory, holds some of the world’s largest reserves of “easily” extractable oil.

“Massive Oil, Gas, and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin in our new and beautiful Greenland!” Trump said in a post on Truth Social.

“The amount of easily available Oil is far greater than that of almost … anywhere in the World,” he wrote, quoting experts.

He did not give details of potential US involvement.

Last month, Trump reached a security deal with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland that expands the role of the US military on the island.

The agreement paves the way for two new military bases and Trump’s planned “Golden Dome” missile defence system, while ‌‌reaffirming ‌‌Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination.

The deal was aimed at ending an almost two-year-long crisis over Trump’s refusal to rule out the US seizing Greenland by force.

In his social media post on Wednesday, Trump also praised the security advantages that both the US and Europe have gained from last month’s pact as “second to none”.

He said that any aerial attack against the US could not be conducted without passing Greenland, arguing that Washington would be able to neutralise any threat as a result.

“Any future attack on the United States will have to come across Greenland, where our defence will routinely knock down drones, missiles, or any other form of weapon not yet even conceived,” Trump said.



“It gives us time, location, and sightline, like nowhere else in the world!”

There was no immediate comment on the US president’s post from the leaders of Greenland or Denmark.

World.title: Russian strikes leave 600,000 without power in Ukraine, as Starlink restrictions affect front line
World.content:
At least 600,000 people in Ukraine are without electricity after deadly overnight Russian missile and drone strikes, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

He said "critical" energy infrastructure had been hit in Kyiv and the capital region, and in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv â despite US President Donald Trump's claim on Sunday that an "energy ceasefire" was in place between Russia and Ukraine.

Three people were killed in Kyiv, officials said. Russia said its "massive" strikes had hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military.

Separately, Zelensky's adviser said speed restrictions on the Starlink communications network had disrupted Ukrainian battlefield "missions".

In Wednesday's post on Telegram, Serhiy Beskrestnov said Elon Musk's SpaceX company had "implemented overnight a speed limit on Starlink terminals".

He said Ukrainian troops had not been informed about this, and the speed limits â set at 100mph (160km/h) â had already resulted in "the disruption of a number of missions".

"It is clear that this action cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation," Beskrestnov said.

In the follow-up post, he stressed that Starlink was the most effective tool for enabling interceptors to shoot down Russia's newly developed jet-propelled drones.

World.title: Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican has said in a medical bulletin.

The 71-year-old underwent a 90-minute surgery on Tuesday at Rome's Gemelli Hospital and was subsequently diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma.

"The operation was successful and there were no complications," the Vatican said. "After the operation, the Pope awoke normally and returned after a brief period of observation to his room."

The pontiff had a "peaceful night" in the hospital, the Vatican said on Wednesday morning, and he is expected to remain there for about a week.

Large crowds had waited outside the hospital for the Pope's arrival on Tuesday, cheering as he waved and smiled through a window as his car went past.

He was met by staff on the hospital steps. "I'm sorry," one of them commiserated, to which the Pope gave a smile and a shrug.

The Vatican said the whole lower lobe of the Pope's right lung was removed "to ensure the procedure was radical".

It was Leo himself who on Sunday announced news of his operation to the world during his weekly Sunday prayers, telling the crowd in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a nodule on his lung.

He reassured pilgrims that the mass was "well-contained" and caught "at an early stage" but that his doctors had advised him to have it removed.

Nodules are quite common and not necessarily cancerous, but after it was examined the medical team confirmed it was, "as suspected by pre-operative tests", the Vatican said.

A Vatican source told news agency AFP that further tests were now being carried out to see whether the cancer had spread.

World.title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
World.content:
The case has highlighted differences of opinion on the trial in Kyiv and Berlin.

Oleksandr Merezhko, who chairs the Foreign Affairs Committee in the Ukrainian parliament, points out that the blasts took place during a time of war with Russia and "Nord Stream 2 was nothing but a tool used by Russia in order to get prepared for the war".

He told the BBC they had no confirmation of the German account: "It's one of the versions."

However, Stefan Meister, of the German Council on Foreign Relations, says successive chancellors in Berlin have done their best to remove the politics from the case.

"They tried to make not a big story out of it, not to give it too much attention, to give it to the institutions, to the judiciary that they will deal with it. This is not a political case. So they tried to depoliticise it," he explained.

In August 2025, Serhii K was arrested after checking into a hotel near the Italian Adriatic resort of Rimini, by police acting under a European arrest warrant issued by federal prosecutors in Germany.

After several weeks of court battles fighting extradition, Serhii K - identified in court documents as Serhii Kuznetsov - was transferred to Germany late last year.

German prosecutors allege that in 2022 he was a serving officer in the Ukrainian army, external, and he had led a group of professional divers, a boat captain and an explosives expert.

While his legal fight was going on in Italy, another Ukrainian man called Volodymyr Zhuravlov successfully challenged Germany's extradition bid in a Polish court.

In a ruling very different from Italy's Supreme Court, the Polish judge ordered Zhuravlov's release in October 2025, stating that the attack on the pipelines was not unlawful, and if Ukraine had organised an armed mission it was "justified, rational and just".

Although he was released by the court in Warsaw, he was arrested last August in Croatia on suspicion of being a suspect who "participated in the dives necessary" for the sabotage.

Last month, Croatia approved his extradition, although it is not clear when that will happen, and if his case could become part of the Hamburg trial.

Despite the difficult nature of the case for Kyiv and Berlin, Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko does not believe it will spoil relations as "it's in the best national interests of Germany to continue to support us".

World.title: Saudi employee charged with planting recording device in OpenAI office
World.content:
A Saudi national has been charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's offices in California, federal prosecutors announced.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked at the AI firm as an engineer, was charged federally with using or endeavouring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications.

OpenAI said it had discovered a "sophisticated recording device" hidden in their San Francisco office and alerted the FBI. The company said it used its AI models to track that it had been planted by an employee.

Prosecutors say the device, wrapped in toilet paper, was found inserted in a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room.

OpenAI, the maker of the popular chatbot ChatGPT, said that it has no indication that source code, model weights or customer data were inappropriately accessed or taken in the incident. It said the employee has been fired.

According to the complaint, Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement.

Patel said that the alleged goal was to capture information about the company's AI product.

Alfozan has been working as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, prosecutors say.

On 30 September, OpenAI employees discovered the device - two days after prosecutors say it had been installed. The device was encrypted, prosecutors said.

OpenAI said they were able to use their AI models "to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier".

According to the FBI, the suspect used a "productivity tool" and a "chatbot" to research sensitive locations at OpenAI and how to secretly place audio equipment.

Chatbot prompts that he is alleged to have searched include "building, customising, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device", prosecutors allege.

He is also accused of using the chatbot to ask about "'build[ing] a continuous audio recorder,' 'customis[ing] Wi-Fi . . . connectivity,' 'improv[ing] audio and live listening,' and 'encrypt[ing] the SD card'".

World.title: Turkish police raid opposition TV station, halting live broadcasts
World.content:
Turkish police have raided the headquarters of one of the country's most-watched news channel, halting its live broadcasts.

Halk TV, which is pro-opposition, said its employees were unable to enter the building in Istanbul on Wednesday morning. The government also appointed a new administrator to run the channel.

Reports in Turkish media said financial crimes police were searching the building and 11 people had been taken into custody in the raid linked to the channel's owner.

It is the latest in a series of crackdowns on news sources deemed to be critical of Turkish President Tayyip ErdoÄan and his government.

Two weeks ago, officials closed a leading news site because of what they called its "LGBT propaganda".

Halk's news channel and live broadcasts on its YouTube page were both offline early on Wednesday.

The channel has been seen by many in the country as being close to the opposition Republican People's Party (CHP). It often voices criticism of ErdoÄan's ruling AK party.

Prosecutors said arrest warrants had been issued for 17 people as part of the investigation into Halk chairman Cafer MahiroÄlu on allegations of bribery, rigging tenders and money laundering, Turkish media reported.

MahiroÄlu, who was reportedly not in the country during the raid, wrote on social media that seven members of his family were among those detained.

"Today is a dark day for Turkey," he said in a video message. "The public's right to information is being seized for political reasons."

The Istanbul Bar Association denounced the move, which it noted came hours before Ekrem ImamoÄlu, widely seen as ErdoÄan's biggest political rival, was due to begin his defence against corruption charges in court, for which he has been in prison for over a year.

World.title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI
World.content:
MI5 is devoting more resource to countering state threats than during the Cold War, the head of the intelligence service has said.

Sir Ken McCallum said threats from foreign adversaries had quadrupled in the last decade, with Russia "aggressor number one" as well as increased Iran-linked aggression against Jewish sites and military bases.

At an annual speech in London, MI5's chief said Russia was waging hybrid warfare at a time when AI was "supercharging the cyber-security contest between attackers and defenders".

He also warned of rising threats from "extreme right-wing terrorism" and said MI5 had "caught terrorists seeking to exploit AI," including by integrating the technology with drones.

He said the biggest threat from the misuse of AI was extremist groups using the technology to harness new and existing bioweapons.

However, he noted that work countering terrorism and state threats was now "pretty much of equal scale" which he described as a "huge shift" in recent years.

Sir Ken said Russia had stopped short of "conventional conflict" against Nato and is instead trying to unsettle European countries while its progress in its full-scale invasion of Ukraine is "minimal and horrifically costly".

Hybrid warfare or hybrid attacks are loose terms which tend to describe non-military methods, for example cyber-attacks, sabotage or misinformation, designed to exert pressure and destabilise an adversary.

These are quite often employed using proxies, but Russia always denies involvement in such attacks despite growing evidence to the contrary.

Sir Ken said MI5 successes in identifying and expelling Russian spies from the UK had left the Kremlin dependent on paying proxies for attempted attacks.

"With its traditional covert footprint eviscerated by almost 1,000 expulsions since the invasion, the Kremlin's global toolkit is weak, he said.

"So we see them scrambling to pay criminals to do their bidding."

He added: "These are not the actions of a great power with the strategic upper hand."

His comments come as a growing number of leaders across Europe have warned Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine.

Asked after the speech about Prime Minister Andy Burnham's recent comments that Russia interfered with the Brexit referendum, Sir Ken said it was "not new news" that there had been attempts from Moscow but distinguished between "interference attempted" and "outcome achieved".

He said it was a matter of public record that there were pieces in Russian media and "so-called internet trolls and bot farms" seeking to influence the Brexit debate, but also stressed that the result of the 2016 referendum was "not in dispute".

He added that he was "worried" about the the ongoing debate on Russian interference.

"I am a little bit anxious that we don't play into our adversaries' hands by making these trolls look 10ft tall," he told reporters.

World.title: Missiles intercepted near Riyadh after Saudi coalition hits Yemen fuel depot
World.content:
Missiles and drones have been intercepted over Riyadh after the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen struck a fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital, Sanaa, its spokesperson says.

Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said projectiles targeting the Saudi capital and other cities were intercepted. No casualties have been reported however fires broke out at Saudi oil company Aramco's building in Dhahran after the strike, officials said.

It comes after the coalition struck the Yemen Petroleum Company's al-Sabaha facility on Tuesday night.

The latest tit-for-tat attacks in the conflict "have potentially negative spillovers for everybody, everywhere", the chief of the the International Monetary Fund said.

The Houthis warned they would target the airport and Aramco refinery in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, and Aramco's headquarters in the eastern city of Dammam.

It came as the Saudi cabinet, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, said the Iran-backed group would "bear the consequences" of its recent deadly attacks on the kingdom.

Thirteen people were killed when a missile hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday, while another person was killed in a similar attack there the following day.

On Tuesday, the coalition said its forces had destroyed three drones north of Riyadh.

The Houthis have said they are targeting airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia with missiles and drones in response to deadly Saudi strikes on territory that they control in western Yemen, including Sanaa.

The Saudi-led coalition has been providing air support for Yemeni pro-government forces mounting an offensive on Yemen's Red Sea coast and several other front lines.

World.title: Trump ousts Kimberly Guilfoyle as US ambassador to Greece after corruption allegations
World.content:
President Donald Trump's administration has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign from her position as US ambassador to Greece, according to White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia.

Guilfoyle, a former Fox News host, was facing mounting scrutiny over reports she allegedly asked a Trump donor to pay her hefty credit card bill in exchange for access to the administration and behaved inappropriately while in Athens.

Trump said on Tuesday that she had done a good job, but will "not be there" in Greece any longer. "I didn't like what I read," he said.

Guilfoyle vowed to defend herself, calling the claims false, and said the ambassadorship had been the "honour of a lifetime".

Zacharia announced during her first - and unusually short - media briefing that Guilfoyle "had been asked to resign" without providing more details.

"She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well," she said.

Guilfoyle, the 57-year-old ex-wife of California Governor Gavin Newsom, was first nominated as envoy to Athens in December 2024, a month before Trump returned to the White House as president.

Around the same time, news broke that she had broken up with Donald Trump Jr, to whom she was engaged.

In a lengthy post on X on Tuesday, Guilfoyle thanked President Trump, said she would always be a loyal supporter and denied any wrongdoing.

"I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity," she wrote, adding she will "not allow false accusations to define my decades of public service".

Her position had become increasingly tenuous as allegations of improper behaviour mounted over the past week.

A series of text messages seen by the BBC - and first reported by The Wall Street Journal - appear to show Guilfoyle asking for the money from Eric Deters, a long-time Trump ally.

"It won't show up anywhere if you wire money to American Express," she wrote in one Signal message.

In another message - dated just days before her US Senate confirmation hearing last July - Guilfoyle wrote: "Honey please I need you to get this done for me today."

World.title: JUST IN: Nigerian government introduces ‘five big fiscal reforms’ to woo investors, engender growth
World.content:
Nigeria’s Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, on Wednesday unveiled five fiscal reforms he said the Nigerian government will introduce to create a conducive business environment, engender growth and boost investments.

The minister spoke at the Nigerian Investors’ Forum held on the sidelines of the World Bank/IMF annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.

The forum, attended by corporate investors, bankers, government officials and others, was put together to showcase Nigeria’s bankable opportunities and strategic investor conversations in Bangkok.

Speaking at the event, Mr Oyedele said Nigeria plans to introduce “five big reforms” in the fiscal space as part of its efforts to attract the right investment and engender development. He listed the key reform areas to include agriculture and food security, power, regulation, inflation and data management.

“I’ll give you some of the five big issues, big reforms, to expect from the government,” the minister said at the forum.

“One of it is agric reform. One of the drivers of inflation is food. So we are trying to now piece this together to find where these problems are coming from. One thing that we’ve seen recently is that when analysts go on TV, economists talk about why there is inflation; they will talk about bad roads, they will tell you insecurity, and I say yes to some extent.

“If roads are bad, they shouldn’t create inflation unless the roads are worse this year than they were last year. So, the data we have shows that roads are better generally than previously.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“So, we know where the inflation and the pressure for it is coming from. We’re going to tackle it there, not only just to bring it down to a single digit, but to leave it there.”

Mr Oyedele said the second significant reform to expect is power.

“You cannot power a one trillion-dollar economy in darkness,” the minister said.

“It’s impossible. So we’re looking at strategies to address the issues; whether it’s market-reflective pricing, dealing with issues around transmission, how do you drive efficiency, which is not there currently.”

The minister said inflation management remains another major reform target.

“So there is a dedicated focus on what we want to do, particularly from the fiscal side, to rein in inflation. And we’re working with sub-nationals. So everybody has their role.

“And this is not just to say something that’s nice, it’s a plan with assigned roles and responsibilities with timelines. So, my role is just to coordinate all of that together.”

Another pain point identified by the government, the minister said, was in the area of regulations.

He said: “We estimate that over-regulation, regulatory burden, lack of clarity, a number of those excessive burdens that we impose on businesses actually are costing us more than the combined revenue from corporate tax, personal income tax, and VAT combined.

“And you can ask me, what is the best example of a win-win outcome? Where the government wins, private sector wins even more. So we have started by developing a framework for economic policy for Nigeria.”

The minister explained further that data management remains key.

“People say, and we agree with them, that it’s difficult to find data about Nigeria, especially from the fiscal side. Something as important as our tax-to-GDP ratio, you can’t find it easily. The World Bank in their NDU quoted an amount of tax-to-GDP ratio that is much lower than it is actually.

“If you go to the IMF today, their numbers are different. Within government, depending on who is saying it and when they are saying it, they quote different numbers. Now, we said, ‘not anymore’.

“So we are currently finalising all of that and it will be available on the website of the Ministry of Finance, finance.gov.ng. It will be updated timely, it will be accessible, it will be credible. We are playing now on visibility and elevating credibility.”

World.title: Gbenga Adeyinka to end Laffmattazz tour in Lagos
World.content:
Nigerian comedian Gbenga Adeyinka will end his 2026 Laffmattazz comedy tour in Lagos on 15 November. The tour has held shows in Nigeria, Canada and the United Kingdom.

The grand finale, tagged Lagos Gets the Last Laugh, will take place at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island, Lagos. The event will begin at 3 p.m.

According to a statement by the organisers, Laughter Incorporated Ventures, the show will feature comedy, music, culture and fashion. It will also mark the end of the tour’s 15th anniversary year and celebrate more than 30 years of Mr Adeyinka’s career in entertainment.

The event’s theme is The Next Chapter: A New Season of Laughter.

For Mr Adeyinka, also known as Gbenga Adeyinka 1st, the Lagos show is a return to a city that helped build his career. The organisers said Lagos provided stages where he performed and audiences who supported his work more than 30 years ago.

Tour across cities

The 2026 tour has held shows in Ibadan, Akure, Calgary, London, Ontario, Toronto and Abeokuta. The Lagos event will be the final show of the tour.

FirstBank is the lead sponsor and official tour partner. The organisers thanked the bank for supporting the tour in Nigeria and Canada.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

They are also seeking more sponsors and brand partners for the Lagos event. According to the statement, brands can support the show through promotions, audience activities and hospitality services.

The organisers said the event would give brands a chance to connect with people through comedy and other cultural activities.

More information about the performers and tickets will be shared through the tour’s official channels.

World.title: Plateau police arrest suspects, recover locally made guns
World.content:
The police have arrested several suspects and recovered locally fabricated firearms and ammunition in separate operations in Plateau State.

The Commissioner of Police, Ayodeji Faniyan, disclosed this on Tuesday at the Inspector-General of Police’s conference in Abuja.

Mr Faniyan, said the command was strengthened intelligence-led operations and community policing to prevent crime and deny criminal elements safe havens.

“Plateau State will be too hot for them to operate,” Mr Faniyan warned, adding that the command had reviewed its crime prevention strategies in response to security challenges across the state.

He said officers had been directed to uphold professionalism, discipline, integrity and transparency in their duties, warning them against corruption and illegal operations.

Mr Faniyan said the command was also strengthening collaboration with residents and other security agencies to improve intelligence gathering and facilitate the arrest of criminal suspects.

According to him, a joint security operation involving the police, military, State Security Services, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, National Drug Law Enforcement Agency and other agencies was conducted in parts of the state following recent security incidents in Mangu, Barkin Ladi, Riyom and Bokkos local government areas.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the operation, which included a show of force, covered vulnerable communities, flashpoints and suburban areas to reassure residents and reinforce security presence.

The commissioner added that the command had launched a statewide community engagement initiative to appreciate residents for their cooperation and rebuild public confidence in the police.

He said the command remained committed to citizens’ welfare, prompt responses to complaints and respect for human rights.

Arrests, firearm recoveries

Mr Faniyan said police operatives had arrested suspects in separate operations across the state, including a 24-year-old man in Jos South Local Government Area from whom officers allegedly recovered a locally fabricated Beretta pistol, two rounds of 9mm ammunition and two double-edged daggers.

He also said operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit arrested two suspects during a routine patrol along the Anguldi-Vom Road and recovered locally fabricated firearms.

In another operation, the commissioner said a 24-year-old suspect was arrested in Bokkos over the alleged sexual assault of a 23-year-old woman while she was working on a farm.

He added that detectives arrested a 40-year-old man over the alleged rape of a nine-year-old girl.

The commissioner said police operatives also arrested a 23-year-old suspect at a hotel in Bassa Local Government Area following intelligence gathering.

He disclosed that four suspects were arrested during a raid in Angwan Rogo, where officers recovered a large quantity of dried leaves suspected to be cannabis and other substances suspected to be illicit drugs.

According to him, the command has sustained surveillance and raids on identified criminal hideouts and security flashpoints.

Mr Faniyan further said mobile police officers operating in Barkin Ladi engaged suspected bandits in a gunfight during an intelligence-led operation in the Kafi Abu area.

He added that police tactical operatives in Barkin Ladi sighted suspected illegal miners who abandoned their activities and fled into nearby bushes.

The commissioner said some of the arrested suspects had been charged to court, while investigations into other cases were ongoing.

He did not provide a breakdown of the arrests or specify how many suspects had been charged.

Police disburse ₦25.8 million to families of deceased officers

Mr Faniyan said the command had disbursed ₦25.82 million to 22 families of police officers who died in the line of duty.

He described the payment as part of efforts to support families of officers who died while serving the country.

READ ALSO: Nigeria condemns death of citizen in South African police custody

The commissioner attributed the state’s security efforts to cooperation between residents, security agencies and the Plateau State Government.

He said he had also engaged traditional rulers to strengthen collaboration between communities and security agencies.

Mr Faniyan reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting residents and visitors, adding that officers had been directed to respect citizens’ rights and uphold the rule of law.

World.title: Olympic Qualifier: Eguavoen speaks on Ajibade’s injury, hails Okpe after big win
World.content:
Super Falcons captain Rasheedat Ajibade will undergo an MRI scan to determine the extent of the injury she sustained during Nigeria’s emphatic 5-0 victory over Comoros in the second leg of their 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games qualifying tie.

The midfielder was forced off in the 23rd minute following a collision with a Comoros defender at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne, Ogun State, on Tuesday. Visibly in pain, Ajibade received medical attention before being stretchered off, with Folashade Ijamilusi coming on as her replacement.

The injury cast a shadow over an otherwise dominant evening for the Super Falcons, who secured a 7-0 aggregate victory to advance to the third round of the qualifiers, where they will face Morocco’s Atlas Lionesses.

Toni Payne and Uchenna Kanu both scored braces, while Christy Ucheibe converted a penalty as Nigeria completed the rout and strengthened their hopes of progressing further in the race for a place at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

However, the immediate concern after the final whistle was the condition of Ajibade, with interim coach Augustine Eguavoen confirming that the medical team would conduct further examinations before providing an official update on the Captain’s injury.

Speaking at his post-match press conference, Eguavoen admitted that he was yet to receive a definitive diagnosis but expressed hope that the injury would not be serious.

“On Ajibade, I have not heard anything,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I was with the medical team, and they said they are taking her to a hospital for an MRI to ascertain the degree of the injury.

“Hopefully, before we get back to the hotel, we will know. As soon as we have information, I am not the one to give it.

“The medical team will contact the head of media, and then you will get an update on Ajibade’s injury. Unfortunately, we lost Ajibade early in the game, but I think, and I hope and I pray, that the injury is very minute.”

Ajibade’s fitness will be a major concern for Nigeria as they prepare for a more demanding encounter against Morocco. The captain is an influential figure in the Super Falcons setup, and her availability could prove important as the team attempts to navigate the next stage of the Olympic qualifying campaign.

Eguavoen praises Super Falcons’ response against Comoros

Beyond the concern surrounding Ajibade, Eguavoen expressed satisfaction with the team’s performance, praising the players for translating their work on the training ground into an emphatic victory.

The Super Falcons had taken a 2-0 advantage into the second leg and completed the job with five unanswered goals, demonstrating their attacking quality and ability to maintain control of the tie.

For Eguavoen, who is currently serving as interim coach, the performance was particularly encouraging as he continues to work with the squad and establish his methods.

“Congratulations to Nigeria,” he said.

“The game today, I’m very pleased. I’m very, very happy. Congratulations to the girls; they made my day. I remember I kept begging them because I’m in a new terrain.

“We need everybody’s support. The response in training showed in the game.”

The coach also acknowledged the improvement shown by Comoros despite the heavy defeat, suggesting that the visitors approached the second leg with a different mentality after losing the first encounter 2-0.

“Yes, 5-0 today, the first leg was 0-2. I would say the Comoros team improved. Today, they improved and were beaten 5-0, so it’s a little bit tricky,” he added.

“I’m 100 per cent sure that they knew today they had nothing to lose, so they had to play. Congratulations to us, like I said, I’m very impressed with the team.”

Nigeria’s victory ensured a comfortable passage into the next round, but Eguavoen will know that the performance against Comoros is only one step in a longer qualifying campaign. Morocco are expected to provide a sterner test, making the Super Falcons’ preparations and the fitness of key players even more important.

Eguavoen backs Blessing Okpe after late Super Falcons Call-Up

Eguavoen also reserved praise for Blessing Okpe, whose performance strengthened her case for a more prominent role in the national team after earning a late invitation to the squad.

The coach revealed that Okpe was initially left out of the 28-player selection but was eventually called up after another player withdrew. He said he had questioned the omission of a forward who had been scoring regularly in the Belarusian league.

According to Eguavoen, a recommendation from someone who contacted him helped draw his attention to the player’s situation.

“On Okpe, I want to say a very big thank you to someone who called me. I got a call from—I won’t mention the name,” he said.

“Okpe was a late invitee. I was like, somebody scoring a lot of goals in the Belarus league and then she is not in the 28. I was like, that means you didn’t take your time.”

The coach added that even if he does not remain in charge of the Super Falcons, he intends to recommend Okpe to whoever takes over the team, citing the forward’s ability to make an impression despite her late arrival.

“Next game, hopefully, I am here. I know I am the Technical Director. If I don’t continue in this job, I will go back to my office.

“Then whoever becomes the coach, I will recommend Okpe. But luckily for Okpe, a player pulled out and she had a chance to come. I think she has proven that her late call-up was worth it.”

Okpe’s display will be encouraging for the forward, who has taken advantage of the opportunity to show what she can offer at senior international level. Her performance also gives Eguavoen another attacking option to consider as Nigeria prepare for the challenge of Morocco.

While the Super Falcons can celebrate a convincing aggregate victory and the emergence of additional attacking options, Ajibade’s injury remains the biggest concern from Tuesday’s encounter. The results of her MRI scan will determine the next steps as Nigeria turn their attention to the third round of the Olympic qualifiers.

World.title: Bauchi records 70 human trafficking cases, three convictions – NAPTIP
World.content:
The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) recorded 70 human trafficking cases in Bauchi State between January and October 2026, securing three convictions during the period.

The agency also rescued 25 indigenes of the state who were trafficked to North Africa, according to the state coordinator, Aliyun Kalli.

Mr Kalli disclosed the figures on Tuesday during a two-day review workshop on the Bauchi State Youth Policy Development Framework, organised by the state’s Sustainable Development Goals office with support from the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).

He said most of the victims were young people lured abroad with false promises of better opportunities.

Mr Kalli urged young people to take advantage of local skills acquisition programmes and other economic opportunities rather than risk dangerous journeys that could expose them to trafficking and exploitation.

He said three convictions had been secured from the 70 cases recorded during the period, while other cases remained before the courts.

The coordinator did not provide details of the convictions or specify how many of the remaining cases had been charged in court.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He added that NAPTIP was profiling returned migrants and working to reintegrate them into their communities.

Mr Kalli also disclosed that the agency was investigating local agents allegedly involved in recruiting young girls from rural communities for exploitation in urban centres.

He did not provide details of the alleged recruitment activities or disclose whether arrests had been made in connection with the investigations.

The coordinator said NAPTIP’s anti-trafficking efforts were built around five strategic pillars: prevention, protection, prosecution, partnership and policy.

He added that the agency had conducted awareness campaigns in more than 50 communities, motor parks and schools across Bauchi State in 2026.

The campaigns also included radio and television engagements, as well as outreach programmes targeting women’s groups.

Mr Kalli urged young people to remain patient and engage in productive activities, expressing optimism that ongoing government reforms would create more opportunities for them within the country.

World.title: El-Rufai planned to stifle EFCC investigation with $600,000 bribe, witness tells court
World.content:
A forensic investigator with the State Security Service (SSS) has alleged that former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai planned to bribe Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) officials and intermediaries with $600,000 to stifle an investigation.

Testifying on Tuesday as the first prosecution witness in the former governor’s trial before Justice Darius Khobo of the Kaduna State High Court in Kawo, Segun Kayode narrated how $500,000 and $100,000 were allegedly set aside for the illicit payments.

According to Channels Television, the witness informed the court that forensic audio recordings captured conversations between Mr El-Rufai and several suspected associates.

The alleged discussions focused on strategies to frustrate an EFCC investigation into a firm named Singularity.

Mr Kayode testified that those mentioned in the recordings included a senior advocate of Nigeria (SAN), another unnamed individual, and a son of the former governor, Bashir El-Rufai.

He alleged that the SAN and the associate were directed to obtain a template from one Ahmadu Sule—previously used to liquidate another firm—to apply to Singularity.

The witness further alleged that the discussions detailed plans to liquidate Singularity in both Nigeria and Mauritius, where the firm was reportedly under investigation by the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Additionally, the audio recordings contained plans to prevent the EFCC from investigating an undisclosed company listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

The allegations form part of the prosecution’s evidence against the former governor and have yet to be established by the court.

Tuesday’s trial proceedings spanned nearly eight hours, with roughly two hours dedicated to playing the recorded audio evidence.

Earlier in the session, lead defence counsel Paul Erokoro (SAN) objected to Mr Kayode’s testimony, arguing that the witness’s name and a summary of his evidence were omitted from the prosecution’s proof of evidence.

Mr Erokoro contended that this omission violated his client’s right to a fair hearing, emphasising that the defence was entitled to prior notice of the evidence it had to meet.

Countering the objection, lead counsel for the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Ayodeji Adedipe (SAN), explained that Mr Kayode was a subpoenaed witness, meaning the omission did not render his testimony inadmissible.

Citing judicial precedents, Mr Adedipe noted that the subpoena had been issued and signed by the court on 30 June, 2026, and that the defence would have full opportunity to cross-examine the witness.

In response, Mr Erokoro clarified that his objection centred on whether the defence had been given adequate notice to prepare, relying on Section 210 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Law, 2017, to argue that the prosecution was required to serve the subpoena on the defence.

In the ruling, Justice Khobo acknowledged the absence of the witness’s name and evidence summary in the proof of evidence but noted that court records confirmed he was subpoenaed.

The judge ruled that the omission did not automatically invalidate the testimony, provided the defence was granted the opportunity to cross-examine the witness.

Following the admission of Mr Kayode’s hard-copy findings into evidence as Exhibit 1, the defence raised further concerns regarding late service.

Justice Khobo ruled that the defence could obtain a Certified True Copy (CTC) of the document for detailed examination.

By consensus of both prosecution and defence teams, the court adjourned the case to 30 November and 1 December 2026, for the continuation of cross-examination.

Mr. El-Rufai arrived at the court under heavy security around 11:50 a.m., ahead of the scheduled noon hearing, accompanied by Isah Ashiru, the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Kaduna State.

His appearance followed an explicit order by Justice Khobo directing the ICPC to produce him in court.

The hearing took place days after the Court of Appeal in Kaduna dismissed Mr El-Rufai’s appeal challenging the High Court’s refusal to grant him bail.

In its 9 October judgement, the appellate court affirmed the lower court’s decision, ruling that the former governor failed to establish sufficient grounds for intervention.

Mr El-Rufai’s ongoing prosecution by the ICPC stems primarily from recommendations in a 2024 Kaduna State House of Assembly probe report that accused his 2015–2023 administration of mismanaging public funds.

The ICPC filed multiple charges against the former governor in federal and state courts, including one alleging that he tapped the phone of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu.

Mr El-Rufai has pleaded not guilty to all charges, maintaining that his prosecution is politically motivated.

He remains in ICPC custody under court-authorised remand orders while his legal team challenges his continued detention.

Mr El-Rufai has been in ICPC detention since 18 February.

World.title: Ondo govt orders river fumigation, emergency water supply in Igbokoda over military aircraft crash
World.content:
The Ondo State Government has ordered the fumigation of the river linked to the site where a military aircraft crashed last week in Igbokoda in Ilaje Local Government Area of the state.

The government also ordered the distribution of nose masks and other health kits to residents following complaints about a foul smell from the site of 5 October Nigerian Air Force (NAF) aircraft crash.

The intervention follows concerns among residents of Igbokoda over possible environmental contamination and health risks as search and recovery operations continue at the crash site.

In a statement on Wednesday by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Idowu Ajanaku, the state governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, directed the ministries of environment and health to begin extensive fumigation of the river following complaints about the offensive smell.

Mr Aiyedatiwa stated that the interventions are necessary as the river serves as an important source of livelihood for residents of Igbokoda and neighbouring communities.

The governor also directed the Ilaje Local Government Area to arrange water tankers to supply potable water to residents if assessments establish that the river is severely polluted and unsuitable for use.

The water supply arrangement, the statement said, would remain in place pending a lasting intervention to address any pollution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Aiyedatiwa, who hails from the local government area, also directed the relevant ministries to distribute nose masks and other essential health kits to residents as a precaution against potential health hazards.

The state government said it would continue to support the Nigerian Air Force’s evacuation efforts while prioritising the safety and welfare of residents in the affected community.

The NAF aircraft crash

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the NAF ATR 42 aircraft, identified as NAF 931, crashed into a swampy area of Igbokoda during a mission from Benin City, Edo State, to Lagos. The publication later confirmed that all the 25 people on board the aircraft including five crew members and 20 passengers died, according to NAF.

Recovery operations have been complicated by the swampy terrain and the aircraft’s submersion in the water.

Following the crash, the Ondo State Government deployed amphibious swamp machines to support the Nigerian Navy, the Air Force, emergency response agencies and local divers in accessing the site and retrieving the wreckage and victims’ remains.

Residents, however, have raised concerns about the increasingly offensive smell from the crash site, while the community’s monarch, Afolabi Odidiomo, has called on the federal and state governments to accelerate recovery efforts and address suspected contamination.

PREMIUM TIMES repeated on Tuesday that the Nigerian Air Force has also constituted a 12-member Aircraft Accident Investigation Board to investigate the circumstances surrounding the crash and recommend measures to prevent a recurrence.

World.title: Nigeria 5-0 Comoros: Five big takeaways as Super Falcons prepare for big Morocco test
World.content:
Nigeria’s Super Falcons took another confident step towards the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games after dismantling Comoros 5-0 on Tuesday to complete a 7-0 aggregate victory and advance to the third round of the qualifying campaign.

Two goals each from Toni Payne and Uchenna Kanu, alongside the no nonsense Christy Ucheibe’s successful penalty, ensured Nigeria finished the tie in emphatic fashion. But beyond the scoreline, the performance offered interim coach Augustine Eguavoen encouraging signs of a team beginning to rediscover its defensive solidity while exploring fresh possibilities in attack.

The Super Falcons were expected to overcome Comoros, particularly after establishing a two-goal advantage in the first leg. However, the manner in which they completed the job was important, especially for a side seeking to rebuild confidence and consistency following a disappointing 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations campaign.

Comoros had thrashed Sudan 30-0 on aggregate in the opening round of the qualifiers, but Nigeria exposed the considerable gulf in quality between the two sides, keeping clean sheets in both meetings and scoring seven unanswered goals.

The next assignment against Morocco will demand significantly more from the nine-time African champions. Before that potentially defining encounter, Premium Times examines five major takeaways from Nigeria’s victory, ranked by their importance to Eguavoen’s rebuilding project.

Super Falcons rediscover defensive steel ahead of Morocco showdown

For a team with ambitions of returning to the Olympic Games, defensive organisation will be just as important as attacking firepower. Nigeria’s two-legged victory over Comoros provided an encouraging indication that the Super Falcons may be finding greater stability at the back.

The Nigerians conceded no goals across both matches, recording consecutive clean sheets for the first time since the group stage of the 2024 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Although Comoros offered limited attacking threat, their impressive 30-0 aggregate demolition of Sudan in the previous round meant they could not be dismissed entirely. Nigeria, however, restricted their opponents and completed the tie without allowing them a route back into the contest.

Perhaps the most encouraging aspect was Eguavoen’s decision to trust a new centre-back partnership involving Shukurat Oladipo and Christy Ucheibe. The pair looked composed, mobile and complementary, showing a promising understanding of their defensive responsibilities.

Ucheibe’s contribution was particularly notable because she combined her defensive duties with a goal from the penalty spot, underlining her value at both ends of the pitch. Shukurat Oladipo put up a performance that reminded all why she was named the best defender in Italy last season.

The partnership still needs to be tested against opponents with greater technical quality and more sophisticated attacking movements. Nevertheless, Nigeria’s defensive display provides a useful foundation for the next round.

Morocco possess considerably more attacking quality than Comoros and are likely to ask harder questions of the Nigerian backline. If the Super Falcons can carry this organisation and concentration into that contest, they will give themselves a stronger chance of progressing.

Morocco test looms as Nigeria face their biggest qualifying challenge yet

The Super Falcons have completed the immediate task, but the real examination of Eguavoen’s side is approaching.

Nigeria will face Morocco in the third round after the Atlas Lionesses advanced following the withdrawal of the Republic of Congo from their second-round tie. The meeting promises to be a much more demanding contest, with progression in the Olympic qualifying campaign at stake.

Morocco have developed into one of Africa’s leading women’s football sides in recent years, making the fixture a significant test of Nigeria’s defensive discipline, midfield control and ability to convert attacking opportunities against stronger opposition.

There is, however, a source of confidence for the Super Falcons. Nigeria defeated Morocco 3-2 in the final of the 2024 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations, a result that demonstrated their capacity to withstand pressure and deliver when the stakes are high.

That victory will offer encouragement, but it should not be mistaken for a guarantee of success. The upcoming tie is a fresh contest, and Nigeria must show that they can reproduce their best football over two legs against an opponent capable of punishing defensive lapses.

The victory over Comoros has given Eguavoen room to assess his options and build momentum. The Morocco games will reveal whether the encouraging signs in the latest performance can translate into a result against elite continental opposition.

For Nigeria, the objective is no longer simply to score freely against a less experienced opponent. It is to demonstrate that the team can remain compact under pressure, compete in the decisive areas and produce the quality required to keep their Olympic dream alive.

Is Uchenna Kanu Super Falcons next Goalscoring Star?

Nigeria have never lacked outstanding goalscorers. From Mercy Akide and Perpetua Nkwocha to Asisat Oshoala, the Super Falcons have enjoyed generations of forwards capable of defining matches and carrying the weight of expectation.

But as Oshoala moves into the later stages of her career, Nigeria must continue identifying players who can shoulder the responsibility of leading the attack. Kanu’s performance against Comoros offered another reason to believe she can play a major role in that transition.

The forward scored twice in Tuesday’s encounter and finished the two-legged tie with three goals, strengthening her growing case as a dependable attacking option.

Kanu brings more than an eye for goal. Her strength allows her to compete physically with defenders, while her mobility gives Nigeria the flexibility to use her centrally or from wider attacking positions. She also showed an ability to remain involved in dangerous situations rather than relying solely on chances presented to her.

That variety could prove valuable against Morocco, where Nigeria may have fewer opportunities and will need their forwards to make the most of openings.

However, the next step is sustaining that effectiveness against higher-quality opposition. Goals against Comoros will provide confidence, but performances against Morocco would offer a more convincing indication of Kanu’s readiness to become one of Nigeria’s leading attacking figures.

With the Super Falcons searching for consistency and a reliable source of goals, Kanu has given Eguavoen another positive selection dilemma.

Michelle Alozie bounces back to remind Nigeria of her class

Michelle Alozie was arguably one of Nigeria’s standout performers across the two legs, delivering the kind of energetic and balanced display that could prove crucial in the more demanding rounds of the qualifiers.

Operating at right-back, Alozie covered the flank tirelessly, combining defensive responsibility with forward runs that gave Nigeria another route into attacking areas. Her work rate and willingness to contribute in both phases helped the Super Falcons maintain their threat while remaining organised.

Her performances were particularly encouraging after a difficult showing at the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations. The Comoros tie provided an opportunity to rebuild confidence, and Alozie took it by demonstrating the qualities that have made her a valuable member of the national team.

Modern full-backs are often required to do much more than defend their own penalty area. They must provide width, support attacks, recover quickly and make sound decisions when possession changes hands. Alozie showed encouraging signs in those areas over the two matches.

Her contribution will become even more important against Morocco, whose greater attacking quality should provide a sterner test of her defensive concentration. At the same time, Nigeria may need her forward runs to help stretch the opposition and create space for the attackers.

Toni Payne also deserves credit for her two-goal contribution on Tuesday, while Under 20 captain, Joy Igbokwe’s performance offered another encouraging sign of the options available to Eguavoen.

Alozie’s displays, however, stood out as a reminder that Nigeria’s progress will depend not only on their most celebrated attackers but also on players capable of delivering consistently across the pitch.

Ijamilusi, Okpe make strong claims for bigger Roles in Eguavoen’s Super Falcons

The depth of Nigeria’s attacking options was another positive to emerge from the victory, with substitutes Folashade Ijamilusi and Blessing Okpe making significant contributions after entering the contest.

Both players registered two assists, while Okpe also won the penalty that Ucheibe converted to complete the scoring. Their impact was reflected in the energy and directness they brought to Nigeria’s second-half performance.

Ijamilusi and Okpe used their pace, movement and willingness to run at opponents to give the Super Falcons additional attacking impetus. Rather than simply maintaining the tempo established by the starters, they helped add another dimension to Nigeria’s forward play.

Their performances will be welcome news for Eguavoen, particularly as the level of competition rises. Against stronger teams, the ability to change a game from the bench can be just as important as the quality of the starting XI.

Both players have operated on the fringes of the senior national team, making their contributions an opportunity to strengthen their cases for more prominent roles. Their involvement also suggests that Nigeria may have useful alternatives available when the preferred attacking combinations need fresh legs or a different approach.

Of course, the Comoros fixture is only one measure of their readiness. The challenge will be to maintain that energy and decision-making against opponents who defend more effectively and allow less space in the final third.

Still, their influence on Tuesday was difficult to ignore. In a qualifying campaign where squad depth could become decisive, Ijamilusi and Okpe have given Eguavoen more options to consider.

A convincing win, but a bigger challenge awaits

The Super Falcons have done what was required against Comoros, securing a comprehensive aggregate victory while recording consecutive clean sheets and giving several players the opportunity to strengthen their claims for regular places.

Kanu’s goals, Payne’s attacking contribution, Alozie’s all-round performance, the promising centre-back partnership and the impact of Ijamilusi and Okpe all provide reasons for optimism, apart from Captain Rasheedat’s injury which was the only blot in the game on the night.

Yet the significance of the result will ultimately be measured by what follows. Morocco represent a different level of opposition, and Nigeria will need to combine the attacking confidence displayed against Comoros with greater tactical discipline and resilience.

The Olympic qualifying campaign remains a demanding journey, but the Super Falcons have taken another step forward. Their next challenge is to prove that this emphatic victory was not simply a result of the gap in quality between the two sides, but evidence of a team building towards a more convincing and consistent future.

World.title: Peller announces planned livestream with Nobel Laureate Wole Soyinka
World.content:
Peller

Popular Nigerian streamer and content creator, Habeeb Hamzat, popularly known as Peller, has announced plans to host Nobel laureate Professor Wole Soyinka on his livestream, promising viewers a session filled with “proper English” and “grammar.”

Peller disclosed the plan during a livestream on Tuesday, saying he would announce further details about the proposed session at a later date.

“I want to do a stream with Mr. Wole Soyinka. I will announce it soon and tell you guys what the plan is. It will be a proper English day on that day. You will hear some ‘grammar’ that day,” he said.

The proposed collaboration has drawn attention because of the contrast between Peller’s humorous, informal streaming style and Soyinka’s reputation as one of Africa’s most distinguished literary figures.

Peller has built a large following through his livestreams, which often feature spontaneous conversations, humour and interactions with celebrities and other content creators.

Soyinka, meanwhile, is a renowned Nigerian playwright, poet and novelist who became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986.

The prospect of bringing the two personalities together has generated interest online, with the anticipated session expected to offer a different experience from Peller’s usual livestreams.

Although Peller said he would provide more information about the plan, no date for the proposed session was announced in his remarks.

It is also unclear whether Soyinka has accepted the invitation.

World.title: 2026 Ballon d’Or: How voting system works
World.content:
The 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony will hold in London on October 26, with an international jury of journalists set to determine the winners of the prestigious football awards.

According to the Ballon d’Or website, the jury for the men’s award comprises journalists from the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings, while representatives from the top 50 nations will vote for the women’s award.

The rankings in effect when the nominees were announced on September 8, 2026, will determine the countries represented on the jury.

Each juror will select 10 players from a 30-man shortlist, ranking them in order of merit. The players will receive points based on their positions, with 15 points awarded to the first choice, followed by 12, 10, eight, seven, five, four, three, two and one point.

The player with the highest overall score will win the award.

In the event of a tie, the winner will be determined by the number of first-place votes received. If the tie persists, second-place votes and subsequent rankings will be considered.

The organisers added that any other disputes arising from the voting process would be resolved by the editor-in-chief of France Football, the award’s organiser.

The October 26 ceremony will mark the 70th edition of the Ballon d’Or.

World.title: US judge backs CNN, MS Now, Politico access to White House
World.content:
CNN’s broadcast booth is seen in the press area of the White House in Washington, DC, September 18, 2026. Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP.

A federal judge blocked on Tuesday the White House from banning CNN, MS Now and Politico journalists, following President Donald Trump’s decision to ban the news outlets last month.

District Judge Timothy Kelly ruled that the Trump administration must grant the journalists access to the White House while the lawsuit filed by the three outlets against the ban proceeds.

Kelly said the outlets were “likely to succeed not only on their due process claim, but also on their two First Amendment claims.”

The First Amendment upholds the right to a free press.

Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House on September 18 for distributing what he called “fake news” and “fiction and lies.”

The three outlets filed a joint lawsuit seeking a preliminary injunction against the ban.

A court order temporarily restored the White House credentials of the journalists. That ban was set to expire Tuesday.

“The Court will extend the relief it already ordered, which will continue to preserve the status quo while this case proceeds,” Kelly wrote in an opinion accompanying Tuesday’s order.

“President Trump likely banned Plaintiffs from the White House because he believes that their reporting is generally inaccurate and biased against him,” Kelly added.

Trump has long attacked media that have aired critical coverage of him, repeatedly blasting the press as the “enemy of the people.”

AFP

World.title: 2027: Atiku urges Nigerians to collect PVCs, promises economic relief
World.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar

By Ayobami Okerinde

The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to make life more affordable and improve security across Nigeria, blaming President Bola Tinubu’s administration for the rising cost of living.

Atiku made the promise in a post on his official X account on Wednesday, while urging registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards ahead of the 2027 elections.

The former vice-president said Nigerians of different ages and economic backgrounds were grappling with financial hardship and insecurity.

“Parents go to bed worried about what they will feed their children tomorrow. Pensioners must choose between buying medicine and buying food. Young people work hard, yet transport, rent and basic needs consume what they earn,” Atiku said

“And across the country, families live with the fear of kidnapping, attacks and whether their loved ones will return home safely,” he added.

Atiku warned that Nigerians should not have to contend with hunger and insecurity at the same time, urging the country to prevent the current challenges from becoming the inheritance of future generations.

He called on eligible voters to collect and keep their PVCs, describing the cards as a means of exercising their democratic rights and seeking change through the ballot.

“If you are a registered voter, please go and collect your PVC. Hold on to it. It is your voice, your choice and your peaceful power to demand change,” he said.

Atiku also accused Tinubu’s administration of making life more expensive and pledged to reverse the trend if given the opportunity to govern.

“Bola made life expensive. I will work to make life affordable again and restore the security every Nigerian deserves,” he said.

“Let us stand together, across generations, and vote for a Nigeria where every family can live with dignity, safety and hope,” he added.

World.title: Nigerian man, Adebayo arrested in Canada after exposing self to three victims
World.content:
A Nigerian man has been arrested in Canada after allegedly exposing himself to three victims in separate incidents aboard Toronto’s public transit system.

The suspect, identified as Adebayo Maoli, 28, of Toronto, is facing one count of sexual assault and two counts of indecent act, according to the Toronto Police Service.

Police said the first incident occurred on September 1 at about 3 p.m. aboard a southbound Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) subway train at King Station.

The suspect allegedly exposed himself to two victims before leaving the train after they activated the security alarm.

In a separate incident on October 3, at approximately 12:10 a.m., the accused allegedly followed a person who had alighted from a subway train at College Station.

Investigators said both individuals boarded an escalator, where the suspect allegedly exposed himself to the victim.

“The victim verbally confronted the accused, who fled the area,” the Toronto Police Service said in a news release.

Maoli was subsequently arrested and charged in connection with the incidents.

He was scheduled to appear in bail court on October 9.

Police said they believe there may be additional victims and urged anyone with relevant information to contact the Toronto Police Service or Crime Stoppers anonymously.

The investigation is ongoing, and the allegations against the accused have not been tested in court.

World.content:
