World.title: 2027: No pathway for Peter Obi’s victory  -  APGA Chairman
World.content:
The National Chairman of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), Sly Ezeokenwa, has said there is no pathway to victory for the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, in the 2027 general election.

Ezeokenwa stated this during an interview on Arise Television’s The Morning Show on Wednesday, arguing that it was in the strategic interest of the South-East to align with President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.

He said APGA would work to persuade people in the region to support Tinubu rather than focus on projecting the number of votes Anambra State could deliver to the president.

“For me, it’s not about bandying about figures. It is about presenting our people with the fact, the truth, the bitter truth, as it were, that in this election — for me, I can say that as painful as it is — there is no pathway for the victory of our so-called brother (Peter Obi) in this election,” Ezeokenwa said.

He added that supporting Tinubu was the better strategic option for the Igbo people, stressing that it reflected APGA’s position ahead of the election.

“It is better in our strategic interest as Ndigbo for us to align with the aspiration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu currently. That is what APGA stands for. That is where APGA stands, and we are going to do everything possible to convince our people why they need to vote for the candidacy,” he said.

The APGA chairman’s remarks come amid political realignments ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo named as the coordinator for the state in Tinubu’s presidential campaign council.

Soludo, who is a member of APGA, has been among the prominent opposition figures whose roles in the campaign have drawn attention to the party’s position on the presidential contest.

Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, was the Labour Party’s presidential candidate in the 2023 election. He is now seeking the presidency under the NDC ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: Champions League: Can Anyone Stop PSG From Winning Three in a Row?
World.content:
Winning the Champions League requires an outstanding team, excellent coaching and a little luck at the right moments. Winning it twice? That proves the first victory was no accident.

Winning it three times in a row? Paris Saint-Germain would instantly have a claim to be one of the greatest teams in the competition’s modern history.

Is PSG Still the Standard?

There’s a reason that PSG are one of the favourites to win the Champions League at 6.50 with BetKing; they’re the consensus pick to retain their UCL title with only Barcelona (5.00) ranked above them.

Those odds reflect how close the leading contenders appear to be, but PSG still have the most important advantage: they know how to win the competition. Their recent success was built on overall team quality, but their attack separated them from everyone else. Last season, PSG created chances in different ways, could score from a variety of sources and introduce match-winners from the bench at will.

With an attacking core of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue and the recently signed trio of Mika Godts, Ferran Torres and Maghnes Akliouche, they have enough firepower to outscore just about anyone as they look to become just the second team to win the Champions League three times in a row.

Arsenal’s Missing Marquee Attacker

The Gunners are one of PSG’s closest challengers, but their summer business will be examined carefully if they fall short again.

With Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli departing the Emirates, the North Londoners had a three-man shortlist of marquee attackers they hoped to sign. Vinicius Jr. (who resigned with Real Madrid), Morgan Rodgers (who opted to join Chelsea) and Julian Alvarez (who Atleti simply refused to let go) were all admired by Mikel Arteta but couldn’t land. That decision may prove sensible if their existing forwards continue to deliver. If the goals start to dry up however, the chance to upgrade their attack could prove costly

Arsenal already possess the defence, midfield control, tactical organization and squad cohesion required to win the Champions League. Whether they have enough match-winners in attack remains the unresolved part of the equation.

Real Madrid’s European Heritage & Barcelona’s Firepower

Real Madrid can never be dismissed from this competition.

Other clubs may arrive in better form or with more balanced teams, but Madrid possess a relationship with the Champions League that regularly defies conventional analysis.

Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Jr are household names who guarantee goals, while Jose Mourinho has been brought in to manage this star-studded squad. Can the Portuguese legend refind his old magic? We’ll see.

Elsewhere in Spain, Barcelona are chomping at the bit to win a sixth UCL title and will believe that this is their season after an electric start to the season. Despite missing out on primary attacking target, Julian Alvarez, the Catalan side has faced few issues in attack with 31 goals scored in the La Liga and just seven conceded (in 7 games).

The UCL is a different proposition than the La Liga, but Real Madrid and Barcelona are priced at 8.00 and 5.00 respectively to win the coveted trophy with BetKing.

The Difficulty of Winning Three

PSG began the campaign as favourites, but winning three consecutive Champions Leagues is extraordinarily difficult. Injuries, suspensions, an unfortunate draw or one poor away performance can undo an entire season. Their opponents have also spent the summer studying the system that conquered Europe twice.

PSG and Barcelona appear to have the best attack. Arsenal and Real Madrid are right behind them, two teams nobody wants to face when the knockout rounds begin. Then, of course, we have Manchester City and Bayern Munich who have two of the most lethal strikers in the world in Erling Haaland and Harry Kane.

For now, the champions deserve their position at the top of the market. Will they remain there until the final? We’re about to find out over the course of an exciting season!

World.title: Alleged Attack: Sowore Files N5bn Damages Suit against AGF, DSS
World.content:
The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has instituted a N5 billion fundamental rights enforcement suit against the Department of State Services (DSS), its Director-General, Tosin Ajayi, the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF), and a Deputy Director of the DSS, Benjamin Bulus, over an alleged violent attack and abduction carried out by armed, hooded DSS operatives within the premises of the Federal High Court in Abuja on 22 June 2026.

The suit, filed on October 13, 2026 and marked: FHC/ABJ/CS/2480/2026, challenges the legality of the DSS operation and seeks judicial redress for violations of Sowore’s constitutionally guaranteed rights to human dignity and personal liberty.

The legal action was based on the plaintiff’s claim that DSS operatives, acting outside the scope of a judicial remand order, violently attacked him within the Federal High Court complex and forcibly transported him in elevators reserved for Federal High Court judges to the basement of the building against his will, injuring him in the process of the violent attack.

According to a statement by Sowore’s lawyer, Mr Peter Femi Joseph, following an order by Justice Mohammed Umar of the Federal High Court, on June 22, 2026, directing Sowore’s remand at the Kuje Correctional Centre pending the hearing and determination of his application seeking a stay of the order revoking his bail and the bench warrant issued against him, operatives of the agency including armed men and women wearing hoods, stormed the fourth floor of the Federal High Court building in a bid to arrest him.

The statement further claimed that operatives descended on Sowore, physically assaulted him, and forcibly removed him from the area before transporting him against his will to the basement of the court complex.

Sowore maintained that he had committed no offence warranting such an operation and that the DSS had no lawful authority to assault, abduct, intimidate, or subject him to degrading treatment within the premises of a court of law.

He further contended that the operation was intended to intimidate and harm him, notwithstanding the existence of a judicial order specifying the lawful process for his remand.

The suit identifies Tosin Ajayi, the DG of the DSS and Benjamin Bulus, a Deputy Director and operative of the DSS, as the officer who led the operation.

Meanwhile, video evidence of the alleged attack, which the plaintiff disclosed was captured with Ray-Ban Meta Smart Glasses, forms part of evidence to be presented as evidence in proof of Sowore’s case.

The suit invokes Sections 34 and 35 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), which guarantee the rights to dignity of the human person and personal liberty.

The Applicant contended that the alleged physical assault, forcible removal, intimidation, and false detention constituted violations of these fundamental rights.

He also seeks to establish the respective legal responsibilities of the DSS, its Director-General, the Attorney-General of the Federation, and Benjamin Bulus for the misconduct.

Sowore is asking the Federal High Court to award him N5 billion in aggravated damages over the alleged assault, abduction, humiliation, intimidation, and infringement of his constitutionally protected rights.

He is also seeking declarations concerning the alleged unlawfulness of the conduct complained of, appropriate injunctive and consequential orders, and any further relief the court considers justified.

Kano Committed to High-impact Health Research, Says KIRCT

Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano

The Kano Independent Research Centre Trust (KIRCT) has disclosed that it will continue to provide high-impact services and cutting-edge research outcomes capable of addressing existing and emerging health challenges in Kano, Nigeria, and beyond.

The Chairman, Board of Trustees (BoT) of the Centre, Prof. Aliyu Abdu, disclosed this at the opening ceremony of the Advanced Bioinformatics Workshop organised by KIRCT in Kano yesterday.

He said KIRCT is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities to enable scientists to conduct advanced research locally without travelling abroad, adding that its researchers are currently working on several health areas, including genomics, breast cancer, antimicrobial resistance, vaccines and others.

Prof. Abdu noted that the Centre has also established mutually beneficial collaborations with research institutions within and outside the region, with plans to expand globally.

According to him, the training covered young scientists to conduct impactful research,s which is one of the mandates of the Centre.

He commended the diversity of the workshop participants, especially with regard to gender distribution, and urged the participants to apply the knowledge to be gained from the workshop for the benefit of humanity.

He thanked the funders of the Centre, Pfizer Inc. and the Kano State Government, for their support, and lauded the board and management of the Centre for the progress it recorded.

In his remarks, the Special Adviser to the Kano State Governor on Health Services and member of the Board of Trustees, Dr. Ibrahim Musa Idris, reaffirmed the state government’s support for the Centre.

He said the administration of Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf is pleased with the Centre’s impressive progress, expressing optimism that the Centre will soon be on the global map for providing innovative health solutions.

World.title: Prospera Finance Wins ‘Fastest Growing Finance Company’ Award
World.content:
Prospera Finance Limited has been awarded the ‘Fastest Growing Finance Company of the Year’ at the BusinessDay Banks and Other Financial Institutions (BAFI) Awards in recognition of the company’s impressive market trajectory, financial innovation, and commitment to excellence.

According to a statement, the award highlights Prospera Finance’s rapid expansion, robust operational performance, and customer-centric financial solutions in an evolving macroeconomic landscape.

Under the leadership of its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Joshua Obinna Umesegha, Prospera Finance Limited has built a reputation for delivering tailored, accessible financial products that empower individuals, small and medium scale enterprises (SMEs), and corporate organisations across Nigeria.

Receiving the award on behalf of the company, the leadership team expressed gratitude to its clients, partners, and employees, noting that the recognition serves as validation of the firm’s strategic vision and execution over the past year.

Speaking on the milestone, Umesegha described the win as a testament to the hard work and resilience of the entire Prospera Finance team, as well as the trust reposed in the firm by its growing client base.

“Winning the ‘Fastest Growing Finance Company of the Year’ at the BAFI Awards is a profound honor for all of us at Prospera Finance Limited,” Umesegha said. “This award reflects our relentless drive to innovate, deepen financial access, and create sustainable value for our stakeholders. As we look ahead, we remain committed to pioneering solutions that drive economic growth and support the financial goals of our clients.”

The BusinessDay BAFI Awards, widely regarded as the benchmark of institutional excellence in Nigeria’s financial sector, employs a rigorous audit and selection process to evaluate institutions based on financial growth, market innovation, corporate governance, and service quality.

Prospera Finance’s recognition as the fastest-growing operator underscores its rising prominence in the non-bank financial services space, positioning it for continued market leadership in the years ahead.

World.title: Austin Albert Makes History With Dubai Real Estate Award
World.content:
Nigerian real estate entrepreneur, Austin Ugochukwu Albert, has made a mark in Dubai’s property market, becoming the first Nigerian to receive the second-highest global sales ranking award from Dubai-based real estate developer, Binghatti Properties.

The recognition, received on behalf of his firm, Loft & Keys Properties, highlights the company’s performance in the competitive international property market.

Dubai has emerged as a major destination for international property investors, attracting buyers with its diverse real estate offerings, luxury developments and investment opportunities.

Operating in this competitive market requires industry knowledge, strong business relationships and the ability to navigate changing investment demands.

For Albert, the latest recognition represents a significant milestone for his company and its activities in Dubai’s real estate sector.

Albert described the award as a hard-earned achievement, acknowledging the challenges his company had to overcome before receiving the recognition from one of Dubai’s prominent property developers.

He also expressed gratitude to God for what he described as a significant moment in his business journey.

“You may not understand how many battles we’ve had to fight to win this recognition by one of Dubai’s biggest and best real estate developers, Binghatti Properties. God is truly great,” he said.

Loft & Keys Properties operates in real estate and global mobility, positioning itself within a market that connects property investment with international business and relocation opportunities.

The award also draws attention to the participation of Nigerian entrepreneurs in the global property industry, where firms compete for visibility, sales performance and recognition from established developers.

For Albert, the achievement marks a new milestone for his company as it continues to pursue opportunities in Dubai’s dynamic real estate market.

However, the award’s significance extends beyond individual recognition, reflecting the opportunities available to Nigerian businesses seeking to expand their presence in international markets.

As Nigerian entrepreneurs continue to explore investment opportunities beyond the country’s borders, Austin Albert’s recognition by Binghatti Properties adds another chapter to the growing story of Nigerian participation in Dubai’s real estate sector.

World.title: IMF Warns Nigeria Against Restoring Petrol Subsidy
World.content:
Peter Uzoho

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has advised Nigeria against restoring broad petrol subsidy, recommending targeted support for vulnerable households to cushion the impact of rising energy costs.

IMF said blanket petrol subsidies were expensive, often benefited higher-income consumers disproportionately and could worsen fiscal pressures amid rising borrowing costs.

Director of the IMF’s Fiscal Affairs Department, Rodrigo Valdés, gave the warning Wednesday during a press briefing on the fund’s fiscal monitor at the 2026 annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand.

His comments followed a question on how the fund could recommend allowing energy prices to reflect scarcity when higher fuel prices in Nigeria could raise transport costs, worsen inflation and deepen poverty, particularly when the government was facing calls to restore petrol subsidy ahead of an election year.

“Protecting people is not the same as protecting the price of fuels,” Valdés said.

He said fuel subsidies or measures preventing prices from adjusting fully to an energy shock had cost countries between 1 percent and 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026.

“It’s first fiscally very costly, and second, if you look at the pattern of consumption, it’s easy to see that that subsidy is readily regressive in many places,” he said.

Valdés said governments should instead use social safety nets and household data to identify people who need assistance.

“There are better tools to deal with this,” he said.

The federal government recently announced a 30-day petrol discount at Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited retail stations, with priority for public transport operators, to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices.

Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, said NNPC retail would sell petrol at cost by foregoing its retail profit margin, describing the measure as temporary relief rather than a return to petrol subsidy.

The government also proposed negotiating a ceiling of N1,350 per litre on petrol’s ex-gantry or landing cost, subject to monthly reviews

The IMF also recommended targeted interventions to cushion the effect of higher fuel prices on transportation costs.

A division chief in the fund’s fiscal affairs department, Davide Furceri, said governments could redirect some of the resources spent on blanket subsidies towards vulnerable consumers.

“For example, you mentioned transportation costs. Yeah, gasoline could go up, and perhaps bus fees may be subsidised in a way that is a much better policy at the end of the day than just a blanket subsidy for everybody,” Furceri said.

He also suggested alternatives such as school feeding programmes, geographical targeting and assistance for vulnerable farmers.

Furceri acknowledged that some countries lacked household registries and digital payment systems needed to deliver targeted support effectively.

However, he said governments could adopt alternative approaches in the short term while developing stronger systems.

He recommended that assistance should be limited, targeted and temporary.

Valdés explained that fuel subsidies could worsen global energy pressures by preventing demand from adjusting when supplies were constrained.

“When you subsidise, you don’t allow, at the end of the day, demand to adjust,” he said.

“And reality is that we have less fuels in the world economy. That means that someone else has to adjust more, and the market produces a higher price for that.”

The IMF official said subsidies were not only costly and regressive but could also have spillover effects on the global economy.

World.title: AG Mortgage Bank Appoints Chieduzie Ogbuehi as  Company Secretary
World.content:
AG Mortgage Bank Plc has announced the appointment of Chieduzie Ogbuehi, as its substantive Company Secretary, effective from September 24, 2026.

Chieduzie is a corporate services executive and legal professional with over 15 years of experience advising Boards and executive management on personnel management, legal, regulatory and dispute resolution matters.

According to a statement, his appointment further strengthens AG Mortgage Bank Plc’s commitment to sound corporate governance, regulatory compliance and effective institutional management as the Bank continues to advance its position in Nigeria’s mortgage and housing finance sector.

Prior to joining AG Mortgage Bank Plc, Chieduzie held leadership roles including Head of Corporate Services at James Cubitt, where he headed the Human Resources, Legal and Company Secretariat functions. Before then, he served as the Head of Corporate and Commercial Transactions at Canaan Partners. He began his mortgage Banking journey as a Legal Officer at Haggai Mortgage Bank Limited.

Chieduzie is a member of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Associate of the Chartered Institute of Secretaries and Administrators, Nigeria (ACIS), Associate of the Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria (ACTI), Fellow of the Institute of Credit Administration (FICA), Member of the Nigerian Institute of Chartered Arbitrators (MCArb), and is registered with the Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria (FRCN).

As substantive Company Secretary, Chieduzie will continue to support AG Mortgage Bank Plc’s commitment to strong corporate governance, regulatory compliance and effective Board and management processes, while contributing to the Bank’s continued growth and institutional development.

World.title: Marwa Canvasses Prioritisation of Mental Health By FG
World.content:
*Says NDLEA rehabilitated 53,800 In 5 Years

Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

Chairman of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), Brig. Gen. Mohammed Buba Marwa (rtd), has urged the Federal Government to prioritise mental health funding, personnel and community-led interventions.

Against the background growing concerns about drug abuse and mental health cases, Marwa said that over 53,800 persons have been rehabilitated through the agency’s facilities in the last five years.

Marwa spoke in Abuja on Monday while chairing The Conversation Conference (TCC) 5.0 organised by Intersect Consortium to mark World Mental Health Month.

He said he chaired the first edition in 2022 and has watched it grow into one of Nigeria’s largest gatherings on mental health, commending the consortium led by Dr. Vincent Udenze and its Chairperson, Hajiya Ammuna Lawan Ali.

“For too long, we treated mental health as a private burden, hiding behind shame and silence. In my work at NDLEA, I see the cost of that silence daily,” Marwa said.

He said behind many drug abuse cases is untreated pain, depression and trauma.

“A young person who found substance before finding help. Drug use and mental illness feed each other. If we only arrest symptoms, we will keep missing the cause,” he warned.

Marwa said the conference theme – strategic investments, partnerships and community-led action – reflects NDLEA’s approach.

He said mental well-being cannot thrive where hopelessness and poverty drive people into harm. In three pilot communities, NDLEA worked with residents to build legitimate livelihoods for families who once depended on illicit drug cultivation, with plans to scale to other geopolitical zones.

“When people have hope, income and a stake in their future, stress eases, families stabilise and communities grow resilient. These were solutions designed for communities, not imposed on them,” he said.

On prevention, Marwa cited the War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) campaign reaching young people in schools and campuses early and without judgment, and the agency’s 24/7 toll-free helpline where a frightened teenager or worried mother can be heard at no cost.

“Over 53,800 persons have passed through our rehabilitation facilities across Nigeria in the last five years. Behind that number are parents and kids who return to families and people who return to school and work,” he said.

He lamented that media focuses on arrests, seizures and forfeited assets, not on counselling and rehabilitation.

Marwa said mental health financing must be at the centre of national planning.

“Mental health cannot remain the poorest relation in our health budget. Every naira spent on prevention, trained personnel and accessible treatment returns to us in productivity, safer communities and stronger families,” he said.

He called for more psychiatrists, psychologists, counsellors, community health workers and integration of mental health into primary healthcare so that no one travels hundreds of kilometres to get help.

“Financing must also be equitable. Care that only the well-off can afford is not a system, but a privilege,” he added.

He said focus on women and children was right. Women carry unseen load of families, often suffering in silence and surviving violence, including displaced mothers and girls with no one to turn to. Children absorb stress of homes long before they can name it.

“The same is true of persons living with disabilities and families displaced by conflict. A system that does not treat them is not yet inclusive,” he said, noting that when mother, child and household are supported together, recovery lasts longer.

Marwa said no single ministry can handle it alone, urging synergy among health, education, security, justice and social welfare ministries.

Earlier, Hajiya Ammuna Lawan Ali said TCC grew from a single-day gathering into a movement, now in its fifth edition. She said this year’s edition asks what conversations must lead to.

“Mental health does not begin in a hospital. It begins in the home, the school, the workplace and community. That is where people experience stress, loneliness, trauma and exclusion. It is also where support and early intervention can begin,” she said.

She urged strengthening of trusted first contacts – family members, teachers, religious leaders, community leaders, primary health workers – and connecting them to professional services.

Managing Director of Intersect Consortium, Dr. Vincent Udenze, shared story of Elizabeth, a mother from Kwara State who produced a first-class graduate but was found stark naked on the street, her luggage stolen, people throwing things at her.

He said he gave her food and took her to his facility where she was treated and regained her health.

Marwa urged participants to commit to financing what works, scaling proven community models, putting women, children and vulnerable first and making help-seeking an act of courage.

“Let TCC 5.0 mark renewed commitment so that mental health becomes integral part of national development agenda and access to quality care is reality for all, not privilege for few,” he said.

World.title: 2027: CSOs, Nigerians Told To Hold Politicians Accountable
World.content:
Nigeria Forward, a socio-political group, has urged civil society organisations and Nigerians to hold politicians accountable for their statements and actions ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The group warned against hate speech, personality attacks and fake news, saying such practices could deepen divisions in the country.

Its Co-Convener, Comrade Ibrahim Abdullahi Waiya, PhD, made the call in a statement issued on Tuesday.

The statement followed the commencement of public political campaigns by candidates and political parties.

Nigeria Forward expressed concern over what it described as the growing use of character assassination and campaign of calumny by political actors.

It urged candidates to focus on policies, manifestoes and programmes that would help voters make informed decisions.

The group also condemned the alleged misuse of digital platforms to spread misinformation and hate speech for political advantage.

It said political ambition should be pursued with decency, mutual respect and patriotism.

“Our politicians must take a cue from their contemporaries in the advanced and developed democracies, where electioneering campaigns are based on issues, manifestoes, policies and programmes that are intended to be implemented for the benefit of the electorates,” the statement read.

The group urged politicians to avoid inflammatory statements capable of threatening national unity and peaceful coexistence.

It also called on civil society organisations, corporate bodies and well-meaning Nigerians to scrutinise politicians’ conduct and hold them responsible for divisive remarks.

Nigeria Forward said the 2027 campaigns should promote issue-based debates rather than personal attacks.

It added that responsible political engagement was necessary to sustain peace, unity and development in the country.

World.title: Cat Matlala STAYS behind bars after surprise bail decision
World.content:
Vusimusi ‘Cat’ Matlala (second from right) appeared alongside his co-accused in the Pretoria Magistrate’s Court. He has provisionally abandoned his bail application in a R95 000-a-month luxury property fraud case. Image: National Prosecuting Authority (NPA)

Controversial businessman Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala has provisionally abandoned his bail application in a fraud case involving a R95 000-a-month luxury home in Pretoria.

Matlala appeared in the Pretoria Magistrate’s Court on Wednesday, 14 October, alongside his wife, Tsakane, and two co-accused.

His legal team informed the court that he would not proceed with his bail application at this stage.



Matlala will remain behind bars as he faces separate attempted murder charges.

WHY DID CAT MATLALA ABANDON HIS BAIL APPLICATION?

Matlala had planned to apply for bail this week, but his lawyers told the court that he would first deal with his separate attempted murder case.

His legal team indicated that he could revive the bail application at a later stage.

The State had planned to oppose his release.

Matlala also faces criminal proceedings linked to alleged attacks involving actress Tebogo Thobejane, taxi boss Joe Sibanyoni and DJ Vettys.

R95 000 LUXURY HOME AT CENTRE OF FRAUD CASE

Prosecutors accuse Matlala, his wife and two others of using fraudulent documents to secure a luxury rental property in Waterkloof Heights, Pretoria.



The State alleges that the accused submitted false information to an estate agency in January 2025 to obtain a lease for the property.

The house carried a monthly rental of R95 000.

Prosecutors also allege that Matlala used an identity document bearing the name Vusimuzi Dlamini and falsely claimed links to the Eswatini royal family.

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) previously outlined how Matlala allegedly used the identity to convince the estate agency that he could afford the rental.

“He portrayed himself as a member of the royal family so that he can be able to prove to the estate agency that he would have funds to pay for the property,” NPA spokesperson Lumka Mahanjana said.

Matlala faces charges of fraud, forgery, uttering and contravening the Identification Act.

His wife, Tsakane, and co-accused Claudette Masethe and Given Makofane also face fraud-related charges.

MATLALA REMAINS BEHIND BARS

The Pretoria Magistrate’s Court previously granted Matlala’s wife and the two co-accused bail of R20 000 each.

The court ordered them to surrender their passports, report to police and avoid contact with State witnesses.

Matlala remains in custody at Kgosi Mampuru II Correctional Centre.

The court postponed the fraud case to 29 October for further investigation.

Matlala and his co-accused have not been convicted of the charges.

World.title: Pensioners still using the green ID book should know this before the cut-off
World.content:
SASSA pensioners aged 60 and older can replace their green barcoded ID book with a smart ID card free of charge at Home Affairs, according to the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) official requirements guide. Other citizens applying for the same card pay R140.

The switch is becoming urgent. The DHA is preparing to announce a roadmap for phasing out the green ID book, which is still used by around 16 million people, according to Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber.

What pensioners must bring

The DHA lists four documents for pensioners applying for their first smart ID. Applicants need their green barcoded ID book, or an affidavit if the book has been lost. They also need proof of residence, or they can simply provide a residential address if they do not have proof.



Married pensioners must bring a marriage certificate, and divorced pensioners must bring their divorce decree. Home Affairs uses these documents to verify marital status, so pensioners whose circumstances have changed should bring the paperwork to avoid delays.

Why the green ID book is on its way out

The minister has warned that the green ID book is particularly vulnerable to fraud. For grant recipients, this matters because SASSA relies on a valid identity document to confirm who is receiving payments.

However, there is no need to panic yet. No official cut-off date has been announced, and Home Affairs has stressed that green ID books remain legal and valid for now. The department has said the green ID book will only be phased out once smart ID access becomes widely available.



Help for elderly and rural pensioners

Long queues and travel costs remain a concern for many older South Africans. In April 2026, a Member of Parliament asked the minister how elderly citizens in rural areas would cope. The DHA replied that it is mindful of the challenges some elderly citizens may face and pointed to the rollout of smart ID services at hundreds more bank branches.

Schreiber said access to smart ID services increased by 250% in just 19 weeks through the bank partnership. Home Affairs planning documents also mention mobile offices and home visits to help citizens who cannot travel.

Pensioners who use a bank branch should confirm whether any fee applies before paying, as the free pensioner category is listed in the DHA brochure. Applying early also means avoiding the rush that is likely to follow once Home Affairs announces a final cut-off date.

World.title: If Lebohang Maboe is your best player, you have some serious problems
World.content:
Lebohang Maboe is now Kaizer Chiefs’ primary playmaker. He missed their 1-1 stalemate with Stellies, and there’s no return in sight.

Maboe misses Kaizer Chiefs match, Chiefs miss Maboe

Lebohang Maboe missed Kaizer Chiefs’ 1-1 draw with Stellenbosch, and it showed. Coach Fernando Da Cruz opted for a back four and a double midfield pivot of Reeve Frosler and Sibongiseni Mthethwa. Although Frosler assisted Mdu Shabalala’s goal, Frosler is a square peg in a round hole and not a long-term option for that role. Chiefs’ regular engine room partnership of Siphesihle Ndlovu and Maboe has been obliterated because of injuries to both players. Maboe has two goals and two assists this season in the league. Without him, they look devoid of creativity. At 32, Maboe is hardly a spring chicken, so what’s the alternative?

The dust settles on another stalemate for Chiefs

A 1-1 draw isn’t the worst result in the world, but Chiefs have now drawn five of their last six Betway Premiership outings and not beaten Stellies in any of their last four H2Hs, a sequence that includes three defeats. They trail champions Orlando Pirates by eight points after just eight matches of the new campaign. Last night, coach Fernando Da Cruz fell ill and had to be attended to by doctors. Next up is a two-legged CAF Confed Cup clash with Red Arrows. Chiefs fans have to wait until 31 October for their next Betway Premiership assignment, and it’s against Orlando Pirates of all people.

World.title: Springbok Bongi Mbonambi remains iced out of Sharks squad

Bongi Mbonambi has found himself in limbo with the Sharks and Springboks of late. Image: Facebook

World.title: Pensioners are exiting this suburb as crime and property prices skyrocket
World.content:
Cape Town’s property market has been celebrating a price boom.

But the city’s pensioners are an unexpected casualty of these price rises.

However, in one suburb, it’s becoming more expensive and more dangerous.



Pensioners are being forced out of this Cape Town suburb

Mature residents who’ve spent decades in the city can’t afford to live comfortably.

It’s a tale as old as Cape Town’s frenzied property market: developers come in, drive up prices; lifelong residents are often forced to move out.

But Table View differs from other property hotspots in that crime is also increasing.



According to first-quarter statistics from the South African Police Service (SAPS), crime is up 5.7% compared to the same period last year.

Annually, crime is up 9.2%.

Theft and commercial crimes are the two most commonly reported crimes in the police precinct.



But drug-related crime makes up about 10% of all reported crime in the region.

The Table View police precinct includes Blouberg, Parklands, Sunningdale, Flamingo Vlei and surrounding areas.

And in each of these suburbs there’s been a tremendous increase in property values.



Across the precinct, the average property sale price is up 25%, crossing R2 million for the first time in the precinct’s history.

By the end of 2025, those over 65 made up a little less than one third of sellers and less than one fifth of owners.

They also made up the smallest share of buyers in the region.



Table View Pensioner Community

But the Table View community hasn’t abandoned its mature population.

Table Bay Mall is the only mall of its size in the city with a dedicated pensioners’ day. This takes place every Wednesday.

In nearby Sandown, for example, the local Spar has a pensioners’ day every Tuesday, where pensioners can get special discounts.



The community is rallying behind pensioners.

Facebook groups like the Living Legends Table View Seniors Club also host free and affordable events to keep the suburb’s seniors engaged.

World.title: R300m drug bust: Key Madlanga Commission witness DIES
World.content:
Gauteng Traffic Police Chief Inspector Samuel Mashaba has died months after facing tough questions at the Madlanga Commission over a R300 million cocaine bust. He was on precautionary suspension at the time of his death. Image: X

Gauteng Traffic Police Chief Inspector Samuel Mashaba, who faced intense questioning over a R300 million cocaine bust at the Madlanga Commission, has died.

Mashaba died at Milpark Hospital in Johannesburg on Tuesday, 13 October, while on precautionary suspension following his testimony before the commission.

The Gauteng government confirmed his death but has not disclosed the cause.



His death comes four months after commissioners questioned him about his involvement in the seizure of more than 715kg of cocaine and his financial relationship with an alleged police informant.

R300 MILLION COCAINE BUST UNDER SCRUTINY

Mashaba testified in June about a July 2021 police operation at a Scania warehouse in Aeroton, south of Johannesburg.

Officers seized cocaine worth approximately R300 million after the shipment reportedly entered South Africa through Durban Harbour.

However, the commission questioned Mashaba about how he obtained information about the shipment and why he had not reported the intelligence through the required police channels.

Commissioners also scrutinised his relationship with businessman Tumelo Nku, who allegedly provided information about the drugs.

Mashaba acknowledged receiving money from Nku but insisted the payments were loans or financial assistance from a friend.



He denied any wrongdoing.

Commission chairperson Justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga challenged his version during questioning.

“You are being untruthful,” Madlanga told Mashaba.

The testimony raised questions about Mashaba’s conduct and his dealings with individuals connected to the operation.

MASHABA SUSPENDED AFTER TESTIMONY

The Gauteng government subsequently suspended Mashaba as authorities investigated possible misconduct.

The investigation focused on alleged breaches of departmental policies, the possible misuse of state resources and his financial dealings.

Officials ordered Mashaba to surrender government-issued equipment, including firearms, cellphones and laptops.

They also barred him from entering government premises and contacting certain employees while the investigation continued.

Authorities had not publicly announced the outcome of the disciplinary process before his death.

LESUFI CONFIRMS MASHABA’S DEATH

Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi extended condolences to Mashaba’s family and colleagues.

“On behalf of the Gauteng Provincial Government, I wish to convey our deepest condolences to the Mashaba family following the passing of Chief Inspector Samuel Mashaba,” Lesufi said.

“We also extend our condolences to his colleagues in the Gauteng Traffic Police and the broader law enforcement fraternity, who are mourning the loss of a colleague.”

MEDIA STATEMENT | The @GautengProvince, through the @GP_CommSafety, announces with deep sadness the passing of Gauteng Traffic Police Chief Inspector Samuel Mashaba, who passed away today, 13 October 2026,

at Milpark Hospital while receiving medical care. pic.twitter.com/iizKwLpoQU — Gauteng Provincial Gov (@GautengProvince) October 13, 2026

The government has not disclosed what caused Mashaba’s death.

There is no verified evidence linking his death to the cocaine investigation, his suspension or his testimony before the Madlanga Commission.

World.title: Pirates match appears on FNB Stadium big screen during Chiefs game [VIDEO]
Missing Gqeberha teen Allegra Styles found after five-day search
World.content:
Allegra Styles and her boyfriend Brent Naidoo were located by police this week. Images via Facebook

Missing Gqeberha teen Allegra Styles has been found safe and unharmed after a five-day search. The 14-year-old and her 25-year-old boyfriend, Brent Naidoo, were located on Tuesday, 13 October.

Allegra disappeared last Thursday after attending a party. She is believed to have had an altercation with her boyfriend.

MISSING TEEN ALLEGRA STYLES AND BOYFRIEND FOUND

Police have confirmed that missing teen Allegra Styles was found safe and unharmed in Middle Street in North End on Tuesday, 12 October. Her boyfriend, Brent Naidoo, was also located.



As the case involves a minor, Eastern Cape police spokesperson Captain Sandra Janse van Rensburg could not share additional information about the couple or the circumstances of their disappearance.

The SAPS’s Family Violence, Child Protection and Sexual Offences (FCS) Unit is investigating the case.

Last Thursday, Allegra Styles was last seen after she allegedly went to a party in Kamma Park after an altercation with her boyfriend, Brent Naidoo. She was reported missing over the weekend.



Police appealed to the public for information about her whereabouts and specifically for assistance from Naidoo.

#sapsEC [UPDATE: MISSING TEENAGER FOUND IN GQEBERHA] The #sapsFCS Unit in Gqeberha can confirm that, during the course of the investigation, they were able the trace Allegra Styles whereabouts as well as her boyfriend.



Members immediately followed up and located the missing… https://t.co/GjkSCIio3o pic.twitter.com/h2usEVzN2K — SA Police Service 🇿🇦 (@SAPoliceService) October 13, 2026

MISSING CHILDREN IN SOUTH AFRICA

According to figures by the SAPS Missing Persons Bureau, around 1,700 underage children are reported missing each year, over 10 years.



Last year, SAPS revealed that 17 968 missing persons had been reunited with their families in the last five years – 2 963 were children under 18 years of age, with 1 919 female and 967 male children.

Missing Children South Africa’s statistics state that 77% of children reported missing to them are found. The organisation states that children are among the most vulnerable victims of gender-based violence.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Shadrack Sibiya continues bid for bail
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Disgraced former Deputy Police Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya is expected back in court on Wednesday as his bail hearing continues.

The proceedings took a dramatic turn on Tuesday when a voice recording introduced serious new allegations into the case.

In the recording, businessman Serge Cabonge allegedly claims that Sibiya received money from alleged crime boss Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala.

Cabonge also allegedly claims that a judge advised him to leave the country after his name surfaced at the Madlanga Commission.

The inquiry has indicated that it plans to obtain Cabonge’s statement as the allegations come under further scrutiny.

World.title: South Africa's water crisis: Is poor municipal management to blame?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Poor municipal management, weak governance, and inadequate infrastructure investment are exacerbating South Africa's water crisis.

Futuregrowth investment analyst Taariq Mohamed says the problem is not necessarily a lack of funding, but how available funds are spent and managed.

Municipalities currently owe water boards more than R25-billion.

Mohamed says poor financial management and insufficient infrastructure investment are hampering municipalities’ ability to maintain and repair water systems, worsening shortages.

He says South Africa’s water availability has also come under pressure from lower average rainfall and population growth, which has increased by about 37% over the past two decades.

While South Africa is naturally water-scarce, Mohamed argues that poor municipal management is compounding the problem.

World.title: Indonesians on fire-ravaged island sue state for clean air
World.content:
PONTIANAK - Every few years, residents of Indonesia's West Kalimantan province contend with devastating wildfires that emit a noxious haze causing illnesses, shuttering schools and stifling economic activity.

Now, they've had enough.

Lawyers have filed a class action case claiming "negligence, omission and failure" on the part of the government that has resulted in "a massive public health crisis" in the province on Borneo island.

Their target: President Prabowo Subianto and 26 officials from the national, provincial and local government, as well as police and emergency services.

"We're not asking for anything excessive. We're only demanding our basic rights as citizens: clean air and a healthy environment," Sisilius Rami told AFP at his home in the haze-blanketed city of Pontianak.

"We... want to breathe fresh air, see clear skies and enjoy the sun," said the 29-year-old, one of four plaintiffs in the case.

Sisilius said the haze affects every aspect of daily life, disrupting schooling and outdoor activities including some farming. Anyone venturing outside must wear a mask or risk inhaling toxins.

World.title: Regulator 'will resign' if any political interference in Man City case
World.content:
MANCHESTER - The chair of English football's Independent Regulator has said he will resign if there is political interference in any future investigation into Manchester City as a result of widespread impropriety.

City have been found guilty on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules by an independent commission.

The club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, but face a severe sanction unless they overturn the verdict.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has come under criticism for his comments saying he would be "really concerned" if City's Abu Dhabi owners left the club following the verdict.

Downing Street subsequently had to backtrack, insisting no one was "above the rules".

Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, has since published all of his dealings with the City hierarchy.

But the case poses a delicate balancing act for the UK government in preserving its longstanding ties with the Emirates without interfering in the independence of the disciplinary action against City.

The club's owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan is vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

The Football Regulator has the power to disqualify and remove club owners and senior executives and force the sale of clubs.

"Our independence is absolute, and my independence personally is absolute," Independent Regulator chair David Kogan said on Tuesday.

"I made it very clear in an interview last year that if we (experience) any form of political interference on the way we operate it is going to result in my resigning from this role, and I stand by that completely."

Kogan has also warned that the English game is on the "edge of financial disaster" despite booming revenues.

The Regulator's first "State of the Game" report found that while English football generated £9 billion ($12 billion) in revenue last season, 94 percent of clubs in the top five divisions were loss-making.

Thirty-two clubs could not survive more than 30 days without owner funding, while 17 would make a loss even if their players played for free.

Kogan added English club football was simultaneously the "richest, best and most deeply competitive in the world while also standing on the edge of financial disaster".

The report forecasts total debt in English football would rise above £5 billion by the end of this season and that net transfer debt was approximately £3.4 billion.

"Everyone needs to take into account the fact that nothing is ever forever," said Kogan.

- 'Alarm call' -

England's Football Supporters' Association said the report was "an alarm call for English men's professional football that must precipitate real and lasting change".

UK culture secretary Lisa Nandy said: "Football fans for years have lived with the anxiety of knowing their club could be one bad owner or poor month away from ruin.

"This report doesn't just validate that anxiety, it has blown the doors off the game with the most stark uncovering of the state of football club finances in England today."

Kogan is set to be interviewed by the House of Commons' culture, media and sport committee next month.

Committee chair Caroline Dinenage, an MP for the main opposition Conservative Party, said: "The IFR is right, the financial risk embedded in English club football can no longer be ignored. They've framed the issue, now they need to show us what they've got."

World.title: Croatia trials full driverless robotaxi service
World.content:
ZAGREB - A Croatian firm that launched Europe's first commercial robotaxi service earlier this year is now testing fully driverless rides in the capital, its chief executive told AFP.

Since April, Verne -- which is backed by Uber and powered by Chinese self-driving firm Pony.ai -- has been operating a commercial robotaxi service in Zagreb.

So far a backup driver, or so-called safety operator, has remained in the driver's seat during the rides.

But on Tuesday, Verne invited an AFP journalist to ride along on what its CEO Marko Pejkovic described as Europe's "first" fully automated robotaxi rides, which he hopes to roll out commercially next year.

"Now we are beginning to test a fully driverless robotaxi service, with no operator in the vehicle anymore."

"This is the first one in Europe."

Autonomous taxis are already operating in the United States and China.

Last month, London became the second European city, after Zagreb, to roll out a service that keeps a safety driver in the vehicle.

At the same time, other companies are competing to launch the continent's first fully automated robotaxi services.

World.title: Court delays can undermine justice, Law Society warns
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Court delays can feel like a denial of justice to those seeking it, although the reasons may sometimes be beyond the control of a magistrate or judge.

In other cases, delays may be legally justified and reasonable.

Nevertheless, they can prolong proceedings for both victims and accused persons.

The murder trial of Kiernan “AKA” Forbes and Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane has entered its second week at the KwaZulu-Natal High Court.

The first day of proceedings was delayed, reportedly due to logistical challenges involving the transportation of accused persons from prisons far from the court. Infrastructure problems, including a non-functioning lift, were also reported.

As a result, the trial began at 11.30am instead of the scheduled 9am start.

World.title: University or trade? Advice for Class of 2026
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Final matric exams are here, and life after school is top of mind for those ending their schooling career.

In today’s tough economy, traditional degrees aren't the only route to success.

More youth are being encouraged to consider skilled trades like welding, electrical engineering, and plumbing.

eNCA hit the streets of Johannesburg to find out what career advice people have for the Class of 2026.

World.title: Sibiya rape accuser fears for her safety if he is granted bail
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - One of the complainants in the case against Shadrack Sibiya says she fears for her safety, as well as that of her family and friends, if the former police top cop is released on bail.

The concerns of the 18-year-old woman who has accused Sibiya of rape were detailed in a statement read by state prosecutor Velile Makasana during Sibiya’s bail hearing.

In the statement, the complainant alleges that a friend told her she had been approached by the defence to make a statement contradicting her evidence, but refused.

The complainant said:

“My trust in the justice system would be betrayed as I would be exposed to the worst situation."

“This is the kind of interference that is currently at play with such a sensitive case,” she added.

She said the incident had taken a toll on her loved ones, whose lifestyles had changed to accommodate security measures.

“My friends and family know how I suffer as a result of the incident that I did not invite. I worry about their safety as much as I do with mine,” she said.

WATCH | Shadrack Sibiya continues bid for bail

The complainant added that safety concerns had restricted her movements and activities, and that her fears had persisted since she initially struggled to report the alleged incident.

“The same fears that I had when I was initially scared to report the matter have since played out. My movements and activities are limited, and I wish this can come to an end,” she said.

Sibiya faces five charges, including rape, human trafficking and three counts of sexual grooming involving a 16-year-old girl.

According to the allegations, Sibiya allegedly gave an 18-year-old woman alcohol before she lost consciousness and was raped at a hotel in Sandton.

Sibiya has denied the rape allegation, maintaining that the encounter was consensual.

World.title: Sh45b shareholder loan: Inside Kenya Airways advanced investor talks
World.content:
Kenya Airways seeks fresh investors as critics question whether its Sh45bn bailout can deliver lasting growth. [File, Standard]

Kenya Airways is at an advanced stage of discussions with prospective investors and will issue an Information Memorandum (IM) subject to regulatory approvals, the national carrier said on Tuesday, as it seeks to recapitalise after years of losses.

The airline said the IM is part of preparations to support future capital-raising and onboard strategic partners. It did not disclose the identity of potential investors, the size of the planned raise, or a timeline.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
