World.title: A new night train will launch between Hamburg and Munich in March 2027
World.content:
A new night train in Germany linking Hamburg and Munich is set to launch on 23 March 2027.

 

Berlin-based Nox Mobility says its first service will run three times a week in each direction, with stops in Bremen and Augsburg.

With a new generation of night trains designed to make overnight rail “the most obvious alternative” to short-haul flights, Nox Mobility previously revealed that it plans connections between 100 European cities by 2035.

Its proposed network includes Paris, Barcelona, Amsterdam, Copenhagen, Warsaw, Budapest and Rome.

What will the new night train offer?

Passengers will travel in individual “Nox Suites”, each featuring a large seat, a table for working or eating, space for large luggage and power outlets.

At night, the seat unfolds into a lounge position, providing two metres of space to stretch out alongside the window.

However, travellers expecting the fully private bedrooms outlined in Nox’s original plans will have to wait. Its “Nox Rooms”, designed for one or two people, are scheduled to join the fleet from 2029.

As Euronews Travel reported in June 2025, the company initially envisaged launching in 2027 with private sleeping cabins. The latest announcement sets out a phased introduction, starting with the seat-based suites.

“With Nox, every passenger has their own space to work and rest in,” said Thibault Constant, Co-Founder of Nox Mobility. “A night on a Nox train should eventually bring together everything that used to take three bookings: getting there, staying the night and the morning at the destination.”

The Nox Suites seat unfolds into a lounge position Max Kissler/Nox Mobility

What time will the trains depart?

One-way fares start at €65. Southbound trains scheduled to leave Hamburg at 9:22 pm, calling at Bremen at 10:30 pm and Augsburg at 7:35 am before reaching Munich at 8:14 am.

In the opposite direction, departures from Munich are planned for 9:20 pm, stopping in Augsburg at 9:51 pm and Bremen at 7:20 am, with arrival in Hamburg at 8:27 am.

World.title: Iran executes man accused of armed attacks during US-Israeli strikes
World.content:
Iran executed a political prisoner in Kerman on Wednesday on charges of carrying out armed attacks during what the Iranian judiciary described as joint American-Israeli military operations on Iranian soil.

 

The Mizan news agency, the official outlet of Iran's judiciary, identified Ali-Sina Mostafavi, 38, as one of "the armed agents of the American-Zionist enemy" and accused him of opening fire on civilians in Azadi Square in Kerman on 24 March, wounding one person and a young girl.

According to Mizan, he also fired on conscript soldiers and passing vehicles on 21 April, injuring further civilians.

The judiciary additionally accused him of participating in protests in December 2025 and January 2026 — which the Iranian authorities call the "Dey protests" and describe as a coup attempt — and of sending footage to Persian-language media outlets based outside Iran, which Tehran brands as hostile.

Among the items seized from Mostafavi, said to be from the city of Bam, were a Brno rifle with telescopic sight, a shotgun, a second unlicensed shotgun, 246 rounds for the Brno and 30 Molotov cocktails, the judiciary said.

Mostafavi, who played the tar and had made a solo ascent of Island Peak in the Himalayas and attempted Ama Dablam, reaching 6,600 metres, was held in Shahab prison in Kerman. He was moved to solitary confinement in his final days and his family were summoned for a last visit.

Reza Pahlavi, the son of Iran's last shah, described Mostafavi on X as "a patriotic young man" condemned after forced confessions extracted under torture in what he called show trials, and urged others to speak out for political prisoners facing execution.

The charge Mostafavi faced, moharebeh, or "enmity against God," in Iranian law represents taking up arms against people's lives, property or honour in a way that creates insecurity.

Tehran has deployed the charge for decades to suppress opponents, critics and protesters.

Second execution this week

Two days earlier, the Mizan news agency confirmed the execution of Omar Dorastaran, 25, identified by the judiciary as a member of the Sunni militant group Jaish al-Adl.

He was accused of helping group members enter Iran, arranging accommodation and transport, and providing support for attacks on IRGC forces in Sistan and Baluchistan province, including the attack on the Paroud base and March 2024 assaults on military installations in Chabahar.

The 2024 attack on the Rask police post was among the deadliest carried out by armed groups in south-eastern Iran. Eleven security forces members were killed.

Dorastaran, single and from the village of Cheraghan in Rask county, was studying at a religious school in the city of Pishin at the time of his arrest, according to human rights organisations.

Halvash, a local media outlet in Sistan and Baluchestan, reported that he was arrested without a warrant and held for an extended period without access to visits or phone calls, and that security agents sought to extract forced confessions through torture.

Sistan and Baluchistan, one of Iran's poorest provinces, has long been the scene of armed clashes between security forces and Sunni militant and Baloch armed organisations. Fighting in the province has intensified in recent weeks.

Amnesty International on Tuesday condemned the execution of five men within a single week in Iran in cases linked to the January protests, and called for coordinated international pressure on Tehran to halt further executions.

The organisation said the Islamic Republic uses the death penalty systematically to intimidate opponents and raise the cost of protest. Iran executed at least 2,159 people in 2025, according to Amnesty.

World.title: Trump announces plans for major oil, gas and mineral exploration in Greenland
World.content:
The US president has claimed Greenland holds vast and easily accessible oil reserves without providing evidence or details. His announcement follows a deal expanding the US military presence on the Arctic island.

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said major oil, gas and mineral exploration was set to begin in Greenland.

His announcement follows a security agreement between the United States, Denmark and the Arctic island's leaders.

What has Trump said about Greenland's resources?

Trump offered no details about which companies would be involved, where exploration would take place or when operations would begin.



"Massive Oil, Gas, and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin in our new and beautiful Greenland!" Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

He also claimed that experts believed Greenland held some of the world's largest deposits of easily accessible oil, without providing evidence.

Greenland is believed to hold substantial untapped oil reserves, but their commercial viability remains uncertain due to high extraction costs, harsh Arctic conditions and environmental restrictions. No commercial oil production has been established in Greenland.

Greenland has significant mineral resources, including rare earth elements used in electronics, renewable energy technologies and military equipment.

What's really in the Greenland deal? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The island has also attracted interest for its potential oil and gas reserves, although exploration in the harsh Arctic environment presents considerable technical and economic challenges.

In August, reports that a US oil company was preparing operations in a remote part of eastern Greenland prompted unease among residents and local authorities.

Trump did not say whether his announcement was connected to those activities.

Why is Greenland strategically important to the US?

In the same post, Trump described Greenland's strategic location as "second to none" for US and European security.

"Any future attack on the United States will have to come across Greenland," he claimed, adding that US defenses there would be able to intercept missiles, drones and other weapons.

Greenland lies along one of the shortest routes between Russia and North America, making it strategically important for missile detection and defense.

Its location is also significant for Trump's proposed "Golden Dome" missile defense system.

Melting Arctic ice has meanwhile increased interest in potential new shipping routes through the region.

What does the US security deal with Greenland involve?

In September, the United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an agreement aimed at easing tensions after Trump's repeated threats to take control of the island, including by force.

Under the 10-page agreement, Washington will establish two additional military bases, at Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland and Mestersvig in the east.

The US already operates the Pituffik Space Base in northern Greenland.

The agreement expands the American military presence and provides for cooperation on missile defense, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty over Greenland and the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination.

Greenland is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

Trump's earlier demands for US control of the island had strained relations between Washington and Copenhagen, both NATO allies.

Edited by: Jenipher Camino Gonzalez

World.title: Fact check: Misleading graph about alleged Russian bot activity
World.content:
Did attacks on Russian data centers reduce bot activity around Germany's AfD? A viral graph claims they did. But it contains significant inconsistencies and provides no evidence to support the claim.

After Ukrainian drone attacks on data centers operated by the Russian technology company Yandex , claims began circulating online that the strikes had disrupted or even halted the activity of Russian propaganda bots. These accounts are often accused of spreading disinformation or artificially amplifying content on social media.

During the Warsaw Security Forum, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also suggested that the attacks on Yandex data centers had disrupted bot activity, saying "there was less hate, less division, and fewer provocations [because] there were fewer bots." In response to BBC Verify , Zelenskyy's office said that, rather than referring to reduced bot activity, the president was "talking about the atmosphere on social media." The office added that it had seen "reports of fewer provocative and hateful comments" from many social media users.

So far, however, there is no clear evidence linking the attacks to a decline in bot activity. According to Josef Holnburger, managing director of the Center for Monitoring, Analysis and Strategy (CeMAS), there is currently "no decline in Russian disinformation activities that could be explained by the attack on Yandex data centers." CeMAS systematically monitors such campaigns.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy suggested the attacks on Yandex data centers disrupted Russian activity Image: Ukrainian Presidential Press Service/AFP

European lawmaker shares graph without evidence on X

Nevertheless, a misleading graph has been circulated as supposed evidence. It was shared, for example, by Czech Member of the European Parliament Tomáš Zdechovský. His post was viewed more than four million times on X. He suggested that the graph might demonstrate a decline in "online activity around AfD," although he did not specify what kind of activity he meant. In reality, the graph most likely demonstrates nothing at all.

The German-language graph is titled "Daily activity over 3 months." It appears to show activity remaining relatively stable before dropping sharply in early October, roughly coinciding with the attacks on Yandex data centers. However, nothing in the graph itself indicates that this relates to AfD-related online activity.

No source and faulty scaling

The same applies to the graph's underlying data. It is unclear which data were used. No source is provided, nor is there any explanation of the data collection process or calculation method for the alleged "activity," which initially ranges between 6,000 and 7,000 before falling below 3,000.

Particularly striking is that the graph extends to October 15. Its final data point appears to correspond to October 14 – a date that was still in the future when the graph first appeared online on October 11. Data for a future date cannot exist.

The graph also contains scaling errors on both the X and Y axes. For example, on the Y axis, the distance between 2,500 and 3,000 is smaller than the other 500-unit intervals. Because the Y axis does not begin at zero, the decline is visually exaggerated. On the X axis, equal periods of time are represented by unequal distances.

It is also unclear which platforms were analyzed and how the variable "activity" was calculated. The absence of a known data source, the inaccurate scaling, and the inclusion of "future" values strongly suggest that this is not a meaningful graph based on factual data and sound statistical methods.

AI involvement cannot be proven, but is possible

It is unclear whether AI was used to create the graph. Given the errors and the apparent "hallucination" of presenting future data, AI involvement cannot be ruled out.

Misleading and error-filled graphs, some of which may have been AI-generated, appear regularly. German public broadcaster BR's #Faktenfuchs team recently reported on one such graph that falsely depicted industrial production in Germany (article in German). False or fabricated graphs can lend credibility to unsupported claims.

The identity of the graph's creator remains unknown.

What do Cloudflare data actually show?

Cloudflare data are also frequently cited in connection with claims of declining bot activity. However, according to CeMAS managing director Holnburger, there is a misunderstanding about what Cloudflare's report actually means. Cloudflare provides services to many websites that block traffic assessed as non-human. Automated web traffic is common and includes, for example, crawlers that check websites for freshly published content. Search engines, including Yandex, rely on these crawlers. Other bots may be used for spam in comment sections.

In a message to #Faktenfuchs Holnburger writes, "a decline in bot activity on websites is something entirely different from a decline in inauthentic behavior by social bots on social networks."

Referring to Cloudflare data , he added: "When looking at overall activity from Russian IP addresses on servers using Cloudflare services, there is no major decline in bot activity." Furthermore, there is no reason to assume that the infrastructure used by disinformation-related social bots would be hosted on Yandex data centers. "It is more likely that these systems are distributed across many different providers," Holnburger writes.

The article was originally written in German and adapted into English by Alima de Graaf

This article is part of a collaboration between Germany's public broadcasting fact-checking teams ARD-Faktenfinder, BR24 #Faktenfuchs and DW Fact check.

World.title: Do non-German nationals commit more crimes than Germans?
World.content:
People without German passports appear more frequently in German police crime statistics than German nationals. A new study explains why.

Every year, when the Federal Criminal Police Office publishes the police crime statistics, theAlternative for Germany (AfD) — a party that is, in part, right-wing extremist — pays particularly close attention. They are looking for crimes committed by refugees, migrants and foreigners living in Germany.

But studies by media scholars show that 95% of the AfD's press releases focus on non-German suspects, while crimes involving German suspects are almost completely ignored.

However, the common narrative of the AfD — that non-Germans are inherently much more violent — is simply not true.

In a new research paper , Susann Prätor, a sociologist, criminologist and professor at the Lower Saxony Police Academy , has taken a very close look at crime data in Germany, together with her colleagues from the University of Zurich and the Lower Saxony Criminological Research Institute.

She looked not only at officially reported crime — that is, all offenses that appeared in police crime statistics — but also at unreported crime: These are all offenses that are not reported or detected, and therefore do not appear in any official statistics but are identified through representative surveys.

"According to police crime statistics, people who do not have German citizenship commit crimes more frequently than German citizens. However, studies into unreported cases show that non-German nationals are twice as likely to be reported. Differences between the two groups are also evident in crimes that go unreported, but they are significantly less pronounced," Prätor told DW.

German offenders are reported to the police much less frequently

Crimes committed by foreign nationals are therefore twice as likely to appear in police crime statistics as crimes committed by Germans.

These statistics record all reported cases and do not specify whether the allegations prove to be true.

When the statistics are adjusted for the bias in the reporting of crimes, foreigners are no longer 2.6 times more likely to commit crimes than Germans, but only 1.7 times more likely. This figure is also consistent with the results of studies on unreported juvenile violent crime. According to these studies, foreign youths are about 1.6 times as likely to commit violent crimes as German youths.

Other factors affecting crime include age and gender. Young men make up a larger proportion of the foreign-born population, and young men are the group most prone to criminal behavior across all societies.

According to Prätor, "categories such as being young, male, poorly educated and having a history of violence are factors that increase the likelihood of violent behavior. A certain concept of masculinity also plays a role, wherever that may come from. But we do not see culture as a factor, contrary to the prejudice that masculinity and violence play a greater role in other cultures."

Prätor points to a survey on attitudes toward violence. According to the survey, 5% of German youths view violence positively. Among those without a German passport, the figure is 10%.

The criminologist has identified a crucial factor: "Family upbringing plays an important role in shaping attitudes toward violence, because these attitudes are formed in the home. If I experience violence in my own home, I will have a different relationship to violence than if I hadn't experienced it," said Prätor.

Germany is, however, on the right track, says Prätor, even if it doesn't always feel that way. "Fifty or sixty years ago, parental violence was much more common in child-rearing than it is today. Acts of violence committed by young people are also far less frequent than they were in the 1990s or the early 2000s."

Prätor emphasizes that it is important to bring objectivity to the debate. A good illustration of this is a look at police records of serious violent crimes — such as aggravated assault, manslaughter, or murder. "Of every 100 German citizens, 0.2% commit violent crimes; among non-German nationals, the figure is 0.6%."

However, Prätor points out that "more than 99% of the people living here in Germany — whether of German or non-German origin — the overwhelming majority in this country do not commit any serious violent crimes at all."

Survivors: Timeline to punish rape in Germany is too short To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Germany must do more to prevent crime

Prätor also trains prospective police officers. She wants to send the message to policymakers that they should place greater emphasis on the positive aspects of migration. She argues that the debate on immigration is far too negative, largely due to an overly narrow focus on police crime statistics. The vast majority of non-Germans integrate exceptionally well, she says.

She wants the government to invest more money in prevention.

"By starting as early as possible with children and adolescents: strengthening social skills as early as preschool, building on that in school and responding when incidents of violence do occur. It's also important to invest in infrastructure and recreational activities in certain regions. After all, a key factor in youth violence — regardless of background — is that young people lack a meaningful daily structure," she said.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
World.content:
Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for greater structure globally.

At first glance, women's football is healthier than ever. A recent report by FIFPRO, football's global players' union, said worldwide revenue is expected to reach over $1bn (€894m) in 2027. The World Cup in Brazil, a first in South America, will be the last with 32 teams and is expected to be the most watched and biggest revenue-generating women's tournament ever.

The good news continues with the U17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, where the tournament is being held every year for five straight years. Germany, France, Spain, Brazil, the United States and defending champions North Korea are all at the 2026 edition of a competition whose reputation continues to grow.

"You can just see where the game is going, which is so exciting," US head coach Ciara Crinion told FIFA. "The level has just gone up. We have to continue to stay with that and compete as well. [The U-17 Women's World Cup] almost feels like that first stepping stone in a major tournament for young players, and now you see how serious it is taken."

Puerto Rico, Australia and Argentina are making their debuts. For Puerto Rico, qualification is a moment of history as no football team in the men's or women's game has ever reached a World Cup tournament before.

"We've embraced this idea of being Puerto Rico's first team to qualify for a World Cup," head coach Andres Mirabelli told FIFA. Alongside national development plans, player recruitment was aided by a diaspora of nearly four million in the United States, perhaps the strongest place for women's football in the world. According to FIFPRO, the regional football average salary in North America is $5,940 (€5,547) per month, which is far higher than any other continent.

Women's game falling short on global standards

But even for the handful of players who make it out of these youth tournaments to a professional career, creating a living out of the beautiful game remains a real challenge. The aforementioned FIFPRO report details that many professional female players across the world barely earn minimum wage, with some even falling below it.

The report, which sourced its data from player surveys across the world, found that only 66% of professional players are paid for 12 months a year. The global average salary is $2,600 (€2,300) a month, but the range varies drastically across the world. In Eastern Europe, for example, that average is just $880 per month. In Africa, it is just $432, but in North America it is just under $6,000.

"I think what you also find in the women's game is the gaps are not just between the top five leagues and the rest. There is a gap there, but even within leagues themselves [there is one]," FIFPRO head of research and strategy for women's football Frankie Brown told DW. "In some of the other leagues you're dealing with teams that are operating professionally, so will be paying their players on a reasonable wage, and playing in the same league as them you'll have players that are on amateur contracts and not being paid at all."

With economic and job security an issue for many, the report reveals that psychological stress factors are now the second main reason many consider leaving football.

"This is one of the most concerning parts of the report," Alex Culvin, the director of women's football at FIFPRO, said in a statement. "Of the 49% of women’s football players considering leaving the sport early, 46% cited their mental health as the reason. In interviews, players say the sport's growth brings new pressures — including extra workload and social media abuse — but that clubs do not have the necessary safeguards in place to support these changes. We want clubs and national associations to provide mandatory mental health support focused on wellbeing, which is independent of sporting performance objectives."

FIFPRO's report is asking FIFA to set a so-called floor for the women's game so that minimum standards in key areas such as contracts, pensions and health can be enforced. Perhaps inspiration can be taken from the labor deal the WNBA agreed in 2026. It was long-negotiated deal that ultimately sent a message to female athletes everywhere to push for better pay, conditions and a greater share of the revenue they help generate.

"It is positive that average salaries are increasing for some players and that more are earning a satisfactory wage, but it’s important to note that there is a huge disparity in pay across regions," said Culvin.

"There is also an imbalance in conditions, not only across the globe but also within regions; in Europe, for example, the difference in standards between the east and west is enormous. This is a gulf we need to work hard to narrow; the growth in the most advanced markets must not be completely isolated from the rest of the industry.

Bayern Munich are one of the biggest clubs in the world, but Germany also has gaps when it comes to baseline support for women playing professional football Image: O. Behrendt/Contrast/IMAGO

Germany aiming to be example of development

With high hopes for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil and recent moves to increase professional football domestically, Germany is aiming to become an example for structural improvement in women's football. Hosting the Euros in 2029 certainly gives them an incentive to improve standards.

While salaries are in the upper tier - in the 2023-24 season, a women's Bundesliga player earned an average base salary of around €48,000 per year - the process of structural development in the country is still in its infancy. A new German FA (DFB) rule shows that even basic professional structures are still being established. Only since the 2025–26 season have teams in the Women's Bundesliga been required to employ assistant coaches, goalkeeper coaches and athletic coaches on a full-time, professional basis.

"The facilities and the staff members," Nicole Anyomi told DW were a factor in her making a recent move to London City Lionesses. "We have 30-plus staff members here whereas in Frankfurt we had like seven or eight. You can learn from each person and there is something new to learn every day. I think that's how you develop as a player faster."

Ultimately, the faster the game grows the greater need to close the gaps.

"Despite playing on different continents, players are connected by their precarity," Culvin said. "The redistribution systems in women's football need to be more effective, touching more players and supporting a more sustainable ecosystem."

Edited by: Matt Pearson

World.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
World.content:
Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.

From mini fans and the cheap chargers to smartwatches bought as part of a New Year's health kick, some 44% of Europeans own at least six "fast-tech" gadgets. And more than half say they keep unused and broken e-waste items languishing at home or throw them in the regular trash instead of recycling.

That's according to a new report by Brussels-based e-waste association WEEE Forum. It describes fast tech, which is booming, as charging and lighting devices under €10 (circa $11), high-tech items like power banks and fitness trackers, and gadgets and lifestyle appliances like cheap mini blenders and fans, as well as single-use electronic vapes.

"So, these electronics are a bit like fast fashion," Magdalena Charytanowicz, WEEE Forum's Communication Manager, told DW.

Cheap e-vapes are part of the rising trend of fast tech that is adding to the growing e-waste crisis Image: Joel Carrett/AAP/dpa/picture alliance

Nearly 40% of buyers recalled discarding a fast-tech item without using it at all or within a month of buying it, and nearly 60% said they had used a product for no longer than six months. Yet the vast majority of respondents were generally satisfied with their gadgets despite short-lived functionality.

This suggests consumers accept the "fast-tech bargain" of poor quality that "does the job for a while" and is easily replaced — similar to fast fashion — according to the report.

The Great Wall of e-waste and what to do about it

About 62 million tons of electronics are discarded worldwide annually. "That's the Great Wall of China of e-waste that is produced every year," noted Charytanowicz, adding that the figure is set to grow to 82 million by 2030.

In Europe, roughly 40% of electronic waste is recycled, yet the rate worldwide is just 17%. This means valuable materials are lost, while electronic waste ends up polluting the environment.

Recycling rare earths in Germany to reduce China dependence To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In 2022, a million tons of critical raw materials were embedded in the 10.7 million tons of e-waste generated across Europe, including manganese, gold, copper and aluminum.

These materials are at "the center of geopolitical tensions," Charytanowicz said, referring to escalating global tensions over access to rare earths and other critical minerals.

"Even the smallest" devices are worth recycling if they contain a circuit board or battery, she said.

Groups like WEEE Forum say more awareness raising is needed on how to dispose of cheap electronic devices, and that recycling should be made as easy as possible.

But the best way to reduce a product's environmental impact is to extend its lifespan through better design and repair, as recycling raw materials is energy intensive.

Charytonawicz said clearer, harmonized EU rules now under consideration could help improve e-waste collection. The bloc's 20-year-old directive is "not really adapted to the changing reality," she said.

Healthcare's increasing digital waste problem

Another growing area of e-waste is digital healthcare. While devices such as diabetes sensors and blood pressure monitors are "transforming healthcare," many are designed to be disposable.

Even small, cheap electronics should be recycled as they contain valuable materials Image: Desmond Tiro/DW

A study published in Nature in December 2025 found sales of wearable healthcare electronics, for example, could reach 2 billion devices annually by 2050, and generate a million tons of e-waste.

Jeremy Faludi, associate professor of sustainable design engineering at TU Delft in the Netherlands, says making health tech — particularly digital devices used in, or issued by hospitals — recyclable or reusable comes with some "much bigger challenges" than normal electronics.

That's in part due to the potential for patient contamination, particularly with digital surgical devices that come into contact with blood or other bodily fluids.

"The way that a lot of things are designed now, you can't recover the stuff because it can't be easily sterilized without the electronics," said Faludi.

How wearables are revolutionizing heart health To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

He worked on the Digital Health in Circular Economy (DiCE) project, an EU-funded initiative, to help redesign digital healthcare devices to "recover critical materials and reduce environmental impacts without compromising patient safety."

A modular design, for example, allows electronic components to be separated from the parts that need to be replaced between patients, making devices easier to reuse.

The four-year DiCE project, which included citizens, hospitals and manufacturers across nine EU countries, found reusable ECG cables — which connect patients to heart-monitoring equipment — cut environmental impacts by up to 81-94%, for example. The sets are usually designed for single use.

Rules around medical waste can also make reuse and recycling more difficult, particularly when requirements differ between countries and often come down to perceived rather than actual risk, Faludi added. He says some 85% of hospital trash is not infectious but everything ends up in the same bins. Better sorting as well as EU-wide regulations around treating non-infectious hospital waste would help here.

Many digital health devices could be reused or recycled if designed properly Image: Marko Prpic/PIXSELL/picture alliance

'Green nudges' help citizens to recycle

Like with other tech, consumer health devices such as blood pressure and glucose monitors often risk being forgotten in drawers or ending up in the wrong waste, simply because people do not know how to dispose of them, said Charytanowicz of WEEE Forum, which is also involved in DiCE.

Pilot schemes in Belgium, Spain and Slovenia that offered free postal returns and collection machines in public places found that more than 60% of people were willing to return unwanted devices if it was a straightforward process.

"What's really important is the convenience so that it can be integrated in your daily routines," said Charytanowicz, adding that "nudges"such as messages that recycling a device could help the health of another person motivate people to "do the right thing."

Edited by: Tamsin Walker

World.title: Germany news: Nord Stream sabotage suspect's trial opens
World.content:
10/14/2026 October 14, 2026 Suicide rate increased significantly in 2025

The suicide rate in Germany has continued to climb, according to official statistics just released by the Federal Ministry of Health.

In 2025, at least 11,334 people killed themselves in Germany. That is a 9.3% increase on the previous year, and 15.6% higher than the average over the past decade.

This is higher than the number of deaths due to traffic accidents, AIDS, murder and manslaughter put together.

The data shows that this is partly due to more women (a 17.9% increase since 2021) taking their own lives, though most suicides are still carried out by men. The increase is also due to an increase in assisted suicides for the elderly and infirm, amounting to over 1,000 people.

In a 2020 decision, Germany's top court struck down a 2015 ban on organized assisted dying providers like Switzerland's Dignitas, and called on the Bundestag to create regulations for the practice. However, lawmakers have declined thus far to do so, putting assisted suicide in a legal gray area in Germany. Direct euthanasia by a single doctor remains illegal.

What is assisted suicide and where does Germany stand? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In August, the Health Ministry proposed reforms such as a national suicide prevention hotline, more support for local and state networks, as well as the creation of a federal office for suicide prevention.

However, medical groups and charities have both said that the proposed €1.4 million ($1.6 million) budget would come nowhere never covering such a scheme long-term.

Editor's note: If you are suffering from serious emotional strain or suicidal thoughts, do not hesitate to seek professional help. You can find information on where to find such help, no matter where you live in the world, at this website: https://www.befrienders.org/

World.title: Iran: Political infighting deepens as economic woes mount during war
World.content:
Hardliners are stepping up pressure on Iran's government and calling for Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's removal. The oil minister resigned, but that's doing little to ease the pressure on President Masoud Pezeshkian.

Hardliners are piling the pressure on Iran’s government and calling for the removal of Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad’s resignation is also failing to ease the pressure on President Masoud Pezeshkian.

As the war continues and diplomatic efforts to find a solution make little headway, the internal power struggle is intensifying. President Pezeshkian’s government is the focus of mounting tension.

Hardliners in Iran's parliament are pushing for impeachment proceedings against Araghchi. A trigger for the discontent was Araghchi's meeting with US negotiators on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Critics accuse the foreign minister of holding the talks without official authorization.

Iran's oil exports have plunged as a result of the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz Image: Asghar Besharati/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

In a letter, Tehran lawmaker Amirhossein Sabeti informed parliamentary speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf that he had registered a motion to impeach Araghchi on parliament’s online portal. Lawmaker Hossein-Ali Haji-Deligani also said parliament could use its oversight powers, including impeachment proceedings.

A structural problem within Iran’s power system

"When the regime is forced to negotiate, as it is in the current situation and in talks with the United States, the supreme leader or the hardline core of power avoids taking responsibility and shifts it onto elected institutions and moderate forces within the government," political analyst Ali Afshari, who lives in the United States, told DW.

Hardliners can use this approach to attack moderate factions over decisions that were previously agreed upon within the power apparatus, Afshari said.

He added that hardliners serve an important function within the Islamic Republic.

"The role of hardliners in the Islamic Republic is to influence public opinion, the political system's traditional supporters and the values of the Islamic Republic in both domestic and foreign policy," he said.

All the Ayatollah's men — ensuring the regime's survival To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Hardliners held a parliamentary majority during the implementation of the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), the 2015 nuclear deal, and voiced their political opposition. Their resistance, however, ultimately did not affect the signing of the agreement.

"The Foreign Ministry is not a decision-maker. It implements what the government asks of it — and Araghchi is operating within that framework," Afshari said.

Lawmakers must first collect a set number of signatures to move forward with impeachment proceedings.

The lucrative business of oil

The timing of the latest move is significant: Iran's government finds itself under enormous economic pressure. Meanwhile, oil exports, which are one of the country's key sources of revenue, have fallen sharply as a result of the US blockade.

The resignation of Oil Minister Paknejad adds to the pressure. Officially, he stepped down for personal reasons.

Umud Shokri, an energy strategist, geopolitical analyst and energy security expert, casts doubt that a change at the helm of the Oil Ministry would alter the situation. Iran relies on networks that enable it to export oil despite sanctions, Shokri said. Opaque structures have become entrenched, making it harder for the government to control key revenue streams.

Circumventing sanctions has become a lucrative business for certain factions within Iran's political system, he said.

"By law, these revenues should be under state control. But we know that has not been the case for years," Shokri said.

Economic opacity has deepened during the sanctions period, he added, under the pretext of national security and protecting the population.

Fighting Iran war, can US military sustain a long conflict? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Private actors with close ties to the country's centers of power, particularly the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), have developed methods to sell oil to the armed forces through hidden channels. Neither the prices nor the commissions charged or the total sums involved are transparent.

"The government has only limited influence over these transactions. The Revolutionary Guards, in particular, would organize and control such deals," Shokri said.

Analysts have signaled that political and economic situation could likely deteriorate further in the coming days and weeks.

This article was originally published in German.

World.title: India news: 'Cockroach' leaders sent to judicial custody amid protest crackdown
World.content:
Skip next section Jantar Mantar: What to know about Delhi's delisted protest site?

10/14/2026 October 14, 2026 Jantar Mantar: What to know about Delhi's delisted protest site?

For decades, a stretch of road leading up to Jantar Mantar has been where Indians came to be heard, press their demands and hold those in power accountable [FILE: May 28, 2023] Image: Altaf Qadri/AP Photo/picture alliance

Jantar Mantar, in central Delhi, is an 18th century open-air astronomical observatory.

For over three decades, a stretch of road leading up to it was where Indians came to be heard, press their demands and hold those in power accountable. That was until last week when the Delhi Police delisted the iconic venue as a protest site.

What sparked the latest protests?

The move came days after a confrontation between thousands of police personnel and anti-government protesters led by India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).

Police reportedly detained thousands of protesters and even reporters on duty last week Image: Bhawika Chhabra/REUTERS

The group, along with student organizations and activists, mobilized thousands to protest against a revision in electoral rolls which reportedly deleted 130 million voters.

While those deleted include dead and duplicate voters, critics argue the staggering number likely includes a vast number of eligible voters. India's poll body and the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party party have denied this.

Jantar Mantar has been the central rallying location for protesters demanding election Chief Gyanesh Kumar's resignation for overseeing the revision.

This is the same location that acted as a home base for the CJP-led youth protests in July over an exam scandal, which resulted in the removal of India's former education minister.

Why is delisting Jantar Mantar controversial?

Now, instead of Jantar Mantar, authorities have designated three alternative venues in Delhi. Campaigners argue those venues will reduce visibility and proximity to lawmakers as Jantar Mantar was surrounded by the nation's biggest institutions.

"Jantar Mantar is in the centre of the town, it is connected, it is next to parliament... it was a very important space for all protests," human rights activist Shabnam Hashmi told AFP. "This is nothing but a move to curb dissent," he said.

CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were among about a dozen people who jumped barricades on Tuesday to enter the grounds of Jantar Mantar, despite the delisting a day earlier.

An Indian court has now sent Das and Ranka to five days in judicial custody over trespassing and other violations.

World.title: Colau ofrece renunciar a su candidatura y cambiar el nombre de Frente Amplio para lograr la unidad con Podemos
World.content:
La candidata de Frente Amplio a la presidencia del Gobierno, Ada Colau, ha abierto este miércoles la puerta a renunciar a encabezar la coalición e incluso a cambiar su nombre para facilitar un acuerdo con Podemos y otras formaciones de cara a las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. “Todo se puede discutir”, ha afirmado en una entrevista en TVE, coincidiendo con el inicio de las primarias telemáticas de Podemos y apenas un día después de que Izquierda Unida, Más Madrid, Comuns y Movimiento Sumar acordaran que Emilio Delgado encabezará la lista de Frente Amplio por Madrid. La exalcaldesa de Barcelona ha insistido en que su prioridad es conseguir “una sola papeleta” de las izquierdas, pese a las dificultades para cerrar un pacto antes del viernes, cuando expira el plazo para registrar las coaliciones electorales.

“Me propusieron como candidata entendiendo que soy una persona de consenso”, ha explicado Colau, que ha dejado claro que su designación no es inamovible. “Si más adelante se suman otras personas al Frente y hay otra persona que genera más consenso, adelante, estoy dispuesta a ceder”, ha asegurado. Su disposición a negociar también alcanza al nombre de la coalición que actualmente encabeza: “Si el problema es el nombre de la formación, se cambia”. La exalcaldesa ha defendido que ninguna cuestión organizativa debería convertirse en un obstáculo para alcanzar el objetivo de una candidatura unitaria.

Desoyendo el mensaje de Colau y después de un debate interno, una hora más tarde, los partidos han lanzado de manera oficial Frente Amplio como marca; con su web (frenteamplio.info), la imagen gráfica en una gama cromática compuesta por el bermellón y el lima, y los perfiles en redes sociales. La coalición, que ha decidido continuar con su planificación, tiene previsto, además, celebrar un acto el sábado en Madrid a las doce del mediodía para presentar la candidatura. De momento, se desconoce quién intervendrá y qué partidos estarán en ella.

Pese a que el último movimiento de la dirigente catalana ha descolocado a algunos cuadros, distintas voces de las formaciones defienden su intervención y la interpretan como una manera de presionar a Podemos para que aclare en estas últimas horas cruciales si quiere de verdad la unidad. En los partidos entienden que puede generar cierta confusión, pero sostienen que la candidata siempre tiene “margen” para marcar posición en determinados momentos de bloqueo.

La oferta de la dirigente catalana llega después de que Podemos rechazara este martes integrarse en Frente Amplio y reivindicara su acuerdo electoral con ERC, que mantiene abierto a la incorporación de otras fuerzas políticas. Irene Montero confirmó la existencia de conversaciones con otras formaciones, aunque evitó concretar sus términos, mientras que Ione Belarra invitó al resto de partidos a sumarse a la alianza alcanzada con los republicanos. La formación morada ha puesto en marcha este miércoles, a las ocho de la mañana, sus primarias telemáticas, un proceso al que ha pedido que concurran los líderes de otras organizaciones de izquierda para elegir una candidatura conjunta.

Colau ha evitado cuestionar esta iniciativa y ha expresado su “respeto” por el proceso interno de Podemos, aunque ha puesto el acento en las posibilidades de entendimiento que todavía existen. “No concibo una candidatura única sin Irene Montero”, ha afirmado. La candidata de Frente Amplio ha recordado que la exministra de Igualdad rechazó incorporarse a la coalición, pero también dejó abierta la puerta a otros acuerdos. “Me quedo con esto”, ha apuntado, convencida de que las similitudes programáticas entre las distintas organizaciones deberían facilitar una negociación. “Nadie entendería que no nos pusiéramos de acuerdo”, ha añadido.

Preguntada por qué ofrece concretamente Frente Amplio a Podemos para facilitar su incorporación, Colau ha admitido que no existe una propuesta cerrada. “No hay una oferta en concreto. Se construyen conversando”, ha explicado. La exalcaldesa ha insistido en que las conversaciones continúan y ha descartado hacer públicas las posibles concesiones de cada parte. “Las negociaciones no las haremos a través de los medios”, ha advertido. Tampoco ha querido dar por imposible un pacto en los pocos días que quedan. “Soy realista. Sé que es complicado. Nos queda mucho trabajo”, ha reconocido, antes de recordar que en otras convocatorias electorales se alcanzaron entendimientos que inicialmente parecían inviables. “El acuerdo es posible si hay voluntad política”, ha defendido.

La candidata también se ha referido a Gabriel Rufián, a quien animó a incorporarse a Frente Amplio después de considerar que había conectado con las demandas de la izquierda. “Lamentablemente, no quiso. Ha generado decepción, pero es legítimo”, ha admitido. Pese al acuerdo alcanzado entre ERC y Podemos, Colau considera que todavía hay posibilidades de entendimiento y ha restado importancia a la voluntad de los republicanos de preservar sus propias siglas. “Creo que no debe ser un problema”, ha señalado, recordando que las organizaciones que integran Frente Amplio mantienen su identidad. “Hay margen para seguir hablando”, ha insistido.

World.title: Cómo crear contraseñas que protejan nuestra vida digital
World.content:
1 Debe ser variada Una clave de acceso se puede componer a partir de distintos tipos de caracteres, como letras mayúsculas y minúsculas, números y caracteres especiales. Utilizar la mayor variedad posible aumenta la dificultad para ser descifrada

2 Debe ser larga Como referencia, es preferible utilizar 16 caracteres o más, cuando el servicio lo permita. Utilizar una frase puede ser más fácil de recordar

3 Evitar la información personal Eludir el propio nombre o el apellido, así como los de familiares, las fechas de nacimiento, los apodos, los nombres de mascotas, los de equipos de fútbol favoritos o cualquier otra información que se pueda encontrar en las propias redes sociales

4 Evitar combinaciones predecibles Muchos usuarios recurren a composiciones como 123456, password y otras secuencias sencillas que conviene eludir

5 Utilizar un gestor de contraseñas Existen programas seguros, de pago y gratuitos, que permiten generar y almacenar estos códigos sin tener que memorizarlos

World.title: La buena cara de la industria cosmética española
World.content:
El sector del cuidado personal y la belleza, que aporta el 1% del PIB y emplea a 50.000 personas, se alza paulatinamente como una industria puntera en España y en el mundo. Sin embargo, su futuro pasa por superar tres grandes desafíos: hacer productos más sostenibles, combatir las falsificaciones y mantener las exportaciones en un clima internacional adverso

LICO Cosmetics Estefanía Ferrer Fundadora y directora ejecutiva Laboratorio de ingeniería cosmética nacido en Sevilla y concebido como una compañía nativa digital. Cantabria Labs Juan Matji Presidente Laboratorio farmacéutico español especializado en productos para el cuidado de la salud de la piel

La industria de la cosmética no tiene que maquillar sus cifras para demostrar su éxito. Así lo cree Óscar Mateo, director de Conocimiento y Estudios de Mercado de la Asociación Nacional de Perfumería y Cosmética (Stanpa). El informe más reciente de la asociación, que integra a más del 90% del sector, en torno a 300 empresas, asegura que en los últimos cinco años, el negocio ha crecido un 44% y ha duplicado sus exportaciones. Este es un ámbito económico amplio que aglutina la fabricación de productos para la higiene personal, el cuidado de la piel y el cabello, el maquillaje y hasta los perfumes. Precisamente estos últimos constituyen, en palabras de Mateo, el buque insignia del sector, gracias al peso de compañías españolas como Puig, cuya presencia trasciende nuestras fronteras.

El otro pilar es el cuidado de la piel, para el que la industria ha adoptado el nombre en inglés: skincare. Debe su crecimiento al interés cada vez mayor por mantener una piel sana y con buen aspecto. Lo dice Juan Matji, presidente de Cantabria Labs, una compañía farmacéutica que fabrica productos, tanto cosméticos como medicamentos, para el cuidado de la piel. “Antiguamente las cremas eran para un cierto grupo de mujeres que contaban con recursos económicos, hoy se ha democratizado”, explica el empresario en un nuevo capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen, de Banco Sabadell.

El auge del sector también obliga a afrontar una nueva lista de desafíos que aparecen por el camino como poros abiertos. Entre ellos, destacan la búsqueda de fórmulas más sostenibles sin perder eficacia, la protección frente a las falsificaciones y la lucha contra la llamada quimicofobia, término con el que Estefanía Ferrer, ingeniera química y fundadora de LICO Cosmetics, describe la desconfianza que ciertos ingredientes generan en la población. Ferrer, cuya marca nació en el entorno digital, comparte conversación con Matji en este episodio del pódcast. La charla entre ambos empresarios sirve para conocer mejor sus historias y desgranar un negocio que enfrenta un futuro fresco y radiante.

“El ‘skincare’ está aquí para quedarse. Antiguamente era para un cierto grupo de mujeres con recursos económicos, pero hoy se ha democratizado” Juan Matji, presidente de Cantabria Labs, sobre el ‘boom’ de la cosmética en España

Las fortalezas Una industria que avanza con paso firme y se expande por el mundo

Una industria en expansión. El sector de la cosmética y el cuidado personal avanza a un ritmo moderado, pero sostenido. Ha pasado de representar el 0,9% del PIB español al 1,03% en los últimos cuatro años. Entre las razones de su consolidación se encuentran el desarrollo de una cultura del cuidado de la piel y el cabello y el bienestar personal, con una mención especial a los cosméticos para el rostro y la fotoprotección solar, que empieza a consumirse de manera notable fuera del verano.

Potencia exportadora. España vende cada año más productos al extranjero y ya supera a manufacturas emblemáticas como el aceite de oliva, el vino y el calzado. Además, España es el segundo exportador mundial de perfumes, solo por detrás de Francia.

Con buena reputación. La industria española produce bajo uno de los marcos regulatorios más exigentes del mundo: el europeo. Además, trabaja constantemente para crear formulaciones más seguras. Para ello invierte de media el 3,4% en I+D+i. La media general de las empresas españolas de toda la economía es el 0,9%, de acuerdo con el Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE). Esto permite adaptarse mejor a los cambios en el mercado. En los dos últimos años se ha reformulado uno de cada tres productos, de acuerdo con Stanpa.

Distribuida por el territorio. Aunque Cataluña, Madrid y la Comunidad Valenciana concentran gran parte de la producción, Stanpa destaca que existe bastante descentralización, como demuestran las empresas protagonistas del vídeo, con sede en Sevilla y Cantabria.

“España compite bien internacionalmente con el ‘skincare’. No tenemos nada que envidiar a los coreanos, que están tan de moda ahora” Juan Matji, presidente de Cantabria Labs, acerca del buen estado de salud de la industria española

Los desafios Un sector que se esfuerza por garantizar la seguridad de sus productos y por reducir su impacto ambiental

Adaptarse a una regulación cada vez más compleja. Los productos y los procesos tienen que responder a nuevas exigencias europeas sobre ingredientes, seguridad, información al consumidor y trazabilidad.

El reto continuo de mejorar en sostenibilidad. Las empresas se enfrentan a varios desafíos para reducir su impacto en el medio ambiente.

Limitar el uso del plástico y mejorar las posibilidades de reciclaje de sus envases

Reducir el consumo del agua en la fabricación de sus productos, así como desarrollar metodologías para medir y reducir su huella hídrica

Encontrar ingredientes biodegradables que no impacten en la naturaleza, sin perder la eficacia

Mantener la competitividad internacional. Permanecer como el segundo exportador mundial de perfumes se transforma en un desafío en un escenario internacional complejo por las tensiones comerciales, los conflictos políticos y el aumento de los aranceles. En 2025, las exportaciones a Estados Unidos cayeron un 13% por el impacto de los aranceles, de acuerdo con Stanpa.

Combatir las falsificaciones. La compra de buena parte de los productos, como los perfumes o la cosmética de alta gama, resulta aspiracional y se enmarca en el lujo accesible. Por eso, son uno de los principales objetivos de los falsificadores. Y estas copias pueden no cumplir los requisitos europeos de seguridad y etiquetado.

Luchar contra la desinformación. El consumidor cada vez está más formado, aun así, se ha extendido a través de internet la idea de que cuantos menos productos químicos tenga una crema o un perfume, mejor será para la salud, un fenómeno que se conoce como quimiofobia, ya que se da por supuesto que los ingredientes químicos pueden ser perjudiciales para la salud. Pero hay que tener cuidado con esa información, resalta la fundadora de LICO Cosmetics. Los materiales que componen un cosmético siempre son químicos, tanto si proceden de una planta como si se sintetizan en un laboratorio. Y deben ser seguros para el consumo humano, algo que se encarga de garantizar el Comité Científico de Seguridad de los Consumidores (CCSC, por sus siglas en inglés).

World.title: Mi contrato de alquiler es hasta octubre. ¿Se renueva dos años de manera automática por los decretos de vivienda? ¿Se mantiene el precio?
World.content:
Los lectores envían sus preguntas al consultorio de vivienda de EL PAÍS en colaboración con Legálitas

Pregunta. Respecto a los decretos de vivienda, ¿significa que mi contrato, que vence en octubre de este año quedaría automáticamente renovado por dos años? Respecto al precio, ¿se contempla la subida del IPC o el precio se mantiene? I. De la Peña

Respuesta. La renovación no es automática, sino que debe solicitarse. Si se prorroga, el contrato continuará en las mismas condiciones y la actualización anual de la renta estará sujeta a los límites legalmente establecidos.

Para poder solicitar la prórroga extraordinaria de hasta dos años deben cumplirse los siguientes requisitos: que el contrato esté vigente a 8 de octubre de 2026, estar al corriente de pago y haberlo estado durante los ocho meses anteriores, y que el inquilino solicite la prórroga antes de la fecha de vencimiento del contrato. Además, es necesario que finalice alguno de los siguientes periodos: la prórroga obligatoria de cinco años (o siete años si el arrendador es una empresa), siempre que el vencimiento se produzca antes del 31 de diciembre de 2028; la prórroga tácita de hasta tres años; y una situación de tácita reconducción, es decir, que el contrato continúe mes a mes o año a año sin haberse renovado por escrito.

Si se cumplen todos estos requisitos, el arrendador estará obligado a aceptarla, salvo que necesite la vivienda para sí o para su familia y lo haya comunicado con, al menos, dos meses de antelación.

Antes de solicitar esta prórroga, conviene comprobar si el contrato ya tiene derecho a una prórroga ordinaria, ya que podría no ser necesario recurrir a la extraordinaria. Si el contrato aún no ha cumplido cinco años, se prorrogará automáticamente por anualidades hasta alcanzar ese plazo, salvo que el inquilino comunique su voluntad de no continuar. Si alcanza ahora los cinco años y el arrendador no comunicó, con al menos cuatro meses de antelación, su intención de no renovarlo, el contrato se prorrogará automáticamente por anualidades hasta un máximo de tres años adicionales.

Durante la prórroga extraordinaria se mantendrán los mismos términos y condiciones del contrato vigente. La renta seguirá siendo la misma y solo podrá actualizarse si el contrato incluye una cláusula de actualización. Además, ya no se aplicará el IPC, sino el IRAV como índice de referencia.

Asimismo, hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2027 existe un límite extraordinario: si la renta supera el índice de referencia de precios, no podrá incrementarse. En el resto de los casos, la subida será la que acuerden las partes y, en ausencia de acuerdo, no podrá superar el 2%.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Viaje a la remota isla escocesa de Islay y a la aún más inaccesible Jura, donde Orwell terminó ‘1984′
World.content:
Una escapada entre destilerías, turba y ciervos donde el paisaje se mete en el cuerpo, las canciones guardan la memoria de quienes se fueron y aún parece posible perderse entre acantilados e historias

Cuando George Orwell llegó a la isla escocesa de Jura para aislarse del mundo en 1946, escribió en su diario: “Este es un lugar extremadamente inaccesible”. Basta con intentar llegar hasta su casa en Barnhill para comprender que no exageraba: Jura está al otro lado de Islay y, una vez en esa isla, todavía hay que seguir avanzando hacia el norte por carreteras y caminos que parecen empeñados en devolver al viajero al punto de partida. Tengamos en cuenta este dato: en Jura viven 250 personas y 5.000 ciervos. Jura es la hermana pequeña de Islay, una de las islas más narcóticas de las West Highlands escocesas (las tierras altas del oeste) y donde viven 3.000 personas que gozan del lujo medioambiental yendo a donde el viento quiera, un viento con propiedades altamente saludables, que despeja y ventila como una verdad incómoda y con el que uno acaba empatizando porque, al fin y al cabo, él también parece tener prisa por detenerse a contemplar.

Para llegar hasta estas dos islas de las Hébridas Interiores, lo primero es aterrizar en Glasgow (bendito problema), la ciudad más divertida del Reino Unido, y si hay que pasar la noche, mucho mejor, porque los bares Nice ‘N’ Sleazy y Stereo no cierran nunca.

Más información En la isla de Rügen, un patrimonio entre lo mitológico y lo real

Observando la silueta de Islay por la ventanilla de la avioneta antes del aterrizaje, uno ya intuye que lo mejor será ser presa de la isla, un grano de arena entregado al aislamiento. Islay tiene algo de territorio que se ha quedado al margen por vocación. El mar, el viento y la turba han definido el carácter de las cosas, y hasta el silencio tiene una textura particular. Es una isla de horizontes bajos, carreteras estrechas en las que más de una vez hay que echarse atrás para dejar pasar al que viene, playas que cambian de humor con la marea y pequeños pueblos donde la vida transcurre como debería transcurrir la vida en todas partes. El whisky parece estar flotando en el aire, en las bodegas y en una forma de entender el paisaje. Islay no se visita, se entra en ella para dejarse llevar.

Vista de Portnahaven, un pequeño pueblo situado en el extremo sur de la isla de Islay. Paul Carroll Y Mhairi Carroll (GETTY IMAGES)

Veamos cinco puntos fuertes para hacernos una composición de lugar y extraerle el mayor partido más allá del tópico de las destilerías y apostar por el paisaje, la fauna, el bienestar, la gastronomía y la hospitalidad local.

1. La costa de Islay desde el mar

Una manera de acercarnos a esa hospitalidad de sus gentes y de su territorio es dejar las cosas en el hotel y acudir a la localidad de Port Ellen para sumarse al recorrido en bote de tres horas con comida (inolvidable) incluida de Islay Sea Adventures. El capitán Harold nos recibe empuñando una gaita cuyos fogonazos conmovedores consiguen caldear el viento.

La destilería de whisky Lagavulin, y los restos del castillo Dunyvaig, en la isla de Islay. Patsy Davies (Alamy / CORDON PRESS)

Desde el mar se contemplan las tres grandes destilerías del sur —Laphroaig, Lagavulin y Ardbeg— y, delante de cada una, la tripulación sirve un trago de whisky para que cada marca se fije en la memoria con el pegamento de haberla probado allí donde nace. Así continuamos hacia el Área Especial de Conservación de Islay, un espacio protegido al que solo se puede acceder para contemplarlo desde el agua. Mientras los simpáticos patrones van contando historias de la isla, su pasado y su patrimonio, recorremos la costa sudeste, entendiendo uno de sus paisajes más hermosos y también uno de los más ricos en fauna. Aquí vive una importante colonia de focas, además de delicados ciervos rojos que te miran con una pureza con la que mira un niño a su rey mago. Con un poco de suerte, durante la travesía pueden aparecer incluso águilas de cola blanca y delfines.

Parte de la actividad organizada por Islay Sea Adventures consiste en un pícnic de marisco tras un paseo en barco. Ben Shakespeare (Islay Sea Adventures)

El momento más extraordinario llega al alcanzar las aguas tranquilas de los islotes del sudeste de Islay (South-East Islay Skerries), porque es entonces cuando empieza el festival del marisco fresco capturado prácticamente a la puerta de la mesa: del mar al plato apenas hay unos pocos kilómetros. Langosta, bocas de buey de mar, salmón ahumado y, aparte, las vieiras, que son las protagonistas. Porque es un placer ver cómo Harold las cocina a bordo, sobre una barbacoa, con mantequilla, ajo y chile. Se agradecen el pan fresco, la ensalada y las salsas caseras, pero como decoración. Comer así es la experiencia que mejor explica la isla. Ningún folleto, ningún libro, ninguna foto puede superarlo. El único problema de esta actividad puede ser el precio: 115 libras (unos 135 euros, al cambio actual)

2. Vida de isla: tartán, ‘fish and chips’, folclore, Hollywood y Port Charlotte

Con un clima tan contradictorio, en el que un amanecer soleado puede transformarse en cinco minutos en un chubasco pasajero, conviene vestirse correctamente. Se explica así que la lana y el tartán sean tan importantes y se hayan convertido en una de las señas de identidad de las Highlands. Para hacerse una idea de hasta qué punto forman parte de su cultura, merece la pena visitar Islay Woollen Mill, una fábrica con una historia estupenda: allí se diseñó y produjo el tartán utilizado en la película Braveheart. La propia fábrica conserva y comercializa la colección Braveheart y ha trabajado también para otras producciones cinematográficas. El tartán es ese tejido de líneas de distintos colores que se cruzan en ángulo recto formando una trama de cuadros y que acabó convirtiéndose en uno de los signos visuales de Escocia. El que aquí se fabrica lo hemos visto también en Rob Roy, Highlander, Harry Potter (forma parte del uniforme de Hogwarts) e incluso en Forrest Gump, aunque en esta película el tartán juega ya como estampado universal y no tanto como emblema escocés.

El taller de Islay Woollen Mill, que trabaja con los tejidos de forma artesanal. Kenny Lam (VISIT SCOTLAND)

Al hilo de la tradición y para ver esas vestimentas, nada como una noche en el pub del Port Charlotte Hotel, en el pueblo de Port Charlotte, uno de esos rincones dulcemente extendidos frente al mar, reconocibles por sus casas blancas de dos alturas, tan bien conservadas. El local es un punto de reunión donde convergen la nostalgia y la identidad. Su fish and chips es tan interminable como irresistible. La sala tiene el encanto de los negocios eternos que abren fuera de temporada. La cerveza acompaña la llegada de los músicos, que se van sumando como si bajaran a la calle para encontrarse con sus amigos. El fiddle (violín tradicional), el acordeón, las guitarras, las mandolinas y la gaita van llenando el pub de canciones y viejas melodías de las islas, como si cada una trajera consigo un pedazo de memoria o una lágrima que se disuelve en el vaso. Cuando suena Westering Home, no hay nada ni nadie que pueda deshacer el nudo del estómago.

Esas canciones, esa música tradicional gaélica o folk, parecen creadas por la naturaleza, el viento, la lluvia, en ese mar que se lleva a la gente de aquí a probar suerte en otros mundos que difícilmente serán mejores. Y es que cuando uno se va, lo único que de verdad se lleva encima, incrustado, es la música: la canción de cuna que le cantaba su madre, las canciones que moldearon su infancia. Es la prenda mayor.

3. Excursión a Jura

Si Jura no es una isla inventada para perderse, no lo es ninguna. Lo que decíamos antes —250 vecinos rodeados por unos 5.000 ciervos— se comprueba nada más cruzar en ferri el kilómetro —apenas cinco minutos— que separa ambas islas. Bienvenidos a las montañas, las turberas, las costas solitarias y los Paps de Jura, esas tres cumbres que dominan el horizonte como una presencia casi mitológica.

Tres ciervos junto a la costa de la isla escocesa de Jura. Chris Morson (Alamy / CORDON PRESS)

Hacia el norte está Barnhill, la remota casa donde George Orwell se refugió para terminar 1984. Pero la historia del escritor británico y Jura había empezado antes. Él y su mujer, Eileen, llevaban tiempo pensando en abandonar Londres y marcharse a las Hébridas. Tanto era así que Orwell ya había iniciado las gestiones para encontrar allí una casa cuando, en marzo de 1945, Eileen murió inesperadamente durante una operación. Tenía 39 años. Orwell se quedó viudo y con Richard, el hijo que ambos habían adoptado pocos meses antes.

Un año después, David Astor, su amigo y editor del periódico The Observer, le sugirió que se marchara a Jura. La familia de Astor tenía propiedades en la isla y conocía Barnhill, una granja aislada en su extremo norte. Orwell llegó en mayo de 1946 y acabó alquilando la casa. Lo que había sido un proyecto compartido con Eileen se convirtió así en su refugio: un lugar donde alejarse de Londres, del periodismo y del ruido del mundo. En Barnhill, sin electricidad, teléfono ni vecinos a mano, encontró el aislamiento que buscaba y terminó escribiendo 1984.

Más amable es la parada en Lussa Gin, donde la ginebra se elabora con botánicos recolectados en la isla. Georgina y Claire nos enseñan su huerto, donde crecen algunos de sus ingredientes: enebro, rosas y tomillo limonero. Allí nos presentan su licor, extraordinariamente botánico, antes de mostrar su nueva creación, una ginebra homenaje a George Orwell llamada Nineteen Eighty Four, con notas de té Assam, cardamomo y rosas. El licor sirve también para hablar del escritor, que nació en la India en junio de 1903, hijo de un funcionario del Imperio británico. Con apenas un año, su madre se lo llevó a Inglaterra. Luego participó en dos guerras, experiencias que acabarían alimentando buena parte de su obra.

Parte del equipo de la destilería Lussa Gin. Lussa Gin

Cuando nos vamos, le digo a Georgina que pensamos comer en The Antlers. Su respuesta llega inmediata:

-Oohh, The Antlers... Desde que abrió, la gente de Jura está más gorda y es más pobre.

Le sobra razón. Esta bakehouse (panadería) roba el corazón hasta a la persona más evitativa con su pastrami y sus sausage rolls (rollos de salchichas). En The Antlers, la gastronomía vuelve a poner los pies en la tierra después de tantas millas de paisaje. En Jura todo parece estar desproporcionado: hay más ciervos que personas, más naturaleza que habitantes y una sensación de espacio que hace que incluso el silencio parezca perdido.

4. El imprescindible paseo al American Monument

Hay que dejar el coche en el aparcamiento de la reserva natural de The Oa, al final de la carretera que atraviesa esta península del sur de Islay. Desde allí comienza el camino hacia el American Monument, un paseo de unos treinta minutos, aunque lo razonable es hacer la ruta circular completa, de unos tres kilómetros y medio, sin ninguna prisa. Y, sobre todo, reservar otra hora para quedarse allí.

El camino es un abrazo constante de la naturaleza: la hierba, el viento del Atlántico, el salitre y esa sensación de ir dejando atrás el mundo... Hasta que aparecen los acantilados, el mar y el monumento, levantado en memoria de los soldados estadounidenses que murieron en los naufragios del Tuscania y el Otranto en 1918, que desde lejos parece suspendido sobre el océano.

El faro de Carraig Fhada, situado en la isla de Islay, es un faro emblemático en forma de torre cuadrada. Catherine Gilbrook (Alamy / CORDON PRESS)

Hay algo de templo en este lugar: un santuario sin techo ante el que uno acaba pidiendo deseos al mar, como quien deja una ofrenda y confía en que alguien, o algo, se encargará de ella. Y luego está el viento, que aquí parece tener permiso para hacer lo que quiera. Empuja, despeina, zarandea, te da la vuelta y te hace gritar al vacío. Un grito que mezcla la alegría y el dolor, la satisfacción de estar allí y la emoción que uno carga.

Después de este paseo solo quedan dos opciones: volver al whisky o entregarse al hotel. La primera pasa por Bowmore, una de las destilerías históricas de Islay, fundada en 1779 y una de las más antiguas de Escocia. Está a orillas del Loch Indaal y conserva uno de los elementos que mejor explican su carácter: sus almacenes de maduración, algunos de ellos situados prácticamente al nivel del mar. Aquí el whisky sigue teniendo algo de paisaje: turba, agua, sal y años de espera convertidos en una bebida.

La segunda opción es bastante más peligrosa para el presupuesto: irse al hotel, pero, en fin, tampoco todos los días se despierta uno en Islay.

5. The Machrie, un hotel convertido en galería

El hotel The Machrie está frente al Atlántico, entre dunas y junto a una playa de siete millas, pero quizás lo más sorprendente está dentro. La colección de arte, reunida y comisariada por su fundadora, Sue Nye, convierte el alojamiento en una especie de galería habitada: las obras aparecen en los pasillos, las habitaciones, el restaurante, la recepción o el gimnasio. Hay artistas escoceses como John Bellany, Pat Douthwaite, Peter Howson o Elizabeth Blackadder, junto a nombres como Tracey Emin, Antony Gormley, Peter Blake, Picasso, Miró, Dalí o Banksy. El arte forma parte de la vida cotidiana.

El hotel y campo de golf The Machrie. KEVIN MURRAY (THE MACHRIE)

Y luego está el paisaje, la ubicación. The Machrie recibe también a muchos jugadores de golf, que encuentran aquí un tapete verde frente al Atlántico. Para quien disfrute dándole a una pelota con un palo y persiguiéndola después por la hierba, probablemente no se pueda pedir más. Para los demás siempre queda sentarse frente al mar. Porque las vistas de la hierba y el océano son de esas que consiguen que uno se quede un rato sin hacer absolutamente nada. Uno mira cómo el viento mueve la hierba y cómo la isla continúa con su vida. Quizá ese sea el lujo verdadero de The Machrie. Y, puestos a confesarlo todo, quizá también el único que importa, junto a la poesía, porque ante este paisaje por fuerza vuelven a la cabeza aquellos versos de Wislawa Szymborska: “Comprendo que mi tristeza no frenará la hierba. Si los tallos vacilan será sólo por el viento”.

World.title: Un recorrido por el Nápoles de Sorrentino y los rincones de la antigua y magnética Parthenope que llevó al cine
World.content:
Puedes amarla u odiarla, pero esta urbe italiana jamás te deja indiferente. Esta es una escapada siguiendo la huella emocional del director napolitano y, en concreto, de su película más personal, un poderoso poema a su ciudad natal, donde su imaginario estalla

Tal como refleja el director napolitano Paolo Sorrentino en su superproducción Parthenope (2024), la Bella Napoli es contradictoria como pocas. Es a la vez caótica y elegante, bella y decadente, sensual y sagrada. Nápoles no es solo una ciudad, es un estado de ánimo y, sobre todo, una sirena que hechiza a quien la mira. Y es que hoy el gentilicio culto o literario para los napolitanos sigue siendo partenopeo, en referencia a su antiguo nombre, Parthenope. Los orígenes de la actual urbe italiana se remontan a una colonia fundada por los griegos de la cercana población de Cumas en el siglo VIII a.C. “Esta primera fundación estaba formada por la isla donde está actualmente el Castel dell’Ovo (Castillo del Huevo) y la colina del monte Ecchia. Era muy pequeña y tomó el nombre de la sirena Parthenope, cuyo culto se desarrolló en esta zona antes de la llegada de los cumanos”, explica nuestra guía local.

En su universo melodramático y onírico, el oscarizado Paolo Sorrentino —por La gran belleza como mejor película internacional en 2014— refleja estos escenarios con su peculiar sprezzatura a través de la vida de una mujer que comparte el nombre original de la ciudad. Nacida en los años cincuenta e interpretada por Celeste Dalla Porta, Parthenope encarna ese misterio eterno de la belleza napolitana. La que fuera la poderosa capital del reino más grande de la península de Italia antes de la unificación en 1861 vivió una de sus épocas doradas a principios del siglo XX, pero, sin duda, forjó su apodo de capital de la dolce vita durante las décadas de los sesenta y setenta. La actual capital de la Campania rezumaba elegancia por doquier con la presencia de estrellas internacionales, el nacimiento de la alta costura local y una sofisticada vida nocturna. Revivimos ese Nápoles magnético, nostálgico y aristocrático y los pasos de juventud de la Parthenope de Sorrentino recorriendo lugares emblemáticos como el hotel Eurostars Excelsior, la colina de Vomero, Posillipo, el Teatro San Carlo y el paseo marítimo Lungomare.

Más información De Bilbao a A Coruña, una vuelta por el norte de España para disfrutar del mejor arte

Hotel Eurostars Excelsior, una institución de la ‘dolce vita’

Gianni Ricci, gerente general del Hotel Eurostars Excelsior, encarna a la perfección al personaje tipo de una película italiana. No hubiera sido de extrañar que Marcello Mastroianni, uno de los mejores amigos de su padre, le hubiera invitado a participar junto a él en alguna de sus famosas producciones. Su vida es tan apasionante como la de este alojamiento que dirige con gran profesionalidad e ilusión desde 2007. La sorpresa fue mayúscula cuando Ricci nos confesó: “Yo nací en este hotel. Mi madre, Titina, trabajaba aquí como planchadora. Estaba embarazada de mí y rompió aguas mientras trabajaba”.

El mítico edificio Liberty que le da cobijo desde 1908 representa esa dualidad napolitana: es tanto un refugio del bullicio urbano como un mirador privilegiado desde el que contemplarlo. Al bucear en la historia del Eurostars Excelsior, averiguamos que el padre de Ricci trabajó como concierge (una figura que prácticamente ya solo existe en establecimientos de lujo, una especie de asistente personal de los huéspedes) desde 1954 hasta 2007. “Cuando él se jubiló, el propietario me llamó directamente porque querían que un Ricci dirigiera el hotel. Inmediatamente acepté la propuesta, ya que mi sueño siempre había sido trabajar aquí”, explica.

Vista de la calle Partenope de Nápoles. GETTY IMAGES

Traspasar su majestuosa entrada en el número 48 de la bellísima Via Partenope es zambullirse en plena Belle Époque. Un primer instante es suficiente para darse cuenta de que uno acaba de entrar en un edificio que ha sido testigo de algunos de los episodios históricos más relevantes de Nápoles. Tal como cuenta Gianni Ricci, “hubo una época en que todo lo que pasaba en Nápoles pasaba en el Excelsior; era como una embajada, un lugar de encuentro de políticos, personajes ilustres, actores de Hollywood…”. Así lo atestiguan las paredes del vestíbulo, con fotografías que ilustran momentos relevantes como un almuerzo celebrado en honor al presidente Theodore Roosevelt en 1909 o la visita de la mismísima reina María Cristina, esposa de Alfonso XII.
