World.title: The Harvard divide over Delhi protests: One group condemns police action, another questions claims of 'siege'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The crackdown on protesters in Delhi has triggered a sharp divide among members of the Harvard University community, with two groups issuing contrasting statements, one condemning alleged police excesses and the other cautioning against what it described as a campaign to undermine India's constitutional institutions.

Disapproving the use of terms such as âsiegeâ to describe the police deployment in Delhi and âthievesâ or âcompromisedâ to characterise constitutional authorities, a section of Harvard affiliates said such language raised concerns about attempts to undermine public trust in democratic institutions.

"Troubling are reports of the use of Harvard Universityâs name to lend credibility to a political campaign without appropriate authorisation.

The language used to describe India as being under 'siege' and to characterise constitutional authorities as 'thieves' or 'compromised' raises serious concerns about the intent to undermine public trust in democratic institutions," the wider cross-section of the Harvard community, including lawyers, policymakers, civil servants, scientists and academicians, said in a statement.

âConstitution, not convenience'

The latest statement signed by 44 individuals raised concerns over what it described as a âconcerted campaignâ against the country's constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission, the Supreme Court, the office of the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and Parliament.





"We are deeply concerned by the negative public discourse and concerted campaign against Indiaâs constitutional institutions, including the

, the Supreme Court, the office of the Honâble Chief Justice of India, and Parliament," the statement released on Wednesday said.

It also addressed the role of law enforcement agencies in maintaining public order, saying their actions should be subject to fair scrutiny but that allegations must be grounded in evidence and due process.

âThe actions of law enforcement agencies to uphold public order deserve fair scrutiny, but sweeping accusations and abusive rhetoric cannot substitute for evidence, due process or institutional accountability,â the signatories said.They also stressed the need to respect public officials and the offices they hold, adding that constitutional principles and civil liberties must not be applied selectively.

âThe Constitution, rule of law, and civil liberties must be respected at all times, not just when it suits our interests,â the statement said.Summing up their appeal, the signatories said: âOur commitment must remain to the Constitution, not convenience; to justice, not selective outrage; and to democratic institutions, not the politics of accusation.â

October 12 statement condemns police action

In a statement dated October 12, around 100 Harvard alumni, students, faculty and staff condemned what they described as the âunprecedented siege of Delhi by police and paramilitary forcesâ and alleged arbitrary, illegal and unconstitutional action against peaceful protesters across the country on October 10.

"We, as alumni, students, faculty, and staff of Harvard University, are deeply concerned by the unprecedented siege of Delhi by police and paramilitary forces and arbitrary, illegal, and unconstitutional police actions against peaceful protestors across the country on 10th October 2026. We strongly condemn police brutality, unlawful detention, and violations of constitutional rights of all peaceful protestors," the letter shared by Live Law read.

Trinamool

World.title: Is Wetland Authority accountable to government or construction companies, asks PMK leader Anbumani
World.content:
PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) criticised the Tamil Nadu government on the delay in notifying the Pallikaranai marshland as a wetland and demanded that all wetlands in the State be notified.

In a statement, he said the Tamil Nadu State Wetland Authority (TNSWA) had informed the Madras High Court that the extent of the buffer zone (Zone of Influence) around the Pallikaranai marshland had been reduced to 316 acres. “The Wetland Authority has been refusing to notify wetlands, including Pallikaranai, but its speed in reducing the buffer zone apparently to ensure that construction companies do not suffer any business losses raises a serious question: is the Authority working for the Government or for construction companies?”

The TNSWA had filed a counter affidavit in the case filed by certain private construction companies, which sought the quashing of the National Green Tribunal’s order dated September 24 last year, which prohibited construction activities within a one-kilometre radius of the Pallikaranai marshland. “In its counter affidavit, the Tamil Nadu State Wetland Authority stated that, at a meeting held with officials from various departments on September 30, 2026, it had been decided to reduce the buffer zone around the Pallikaranai marshland from the 8,397 acres identified by the National Green Tribunal to just 316 acres,” he said. While he supports determination of buffer zone around the wetlands, Dr. Anbumani said it should be “scientifically determined”.

“The Wetland Authority has moved with lightning speed to reduce the buffer zone in order to protect the interests of construction companies, which claim that their businesses have been affected by the National Green Tribunal’s order issued a year ago. Why, then, has the Authority shown no similar urgency in implementing the Supreme Court’s judgment of December 11, 2024, which directed that the boundaries of the Pallikaranai marshland be surveyed and officially notified to protect it from decades of degradation? Is protecting the interests of private construction companies more important than protecting the Pallikaranai marshland?”

He said: “The Tamil Nadu government must immediately take steps to notify Pallikaranai and all wetlands across Tamil Nadu. The government must also immediately abandon the work to construct a six-foot-high protective wall extending three kilometres around the Pallikaranai marshland and a two-kilometre-long walkway.”

World.title: 30-acre land at Kinfra’s Petrochemicals Park in Ambalamugal proposed for Keralam govt’s J.C. Daniel Film City project
World.content:
The Ernakulam district administration has identified 30 acres at the Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation’s (Kinfra) Petrochemicals Park in Ambalamugal for the proposed J. C. Daniel film city project.

The proposal has been forwarded to the Keralam government, which plans to set up the film city under a public-private partnership (PPP) model. The 30-acre land parcel has been identified within the park which is spread over a total of around 481 acres, according to sources.

The Keralam government had included the film city project in the revised Budget 2026-27 presented by Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan, who also holds the Finance portfolio, on June 19, 2026.

Better connectivity

Though multiple revenue land options were considered in the initial stage, the authorities zeroed in on the Kinfra’s land in Ambalamugal in view of its improved connectivity and access as the project is being planned as a one-stop destination for film shooting.

The Department of Culture had sought the feedback of stakeholders in Malayalam cinema on shortlisting an ideal location for the film city project. The government had preferred Revenue land in order to cut the cost involved in acquiring private land for the venture. The district administration was told to identify around 25 to 30 acres of Revenue land, including sites earmarked for industrial development, according to officials.

Studio floors, entertainment and gaming zones, exhibition centres chronicling history of Malayalam cinema, state-of-the-art screening facilities and virtual production studio are among the key facilities under consideration at the film city.

The government has also received suggestions to invite private investment in setting up premium hotels, pre and post-production studios and space for holding film previews, audio and trailer launch at the film city.

A detailed project proposal will be formulated after considering various suggestions that had emerged through consultations involving various sections of Malayalam cinema.

The government will also rope in experts for coming up with a unique design for the proposed film city, according to sources.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Class 12 board exams to begin on March 3, 2027; Class 10 exams on March 17
World.content:
The State Board public examinations in Tamil Nadu for Class 12 will be held from March 3, 2027, to March 29, 2027, the Tamil Nadu School Education Department announced in Chennai on Wednesday (October 14, 2026).

Releasing the examination schedule for students of State Board schools, School Education Minister Rajmohan said that the examinations for Class 10 students will begin on March 17, 2027, and end on April 12, 2027.

The Class 11 arrear examinations will begin on March 5, 2027, and end on April 1, 2027. The tentative result dates are May 7, 2027, for Classes 12 and 11, and May 20, 2027, for Class 10. For all three sections, the first paper will be the language paper.

Each examination will last three hours and will begin at 10 a.m. Students will get 15 minutes to read the question paper before beginning to write at 10.15 a.m. The examination will conclude at 1.15 p.m.

Mr. Rajmohan wished the students, teachers, and parents a “peaceful and wonderful examination” season. “Some training in the lessons and writing skills, along with an understanding of the lessons, will be provided to students. Learning should be fun and not a burden,” he added.

Responding to a question on paper leaks, he stressed that all efforts were being made to ensure that even the smallest gaps were monitored and rectified.

World.title: Punjab police arrests key operative in social media influencer Mad Sandhu murder case
World.content:
Punjab Police on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) said they have apprehended a key operative, identified as Jobanpreet Singh, in the murder of social media influencer Mad Sandhu, from Mumbai

Director General of Police (DGP) Gaurav Yadav on Wednesday (October 14) said that Counter Intelligence (CI) Jalandhar, in coordination with the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) apprehended Jobanpreet Singh from Chembur in Mumbai.

“The arrested accused, Jobanpreet Singh is a resident of village Jandoke in district Tarn Taran. Police teams have recovered three sophisticated pistols—including one 9MM Glock, one 9MM Beretta and one .30 bore PX5—along with five magazines and 11 live cartridges from his possession,” he said.

On October 3, 2026, two motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire at Madhu Sudan Singh alias Mad Sandhu on Loharka Road in Amritsar, resulting in his death. An FIR under sections 103 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act was registered at Police Station Cantonment at Commissionerate Amritsar.

Earlier, two of his module associates, identified as Harsimranjit Singh alias Sangha and Fateh Singh, both residents of Village Sanghe, Tarn Taran, were also tracked down and apprehended in Surat, Gujarat, in a coordinated operation with Gujarat ATS. A total of 11 persons, including one of the shooters, have been arrested in this case.

“Preliminary investigation has established that Jobanpreet Singh played a pivotal role in arranging weapons, financing, and providing logistical support to the shooters at the behest of foreign-based handlers. During interrogation, accused Jobanpreet confessed to his involvement in three separate extortion-linked firing incidents in Tarn Taran district. Further investigation is underway to uncover the wider network and establish its backward and forward linkages, he added.

World.title: Jantar Mantar: From astronomical observatory to landmark protest site
World.content:
The Delhi Police on Monday (October 12, 2026) announced that Jantar Mantar has been denotified as a protest venue. The decision followed recommendations made by a committee constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs to identify alternative sites for demonstrations.

“Three new venues, namely Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi, have been designated for the organisation of protests and demonstrations,” the police said in a statement

Also see: Anti-CEC protests, October 12, 2026 | Live updates

Here is a look at the history of Jantar Mantar, how it evolved into one of the capital’s most prominent protest sites, and some of the major demonstrations held there in recent years.

An 18th-century monument

The Delhi Jantar Mantar, originally known as Yantra Mantra, was built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur as an astronomical observatory at the behest of Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah. Constructed around 1724, it relied on naked-eye observations, with its instruments, or yantras, providing remarkably accurate readings.

Built of brick rubble and finished with lime plaster, the observatory comprises four principal instruments: the Samrat Yantra, Ram Yantra, Jai Prakash Yantra and Mishra Yantra. Its primary purpose was to compile astronomical tables and predict the movements and positions of the Sun, Moon and planets. The name “Jantar Mantar” is derived from the words for instruments and calculations.

The Delhi observatory was the first of five Jantar Mantars established by Jai Singh II. The others were built in Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura, which no longer survives, and Varanasi.

In addition to the four principal instruments, the complex contains 14 geometric devices used to measure time, forecast weather, track planetary movements and determine celestial altitudes. These fixed structures were designed to minimise the effect of vibrations and were carefully aligned to specific directions.

Delhi’s protest landscape

Jantar Mantar was not always Delhi’s preferred venue for protests. Earlier, the Boat Club lawns were the focal point for major agitations, including the anti-cow slaughter demonstrations and mobilisation during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Subsequently, the Ramlila Maidan emerged as a key venue where thousands gathered to voice their opposition to government policies. It was also the site of the India Against Corruption movement, which captured widespread public attention.

Over time, however, Jantar Mantar became synonymous with public protest. From smaller pressure groups to national parties and Opposition alliances, a wide range of organisations chose the site to press their demands. Most recently, it has served as a venue for protests by Opposition parties seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Delhi’s protest hub

Its location, less than 3 km from Parliament, has made Jantar Mantar a symbolic alternative to marches towards Parliament. The site allows demonstrators to voice their concerns within close proximity of the country’s political establishment while remaining outside Parliament’s high-security perimeter. Its nearness to Parliament has also enabled political leaders and legislators to step out of the House and directly address protesters.

Lokpal Bill movement

Anti-corruption activist Anna Hazare began his fast at Jantar Mantar on April 5, 2011, demanding the enactment of the Jan Lokpal Bill drafted with inputs from civil society groups.

Also read: Deconstructing the Anna Hazare campaign

The agitation sparked a nationwide debate on corruption and accountability. Hundreds of supporters thronged Jantar Mantar, with some joining Mr. Hazare’s fast and others expressing solidarity with the movement.

Nirbhaya protests

Following the death of a 23-year-old physiotherapy student who was gang-raped in Delhi, large crowds gathered at Jantar Mantar on the night of December 30, 2012, demanding justice and stronger laws to address violence against women.

Also read: ‘It is multiorgan failure of society, state’

The protests, which were largely peaceful at the beginning, witnessed clashes the following day after some demonstrators attempted to march towards central Delhi and were stopped by police.

Anti-CAA protests

Thousands of people opposing the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and the proposed National Register of Citizens gathered at Jantar Mantar on December 19, 2019, after police prevented rallies from proceeding from locations including Mandi House and the Red Fort.

Also read: Dispersed crowds hold massive anti-CAA protest at Jantar Mantar

On December 25, 2019, another large march converged on Jantar Mantar. Ahead of the demonstration, prohibitory orders under Section 144 were imposed around Mandi House, prompting many protesters to assemble elsewhere before proceeding towards the designated venue.

Wrestlers’ protest

Olympians and international wrestlers, including Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik and Bajrang Punia, launched a sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar on January 18, 2023, against the Wrestling Federation of India and its then president, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh.

Ms. Phogat alleged that women wrestlers had faced sexual harassment, allegations that Mr. Singh denied.

The protest was initially suspended after discussions with government officials and assurances that an oversight committee would examine the allegations. However, leading wrestlers resumed their agitation on April 23, 2023, stating that no meaningful action had been taken.

On April 28, 2023, the protesters welcomed the Delhi Police decision to register an FIR against Mr. Singh, describing it as an important step, while maintaining that their agitation would continue until further action was taken. A week later, on May 3, 2023, tensions escalated when a scuffle broke out between protesters and police personnel at the site.

CJP protest against NEET paper leak

On June 20, 2026, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) launched an indefinite sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar over the alleged NEET paper leak.

The agitation gained prominence after activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the protest and began an indefinite hunger strike on June 28, 2026. What began as a campaign centred on examination irregularities broadened into a movement focused on youth unemployment, recruitment examinations and governance issues.

The protesters demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak controversy, alleged irregularities in CBSE’s on-screen marking process and wider examination reforms. The agitation eventually ended following Mr. Pradhan’s resignation.

World.title: Dhinakaran questions Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s ‘silence’ over Cauvery water dispute with Karnataka
World.content:
AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Tuesday (October 14, 2026) questioned Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay over his “silence” on the Cauvery water issue with Karnataka, though he held talks with his Andhra Pradesh counterpart regarding Krishna river water.

“Why is Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Mr. Joseph Vijay, who holds talks with the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister for Krishna river water, maintaining silence over the Cauvery issue? Is the alliance [TVK’s alliance with the Congress] more important than the State’s rights and the livelihood of the farmers?” Mr. Dhinakaran questioned in a social media post.

If there were issues with holding talks with Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar in person by visiting the State, Mr. Dhinakaran asked, had Mr. Vijay raised the Cauvery water issue with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi during his recent visit to Chennai? “Has Mr. Vijay decided to sacrifice the livelihood of the people in the Cauvery Delta region in exchange for the support of the Congress, which is holding up the minority TVK government?” he asked.

World.title: Chennai hospital organises breast cancer awareness programme
World.content:
To commemorate Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Iswarya Breast Centre at Iswarya Hospital at Taramani in Chennai, organised a special Villupattu programme titled ‘Varumunnar Kaappom’ on Sunday.

The programme was performed by Kalaimamani Bharathi Thirumagan to spread awareness about breast cancer and the importance of early detection, according to a release.

Deepa Chegu, Director and senior consultant at Iswarya Breast Centre, addressed the gathering on the importance of early detection and explained the available screening methods, including breast self-examination and mammography.

S. Rajasundaram, Director of Oncology and CEO of Iswarya Hospital, highlighted the importance of breast cancer awareness and timely medical intervention. Breast cancer survivors also shared their personal journeys, the release added.

World.title: PTI carried out 'political suicide attack' on its own KP govt, says Bilawal
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Wednesday blamed the PTI’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government for the circumstances that led to the imposition of emergency in the province, terming it a “political suicide attack”.

He made the remarks while addressing the National Assembly, which was discussing the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, for which the Centre had cited the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

The NA question hour session was suspended due to discussions on the emergency. During the session, Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry tabled a motion regarding the proclamation of emergency, while Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar opened the discussion.

At the outset of the proceedings, opposition members were sitting calmly and did not stage any loud protest.

Bilawal began his speech by highlighting that emergency and governor’s rule in KP were measures taken under the Constitution.

Reading the relevant provisions, Bilawal asserted that the Centre tried its best to “engage the opposition so this step did not have to be taken”.

“They will have to accept, even if not publicly, but the responsible leadership of the opposition knows that the PTI itself carried out a political suicide attack on its KP government,” he remarked.

The PPP chief maintained that the PTI could not deny that its “leadership, particularly in the province had a key role in the political, constitutional and legal circumstances” at present.

Bilawal emphasised that the PPP’s stance was that “before employing this constitutional atomic bomb, we must engage with PTI and the opposition and try to address the federal government’s reservations that they were not supporting them in the war against terrorism”.

He observed: “If political space is restricted for one political party, it is impossible that it remains restricted for that particular party; it is limited for every political party, political worker and Pakistani citizen.

“We are responsible for this, but you cannot deny that you are also responsible for it,” he said.

Terming the imposition of emergency a “difficult decision”, Bilawal recalled alleged remarks by Sohail Afridi — the KP chief minister whose role is now non-functional — that he would not combat terrorism the way the Centre wanted.

“If this was not a political suicide, then what else was it?”

The Bhutto scion wondered if the opposition and Afridi had left any reason for President Asif Ali Zardari, who he said prides himself on passing the 18th Amendment, to “refuse to sign” the emergency proclamation.

He argued that due to the PTI’s actions and statements, neither the president, the Centre, nor he had any legal or political reason left for not imposing emergency in KP.

“But even today, I would recommend to the federal government that we extend our hand forward once again for negotiations, political discussions and try to find a resolution and a middle path,” Bilawal added.

The PPP chairman noted that emergency was “always a stopgap measure”.

“We cannot sustain the emergency forever,” he added, emphasising that while the counterterrorism fight would be better than before, an “all-of-society and all-of-country response” was needed to eradicate it completely.

Regarding the Oct 3 talks of a joint delegation of the PPP and the government with the opposition, Bilawal said, “Late at night, I was informed that congratulations, negotiations are succeeding.”

He said the PTI was willing to declare the areas in KP with surging terrorism as “terrorist areas”, and the opposition was about to agree that the federal and KP governments would sign a pact on joint efforts against terrorism. However, the dialogue collapsed.

The former foreign minister pointed out that the security challenges Pakistan was facing were “way more complicated” than before, adding that India “could still not digest […] its embarrassment” from the May 2025 conflict.

Referring to remarks by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi that its ‘Operation Sindoor’ was still ongoing, Bilawal said: “It means that India is still sponsoring terrorist incidents in Pakistan, sometimes in the form of TTP (Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan) and sometimes in the form of separatist terrorist groups.”

He reiterated Pakistan’s stance that India was involved in terrorist activities being conducted from across the Afghan border.

The ex-foreign minister then highlighted Islamabad’s role as a mediator in the US-Iran war.

“But there is a state — which we do not recognise as a state — that will neither be happy nor ever forget that you took this step. And those Zionist forces will and are interfering in Pakistan’s internal politics and state.”

Concluding his speech, the PPP chairman emphasised the need for building consensus on “some fundamental issues” for an empowered lower house.

“Even today, we are saying, come and at least begin from this house,” he said while addressing the opposition benches.

At one point during the proceedings, the NA speaker noted that the Oct 3 dialogue was held in a cordial atmosphere, praising both sides for “attempting more than their capacity that the matter is settled”.

However, he said some matters were beyond the parties’ control and voiced his support for forming the same committees for negotiations if ever needed in the future.

Gohar demands implementation of NAP

Speaking on the NA floor, PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan’s said his party “rejected” the Centre’s move to impose emergency in KP.

He asked what “terrorism” Imran’s wife or sisters had allegedly been involved in that they had been put behind bars, or what the accusations were against the PTI MNAs and MPAs who he said were detained.

Gohar further said, “One person is not present in the house currently. When he comes during a joint session, then I will reveal the reality of the negotiations.”

He affirmed that the PTI had raised its voice against terrorism, adding that measures against the scourge must be taken according to the National Action Plan (NAP).

Responding to Gohar’s remarks, Bilawal said the PTI was busy in its long march while the people of KP were being targeted by terrorists.

Bilawal reiterated that the opposition could keep arguing against the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, but no one could deny that the decision was grounded in the Constitution.

“I cannot insist on the government to continue talks with PTI despite being defrauded multiple times,” the PPP chairman said.

Pointing towards Gohar and NA Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Bilawal said: “I believe that none of them is allied with terrorists. I believe that they will definitely want to combat terrorism; however, they cannot deny the fact that their former chief minister contradicted this fact.”

Bilawal again requested all the stakeholders to unite and combat terrorism collectively. He also called for the provision of all facilities to the incarcerated PTI founder.

‘Threat to national security’

Addressing the house, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar explained that emergency was imposed in KP as the security situation there was becoming a threat to “national security”.

Tarar noted that after the proclamation of emergency was issued, the Constitution’s Article 232 required that both houses of the parliament approve the measure.

He recalled that the federal cabinet examined “material” regarding terrorism in the province during its Oct 11 meeting and then advised Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to recommend the imposition of emergency.

He noted that some people compared the measure to the emergency imposed by former dictator Gen Pervez Musharraf on Oct 12, 1999.

The minister particularly noted “internal disturbances” and cross-border infiltrations. He contended that the situation since Oct 15, 2025, when Sohail Afridi’s government came into power in KP, was “turning into a threat to national security to an alarming extent”.

He went on to highlight that there was a rise in terrorism in KP, especially after 2021, due to the approach of the provincial government.

“Perhaps there might be foreign, diplomatic and political reasons behind it, which got inflamed due to a political party’s point of view.”

Tarar stated that 2,911 incidents of terrorism took place between 2021 and 2024 in KP, but they surged to 3,787 incidents between Oct 15, 2025 and Oct 9, 2026.

He criticised the KP chief minister for ignoring martyred security and police personnel, and for instead preferring to promote his political designs and make visits across the country.

“Even this was announced that the federal capital will be conquered,” he said, referring to the party’s plan to hold a protest long march towards the federal capital.

The PML-N leader expressed his government’s gratitude to NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq for providing a platform for dialogue between the Centre and the opposition. He reiterated the government’s stance that the PTI had the agreement draft changed multiple times, but even then backed off from it.

Tarar observed that the PTI demanded the release of their party founder Imran Khan and his treatment in a private hospital despite knowing that only courts could provide such a relief.

He said two days would be “remembered in the country’s democratic history with regard to misfortune and a political party”.

On the emergency measure, the law minister noted that a special mechanism has been introduced for 12 districts of KP.

Speaking after Tarar, Achakzai criticised him for trying to prove that terrorism was not tackled in KP.

The opposition leader questioned the government’s mandate in the February 2024 general elections, quipping that the opposition would “surrender” if the minister could swear that the government won those polls fairly.

Achakzai alleged that the incumbent ruling coalition was formed “illegally”.

‘You do not have clean hands’

Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif went on to recall the tenure of the PTI government in the Centre and assailed the party’s past actions.

Referring to ex-prime minister Imran Khan’s plan to resettle members of the TTP, he said PTI tried to convince the then-opposition that “bringing these terrorists back would be better for Pakistan”.

The PML-N leader mentioned the 2019 episode of an Indian pilot’s capture in Pakistan: “They had threatened and we were surrendering. The then-prime minister was saying, ‘What should I do? Attack India?’”

Asif urged the opposition to reflect on its past actions, adding that Imran often used to praise former army chief retired General Qamar Javed Bajwa.

“As long as this contradiction remains in our words and actions and in our society, the circumstances of this country will not fix.”

He narrated his time behind bars during the PTI government, when Shehbaz “smuggled a blanket” to him to brace the low temperatures. “I used to eat the jail’s food,” he said, claiming that orders were given to remove the geyser when it was installed.

“But we did not hold rallies or mourn at D-Chowk or dig graves. We did not martyr police and law enforcement personnel,” Asif remarked.

“You demand equity when you have clean hands. You do not have clean hands, you cannot demand equity; this is a thousand-year-old principle,” he contended.

“You know very well what Gen Musharraf did to me. There was a 4x6 cell in Attock jail,” the PML-N politician said, emphasising that he stood with his party and ex-PM Nawaz Sharif.

Speaking on the current political situation, Asif alleged that Afridi used to “take directives […] from a person sitting in Afghanistan”.

He referred to a statement by the TTP condemning the imposition of emergency and deployment of troops in certain places. “Who is their ally and who is their rival?” he said.

The minister further countered the PTI’s stance that its leaders have not been able to meet Imran, who is imprisoned in the Adiala jail. “Meetings are held, [but] a lot of them are not publicised or brought on record,” he maintained.

Farooq Sattar urges PTI to ‘openly condemn terrorism’

In his remarks on the floor of the lower house, Farooq Sattar expressed Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan’s (MQM-P) confidence in the decision taken by the prime minister.

“This was an extremely difficult decision, but so unavoidable that you had no other option,” Sattar said about imposing emergency and governor’s rule.

“We trust your decision as we trust your experience, capabilities, political acumen, and that you made this decision in the interest of the nation,” he added.

The MQM-P lawmaker contended that the PTI was “on the wrong side and does not have concrete arguments” to declare that the decision was baseless or made with political motives.

“The main issue is of the mindset,” he declared, adding that Imran had “publicly said that the war on terror is not ours”. “This is their policy. This is their mindset.”

Sattar questioned whether the KP government had ever published reports to expose terrorist hideouts and extremist trends. He further raised questions about the government’s pursuit of cases against suspected terrorists.

“Openly condemn terrorism; else, the allegation of backing [it], if a commission is formed and God forbid, it is proven in the inquiry that there is political extremism and terrorism complicity, there is a nexus, then where will you go?”

Sattar recounted his past MQM experiences, saying, “I have also suffered such times. A lot of times, the narrative coming from the top was difficult to defend. Today, I feel that Barrister Gohar is also not in the position to defend his [party’s] position on KP.”

World.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia 'totally unacceptable', says Dar
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday said that Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia were “totally unacceptable”.

He made the remarks while addressing a joint press conference after the 8th session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) alongside Oman’s Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, who is currently on an official visit to Pakistan.

At the outset of his presser, Dar said that the two sides would sign a protocol with regard to the commission.

He said that this reflected “a shared resolve to further strengthen and expand bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual interest”. He said that the two sides would also sign an agreement for mutual visa exemption for holders of diplomatic and official passports.

“Pakistan-Oman friendship remains strong and forward-looking,” he told media. The two ministers would after the press conference sign “a number of bilateral agreements”, Dar said.

He added that the two ministers had also agreed to hold a business-to-business investment forum in Pakistan.

The ministers discussed the situation in Gulf as well, he said, adding that “Pakistan remained committed to contributing constructively to diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region”.

Dar said that the two sides also exchanged views on recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He said that he conveyed Pakistan’s condemnation of the attacks.

“I underscored that attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are totally unacceptable. My brother [Albusaidi] actually fully endorses this. Violations of international law pose a serious threat to regional peace and security,” he said.

“I reaffirmed Pakistan’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and our unwavering commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” he said.

They also “emphasised the urgent need for unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza”, Dar said.

DPM Dar also stressed that India’s unilateral abeyance of the Indus Water Treaty was “a material breach of international law”.

“This action threatens the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” Dar said.

Speaking at the occasion, Albusaidi said the JMC had “provided an important opportunity to review the state of bilateral relations”. He said that two sides “reaffirmed the strength of the longstanding ties” between the two countries.

“Both Oman and Pakistan attach great importance to dialogue and diplomacy as essential means of addressing regional challenges, easing tensions and promoting peace and stability,” Albusaidi said.

He also appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic role in the US-Iran war. He reaffirmed the two countries’ “shared commitment to further deepening our bilateral partnership and broadening cooperation across centres of mutual benefit”.

The two countries agreed that dialogue and diplomacy were “the only way forward” to resolve regional conflicts, Dar said in response to a reporter’s question.

“We are both on the same page,” he said.

Meanwhile, Dar told reporters that a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) would help expand business activities, adding that he was told that barring one, all countries had consented to the agreement.

Responding to a question about the gaps in between bilateral talks between the two countries, Dar said Albusaidi’s visit was previously delayed because Pakistan had been involved in mediation efforts between US and Iran.

Albusaidi added that discussions had continued “behind the scenes”.

Responding to a question about the Strait of Hormuz, Albusaidi said that Oman was committed to “unhindered navigation” through the strait “because of its vitality to the global economy and the region”.

Dar commends Albusaidi’s efforts towards regional peace

Albusaidi arrived in Pakistan on Tuesday on a two-day visit.

Speaking at the outset of the 8th session of the JMC, Dar said the two had “worked out” certain areas of bilateral interest and discussed global issues in detail, including the US-Iran war, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab and Gaza in their restricted meeting.

Dar said the two sides had also discussed Jammu and Kashmir and other pressing regional issues. He commended Albusaidi’s leadership and efforts towards regional peace in the Middle East.

“I personally greatly admire your efforts. I know how much hard work you have put in,” he said, noting that Pakistan’s position on the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was “very unique”.

“We are members of both the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and, obviously, the United Nations and other multilateral bodies,” Dar said.

He stressed, “There should not be any long gaps between bilateral engagements,” noting potential in the areas of trade, economic activities and investment opportunities.

Dar said he had promised to visit Oman in 2027 to hold the next session of the commission there. He added that both sides had identified areas of mutual interest and discussed possible meetings.

He said Pakistan and Oman cooperated closely and cordially, adding that although their diplomatic relations had completed 55 years, their ties went back “centuries”.

Dar said the two countries shared a history of “love and affection”, particularly in relation to Balochistan and Gwadar. Referring to discussions on Bab al-Mandeb and recent developments involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, Dar said both sides shared similar views on resolving regional issues.

He said the impact of regional tensions was also visible in Pakistan, where energy supply chains had been affected, and fuel prices had skyrocketed, adding that the “common man could not afford the resulting burden.”

Speaking on the occasion, Albusaidi said Oman was committed to further strengthening bilateral engagement and cooperation in various fields that could bring greater benefits to the people of both countries.

“I am delighted to be here with my delegation in Islamabad this morning, in this very warm, friendly and brotherly country, Pakistan, with which, as you have rightly said, we share bonds of history, culture, tradition and unity,” he said.

He said the Pakistan-Oman JMC was one of the mechanisms for exploring further avenues of collaboration, adding that the two countries also had a business council and a political consultation mechanism between their foreign ministers.

“We can do much more, and as we made a joint commitment this morning to make this meeting a success, I believe the more we do, the more we can deliver on the promise and the aspiration of our leaderships and our people,” Albusaidi said.

He also commended Pakistan’s role in supporting dialogue and diplomacy in the region.

“Your efforts to encourage engagement, understanding, respect and recognition are commendable, and I salute you for all your efforts,” he said, adding that Oman greatly appreciated Pakistan’s role in providing space for dialogue between Iran and the US.

Albusaidi said there was significant potential for economic cooperation between Oman and Pakistan, particularly in trade, logistics, port connectivity, energy and food security.

“The potential exists, and our task is to remove any obstacles and create the conditions that allow businesses to thrive so that we can fully benefit from this potential,” he said.

He also called for greater cooperation in tourism, academic and technological fields, as well as more regular exchanges between the people of the two countries.

“Once again, I appreciate the efforts of our private sector and industrial partners,” Albusaidi said, adding that he looked forward to further discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation.

Dar, Omani FM call for sustained bilateral engagement

Earlier in the day, Dar held a meeting with Albusaidi ahead of the JMC session, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

The two ministers reaffirmed the close, fraternal ties between Pakistan and Oman and underscored the importance of sustained high-level engagement to deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly trade, investment and people-to-people contacts, according to the FO.

“The two sides also exchanged views on regional developments and emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in advancing lasting peace and stability”, the FO said.

Albusaidi commended Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and security, while Dar acknowledged and appreciated Oman’s constructive role and shared aspirations for regional peace and stability, the statement added.

A day earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) said the JMC session would review the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Oman bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation.

The visit “reflects the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Oman and is expected to further deepen mutually beneficial cooperation

Last week, DPM Dar chaired an inter-ministerial meeting in Islamabad to review preparations for the upcoming JMC session, according to state-run Radio Pakistan.

The meeting reviewed the agenda, bilateral agreements, and arrangements for the co-chairing of the JMC session, it said.

World.title: Makkah Alliance secretary general meets PM Shehbaz, briefs premier on defence cooperation
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday met the newly appointed secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance, retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, and was briefed on the strategy to promote “defence and strategic cooperation” under the pact, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.

Mahmood was appointed as the first secretary general of the defence alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month. The agreement — signed on August 7 — empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all.

During the meeting held on Wednesday, the premier reiterated that the pact was a “historic milestone for peace, unity, and stability in the region” and wished the secretary general well for his new role.

PM Shehbaz also reaffirmed Pakistan’s “unwavering commitment” to the protection of Saudi Arabia’s “sovereignty, territorial integrity and security” during the meeting as the Gulf state, which is a signatory to the pact, has faced escalating tensions with Yemen’s Houthi rebels in recent days.

The premier said Pakistan “stands shoulder to shoulder” with Saudi Arabia, according to Radio Pakistan.

The meeting comes amid heightened tensions in the Middle East. On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen, targeting fuel and energy facilities it said were being used to support missile and drone attacks, as the Yemeni group threatened a “harsh and painful” response against Saudi airports, refineries and oil installations.

Hours later, Saudi authorities issued warnings of potential hostile aerial threats in the kingdom’s eastern province and Riyadh.

Loud explosions were heard near Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran, according to witnesses. Later, a Saudi energy ministry official confirmed the attack. Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency said that four people — two women, a man and a child — were wounded by debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles in the capital and that 15 homes were damaged.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July.

Against this backdrop, Pakistan has repeatedly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia. On October 5, in an emergency meeting of the Makkah pact in Riyadh, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye agreed to the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, maintained that Pakistan and Turkiye had “presence in theatre” and only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

On September 18, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”.

Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan will “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalates. The defence minister said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries.

World.title: FCC rejects Bushra Bibi's petition seeking suspension of 7-year Al-Qadir Trust sentence
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) on Wednesday rejected a plea moved by the spouse of incarcerated former premier Imran Khan, Bushra Bibi, seeking suspension of her seven-year sentence in the £190 Al-Qadir Trust case.

Earlier in the day, a two-judge FCC bench consisting of Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan and Justice Ali Baqar Najafi reserved its ruling and directed senior counsel Salman Safdar, who is representing the appellant, to submit written arguments before the court.

The detailed order for dismissal will be issued by the FCC later.

Bushra had moved the FCC in July seeking the suspension of her sentence, with her criminal appeal contending that the appellant, being a woman with a serious medical condition, was entitled to the suspension of her sentence. On Sept 17, Safdar moved an application before the FCC, seeking early hearing of the appeal, citing a rapidly deteriorating ocular condition that threatens the appellant’s remaining eyesight.

Earlier this month, senior members of the PTI’s legal team approached the FCC for early fixation of the criminal appeal. However, no fresh application was filed, and only a verbal request was made for early registration and fixation of the case.

On Wednesday, the court took up Bushra’s criminal appeal, in which she contended that, as a woman and in view of her serious medical condition, she was entitled to the suspension of her sentence, as similar relief was contemplated under the first proviso to Section 497(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja was also present in the courtroom during the hearing.

Safdar argued that the courts have always maintained a lenient view regarding women. He added that the National Accountability Bureau’s (NAB) conduct in the past 13 months had been objectionable since it repeatedly sought adjournments and objected to the plea for suspension of the sentence.

Following the conviction, there is now a legal basis for granting bail to the appellant, the counsel argued.

However, the FCC CJ asked the counsel not to delve into the merits of the case at this stage since the matter was concerned with the suspension of the sentence.

Moved under Section 32-A of the National Accountability Ordinance read with Article 175F(1)(a) of the Constitution, the criminal appeal pleaded before the FCC that Adiala jail authorities had not complied with the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) directions to facilitate the appellant’s meeting with her counsel.

Her counsel was instead permitted to meet the appellant’s husband, incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan, who disclosed that both he and the appellant were being illegally kept in solitary confinement and were denied access to family, friends, counsel, political party members and each other.

Imran also reportedly told counsel that neither he nor the appellant had been provided with books or television, thereby subjecting them to complete isolation from human contact and depriving them of information about the outside world.

The appeal reiterated that the appellant’s daughters had subsequently confirmed the situation when they met her after her eye surgery on April 17, 2026.

Such treatment amounted to an unauthorised enhancement of sentence, violated the prisoners’ fundamental rights to life and dignity guaranteed under Article 9 of the Constitution, and warranted the FCC’s immediate intervention, the petition argued.

The appeal regretted that the appellant had been subjected to continuous solitary confinement, which had demonstrably taken a grave toll on her physical and mental health.

In view of her deteriorating medical condition, Bushra should not be subjected to solitary confinement, even if such punishment had been imposed by a court, the petition pleaded.

It added that her “unlawful confinement” was in “blatant disregard of the applicable law and prison rules”.

The petition further said that the appellant’s counsel or her family were not informed of her eye surgery while incarcerated. It added that after the surgery, Bushra’s daughters were permitted to meet her, and at the time, she was in “a visibly alarming and distressed condition”.

“After undergoing such a serious medical procedure, the appellant was shifted back to jail and to date being kept in conditions of isolation, without any dedicated medical supervision, attendant, or nursing care, despite her impaired vision and vulnerable condition,” the petition said.

“Such treatment of a medically compromised prisoner, particularly a woman, is manifestly cruel, inhumane, degrading, and is wholly inconsistent with the constitutional guarantees of dignity and humane treatment”.

The criminal appeal contended that the prosecution had alleged that the appellant and her husband, through their associate Farhat Shahzadi, had received 240 kanals of land from co-accused Ahmad Ali Riaz Malik for personal gain.

However, the evidence on record established that the entire amount had been deposited into an account maintained at the National Bank of Pakistan in the name of the registrar of the Supreme Court of Pakistan.

“The prosecution has thus failed to produce any credible or legally admissible evidence linking the appellant to any personal gain arising out of the alleged transaction,” the appeal argued.

It added that the “material contradictions, coupled with complete absence of substantive proof, expose the inherently flawed nature of the prosecution case and the proceedings conducted thereunder, which alone furnish sufficient grounds for suspension of sentence”.

The appeal contended that NAB selectively prosecuted the appellant and her husband while deliberately excluding six other individuals who were allegedly implicated in the matter.

The petition further said that the core allegations revolved around the Malik Riaz family and others, but they had not been subjected to prosecution.

“This selective and incomplete approach has resulted in a defective and biased investigation, culminating in the unjust framing of charges and subsequent conviction of the appellant,” the appeal contended.

The former first lady was handed the sentence in the case in January last year, and remains imprisoned at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail. The court found Imran and Bushra guilty of giving undue favours to property tycoon Riaz in retrieving his laundered money from the United Kingdom.

Bushra, along with the ex-PM, had initially moved the Islamabad High Court (IHC) for the suspension of her sentence in July last year. But the high court dismissed their requests in May 2026, observing that their appeals against their convictions had already been fixed for hearing.

Subsequently, the two approached the Supreme Court against the IHC decision, but the SC office returned the petition as being not maintainable, explaining that since the IHC had passed the impugned order while exercising jurisdiction under Section 32 of the National Accountability Ordinance (NAO), 1999, the remedy lay exclusively before the FCC under Section 32-A of the ordinance.

Bushra then moved the FCC on July 30, with her criminal appeal contending that the appellant, being a woman with a serious medical condition, was entitled to the suspension of her sentence, as similar relief was contemplated under the first proviso to Section 497(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).

Her latest application for the appeal’s early hearing, which was rejected on Monday, also stated that her rapidly deteriorating ocular condition threatened her remaining eyesight.

World.title: Pakistan, Russia agree to finalise extradition treaty, to sign MoU on prevention of organised crime
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Russia on Wednesday agreed to finalise an extradition treaty and pledged to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation in preventing organised crime and exchanging information.

Minister of Internal Affairs Vladimir Kolokoltsev arrived in Pakistan on Monday. He is undertaking a four-day visit at the invitation of Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, marking the first instance of a Russian interior minister visiting Pakistan.

The understanding was reached during a meeting between Naqvi and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Kolokolstev in Islamabad. The meeting was followed by delegation-level talks, the interior ministry said in a statement.

Naqvi, during the meeting, said the proposed MoU on prevention of organised crime would be an important milestone in cooperation between the two countries.

The two sides pledged to enhance mutual cooperation in areas of shared interests as they agreed to finalise an extradition treaty and an agreement on the exchange of criminals.

Both sides resolved to promote cooperation in areas of mutual interest and decided to ensure early implementation of a readmission agreement, according to the statement.

They also agreed to enhance cooperation between the Anti-Narcotics Force and relevant Russian institutions.

It was agreed in the meeting that working groups from the interior ministries of both countries would soon visit each other.

The two sides also discussed sending skilled manpower from Pakistan to Russia and facilitating visa acquisition for tourists and the business community, as per the statement.

They agreed to enhance cooperation for the prevention of cybercrime between the National Police Academy and the Russian Police Academy, the statement said.

Naqvi said easing the visa regime would increase people-to-people contact between the two countries. He also expressed desire to benefit from Russia’s experiences in curbing cybercrime.

He further noted that at present, 1,300 Pakistani students were studying in Russia and Pakistan wanted more students to study there.

Russian Interior Minister Kolokolstev, for his part, said joint measures were essential for the prevention of all organised crime, including terrorism, drug smuggling, and illegal migration.

He said Russia had brought a 33 per cent reduction in cybercrime through effective measures.

The meeting was attended by Minister of State Tallal Chaudhry, the Russian ambassador in Pakistan, special and additional secretaries to interior and other senior officials.

In recent years, Pakistan and Russia have significantly strengthened their economic ties, driven by mutual necessity.

In January, Russian President Vladimir Putin had said Moscow’s relations with Pakistan were “ genuinely mutually beneficial ” and that it maintained close ties with Islamabad.

Last July, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister Alexei Overchuk called Pakistan and Russia “ natural allies ”, stressing that Putin viewed Islamabad as an important strategic partner in the areas of economy and energy.

Following Western sanctions related to the Ukraine conflict, Moscow turned toward new energy outlets, while Islamabad simultaneously sought more affordable fuel sources to reduce national import expenses.

World.title: Section 144 imposed in DI Khan, pillion riding and public gatherings banned
World.content:
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: The district administration imposed Section 144 across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Dera Ismail Khan district, banning pillion riding and public gatherings, rallies and processions until Nov 11, citing law and order concerns.

The restrictions were imposed through an order issued by Deputy Commissioner Hikmatullah on Oct 13 and took immediate effect.

Under the order, public gatherings, meetings, processions and rallies that could potentially disturb public order, disrupt traffic or obstruct the movement of citizens have been prohibited.

The administration has also imposed restrictions on the display of weapons and the installation of tents and temporary structures on public roads, according to the notification.

The order said the measures had been taken in view of the prevailing law and order situation in the district.

Those found violating the restrictions would face legal action under Section 188 of the Pakistan Penal Code, the administration warned.

The restrictions will remain in force across the district until Nov 11, unless withdrawn or modified by the competent authority before that date.

Section 144 is a provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure which empowers local authorities to ban public gatherings such as rallies, processions and sit-ins, as well as the open display of weapons.

Currently, Section 144 remains in effect in several areas of the country.

On Sunday, it was imposed in Karachi, set to remain in effect till Oct 20. On Saturday, Section 144 was imposed in Rawalpindi district for a period of 30 days.

Punjab Home Department also imposed Section 144 across the province until Oct 15 in view of serious threats to public peace, tranquility and the safety of life and property.

World.title: Security forces kill 5 terrorists in Balochistan's Washuk: state media
World.content:
Security forces killed five terrorists in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Balochistan’s Washuk, state-run Pakistan TV reported on Wednesday, citing security sources.

Terrorist hideouts were targeted with advanced weapons, sources said.

State media added that four terrorists were also injured, identifying them as belonging to Fitna al Hindustan.

The state refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

The IBO was conducted under Operation Raddul Fitna 3, state media said, adding that “advanced weapons and ammunition” were recovered.

“Security forces remain determined to eliminate terrorism from Balochistan,” state media said.

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to security forces for the Washuk operation in a statement on X.

“Effective operations against terrorist elements attempting to disrupt peace and security and spread fear and panic among the public in Balochistan will continue,” President Zardari was quoted as saying.

He added, “Conspiracies by the terrorists’ foreign patrons and their local facilitators will be thwarted at any cost”.

Terrorism in Balochistan

Balochistan has witnessed terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time.

Ten terrorists were killed in a targeted IBO conducted by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in Balochistan’s Barkhan district, the Home Department said on Oct 10.

In Chagai, security forces killed two terrorists on Sept 29.

The military’s media affairs wing said on Sept 27 that more than 71 terrorists had been killed in Shaban and other areas of Balochistan.

On Sept 17, three terrorists were eliminated in an IBO in Balochistan’s Awaran district’s Badrang area. Another three were killed i n Mastung on Sept 14. Earlier in September, 21 terrorists were killed in separate engagements in Nokcha, Chagai, Ziarat Cross, and Pishin.

World.title: India festival boat capsize kills 13 children
World.content:
Rescuers dragged out 13 dead children from India’s Ganges river after an overloaded boat capsized en route to a Hindu festival, officials said Wednesday, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressing grief over the “deeply painful” tragedy.

The boat overturned late Tuesday in Vaishali district in eastern Bihar state, with locals rushing to pull people out of the water in the dark using mobile phones to find the bodies.

“It was dark when we suddenly heard children screaming and crying for help as the boat capsized,” Ravi Yadav, a young villager who joined the rescue effort, told AFP.

“We managed to rescue only three children, using the light from mobile phones and torches, because it was dark.” Villager Ramlakhan Rai said the boat was “small” and “not in good condition”, saying people were crammed onto a vessel suitable for just a handful.

“It is devastating — a few families have lost all their children,” he said.

Six people were pulled out alive, including two children reported to be in critical condition.

Medic Nirmal Kumar, from the local health centre, said four children and two adults were sent to the district hospital.

“We tried our best to revive them… but 13 were already dead,” Kumar said.

Vaishali district magistrate Varsha Singh told AFP 13 bodies had been recovered.

“The loss of lives in the boat capsizing incident in Vaishali, Bihar is deeply painful,” Modi said in a statement on Wednesday, announcing compensation for their families.

“My thoughts are with the bereaved families in this difficult time.” Boat accidents are common on Indian waterways, often blamed on overcrowding, poor enforcement of safety norms and inadequate life-saving equipment.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced. Bangladesh Bank’s green refinancing fund should be expanded. Rooftop and residential solar customers should be eligible for collateral-free loans. The LC margin for renewable equipment should be limited to 5%.

Net metering must be simplified. Approval should be completed within 15–30 days through a one-stop service. Approval, interconnection, inspection, billing adjustment, and utility coordination should all be simple and time-bound. Wheeling charges for renewable energy should also be kept reasonable and low. The Merchant Power Policy should be clear, simple, and investment-friendly so that industries and commercial consumers can directly procure renewable electricity.

Agriculture should also be included in the solar transition. Bangladesh can set a target to convert 1.5 million diesel irrigation pumps into solar pumps. This will reduce diesel imports, lower farmers’ production costs, and protect the environment. The program should include duty-free facilities, low-cost loans, investment support, and local service networks.

Waste-to-energy should also receive policy support. City corporations need clear rules, easy financing, and private-sector participation to enable urban waste management and distributed power generation to work together.

Bangladesh now needs a phased national roadmap for renewable energy.

In the short term, within 0–6 months, customs duty, VAT, and taxes on renewable energy equipment should be reduced to zero. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and energy storage should be withdrawn. Approval for net metering should be obtained within 15–30 days. Industrial and commercial solar installations should be eligible for special incentives. The 31 suspended solar projects should be reassessed. Wheeling charges should be rationalised.
